News.title: Steve Tandy frustrated as Wales let lead slip against Australia
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Steve Tandy expressed his frustration after Wales were edged out in a Nations Championship thriller by Australia.

Wales were unable to build on their shock win over New Zealand seven days earlier – their first victory over the All Blacks for 73 years – as Australia held on for a 29-26 success in Cardiff.

Skipper Dewi Lake scored twice, while Blair Murray and Ryan Elias also crossed for tries as Wales picked up two bonus points.

Wales finished fifth in the northern hemisphere placings, meaning they will play Japan at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, on finals weekend to decide who finishes ninth in the inaugural Nations Championship.

“Obviously, we’re disappointed to lose the game,” said head coach Tandy after Wales had let a 21-19 lead slip in the second half.

“I don’t think we were as accurate as we could have been, particularly being held up three times.

“At the start of the game, I felt we could have got ahead on the scoreboard and built some pressure.

open image in gallery Australia’s Taniela Tupou scores against Wales in their Nations Championship win (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

“After such a monumental game last week, with all the energy and emotion that went into it, I thought we stuck in the game really well and scored four tries.

“It would have been easy to find ourselves 12-0 down and perhaps let things drift, but I thought we stayed composed.

“We got seven points before half-time, which was big. Then we bounced back and took the lead. I thought that try told you a lot about the intent and mindset of the group.

“Overall, we’re frustrated at losing, but there are plenty of positives to take from the performance as well.”

open image in gallery Dewi Lake celebrates scoring Wales’ first try against Australia (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

Japan present familiar opponents for Wales as Saturday’s clash in London will be the fifth game in 16 months between the two sides.

Wales squeezed past Japan 28-21 in their autumn opener, but Eddie Jones’ Brave Blossoms have been thrashed by England and Scotland over the last two weekends.

Tandy said: “We’ve got to build on this and be better than we were this week in terms of our performance. It’s something we can’t get away from.

“We’ve had a good tournament so far, and we’re disappointed with today. But we want to finish on a high, and that will only be as good as the performance we produce.

“I can rotate the team and we’ll still put in a performance. Ultimately, we’ve got to perform. It doesn’t matter who wears the shirt – we’ve got to perform.

open image in gallery Tomos Williams, pictured being tackled by Australia’s Harry Potter and Rob Valetini, was replaced after picking up a groin injury (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

“Whenever we put a team out, the objective is to win a Test match. That will be no different next Saturday.”

Scrum-half Tomos Williams will be assessed after leaving the action early in the second half with a groin problem.

“I thought the boys did pretty well. We’re growing as a team and we’re a young group. Think about where we were 12 months ago,” said Tandy.

“The boys have got a couple of days off now, so we’ll look at the changing room and see where we are with injuries.”

“We’ll definitely freshen things up for next week.”

News.title: COP31 climate talks close to final deal, says summit president
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

United Nations climate talks in Turkey have approached a final deal as COP31 presidents hope to finally achieve consensus on how to advance the fight against global warming.

COP31 president Murat Kurum told a late-night plenary session: “We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” as the conference was set to reconvene on Sunday morning to approve the deal.

To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts warn of the need for urgent and deep cuts to emissions, mainly from the use of coal, oil and gas. The world is already on track to blow past the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperature.

Civil society organisations wrote to Cop31’s joint presidents, Australia’s Chris Bowen and Murat Kurum, overnight to tell them they had hours left to avoid making it “one of the most disappointing Cops [the UN] has ever had”.

“The Global South is being abandoned,” they said. “Developed countries have blocked progress across the negotiations and arrived with no new finance commitments.”

Negotiators ran past a Friday deadline, straight through Saturday and into the early hours of Sunday. Their new version of the deal text refined an earlier draft, which had been heavily criticised by some for lacking ambition because it contained no reference to ending the use of fossil fuels.

Kurum has said he felt concerns around fossil fuels had been addressed, as had those around helping developing countries finance their adaptations to climate change.

Delegations have until 3am GMT to raise any objections to the deal, with a session scheduled at 6am GMT to begin approving it.

Australia led the talks with Turkey, which is hosting the meeting, and nearly 200 delegations from the world’s richest, poorest, largest and smallest nations. It was hoped that a year of climate disasters could help sharpen minds at the conference.

Devastating floods in Mozambique flooded more than 150,000 homes and killed at least 22 people. Coming off the back of other climate disasters in the country - including Cyclone Kenneth in 2019, as well as a crippling drought across 2023 and 2024 - charities told The Independent they were struggling to attract donors due to foreign aid cuts.

In August, after a piece of melting glacier dislodged high up in the mountains, devastating floods in Nepal caused an estimated $4.8bn in damages, and left 1,500 dead and 10,000 injured.

There is also the threat a record breaking El Nino weather event that the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP) has projected that an additional 49 million more people could be pushed into hunger globally.

A climate “loss and damage” fund was established at Cop27 in Egypt in 2022 in order to provide developing countries with compensation for climate disasters. But it has so far secured just $822m in pledges, and countries affected by climate disasters are limited to apply for only $20m per disaster – less than half a per cent of Nepal’s needs.

“Nepal did not create the climate problem. But we keep being hit by massive floods, not just this year but also in 2025, 2022 and other years,” said Bisesh Sangat, a Nepali attendee of Cop31 who works for the NGO Practical Action. “There’s a lot of big infrastructure losses, but also the human losses mean that you go to villages and there are lots of widows and children without fathers, so the losses are very profound.”

There was already deep disappointment after a draft published on Thursday afternoon failed to include any mention of fossil fuels - despite the fact that this had previously been mentioned in the outcome of Cop28 in Dubai in 2023.

This cover decision is seen as the key outcome of the UN climate conference, and is set to be a key signal that countries will take home and implement in national policy.

Mohamed Adow, director of the Power Shift Africa thinktank said: "If this version of the text remains, it will be a ghost COP. The summit will have nothing to show for what happened here. After the progress made in 2023 at Cop28 in Dubai where fossil fuels were mentioned for the first time, there is now no mention of the f-word at all. Cop31 has been muzzled on the most important threat causing the climate crisis."

Stories emerging from the negotiating room suggest that the usual suspects were to blame for an outcome that was less ambitious than hoped. Saudi Arabia has been among the main objectors to any wording on the “transition away from fossil fuels”, with insiders suggesting that the world’s largest oil exporter played a key role in blocking ambitious language.

Pelin Zorlu, senior research fellow lead on climate and energy at the Chatham House think tank, said: “The Cop Presidency has acknowledged the difficulty of reaching consensus on fossil fuels, with opposition from the Arab Group, Russia and others.”

But others pointed their fingers at the EU for not being ambitious enough, particularly around Turkey’s high profile pledge to raise electricity's share of total final energy consumption from around 23 per cent today to 35 per cent by 2035. Such a move makes sense if the electricity is powered by renewables – but not if it is done so with coal.

Laurie van der Burg, from NGO Oil Change International, said: “The EU is trying to shift blame onto others and it is deeply hypocritical. At the beginning of Cop31, it signalled it was prepared to drop the renewable energy sources ask from the electrification target and it has failed to put forward an EU fossil fuel transition roadmap. Even worse, the EU blocked progress on the public finance, adaptation, and just transition that developing countries urgently need. These are not side issues. They are essential to making a fair fossil fuel phaseout possible and protecting communities from climate disasters.”

At the same time, the EU and other wealthy democracies have expressed dismay at receiving too much blame when it is they who are providing the bulk of climate finance - and especially so with the US absent. EU member states provided €32.3bn in public “climate finance” in 2025, which mobilised a further €9.3bn in private finance.

There is growing disquiet that the group of countries who are required to provide this “climate finance” – crucial capital needed to decarbonise and adapt to climate change – is fixed around a list of developed countries that was devised in 1992, known as “Annex II”. It means that newly-wealthy countries, including China, the UAE, South Korea and Singapore, do not officially have to provide climate finance, while the likes of Greece and Portugal are required to.

While plenty of lobbyists were in attendance, one group was conspicuously absent: world leaders. Neither China’s Xi Jinping or India’s Narendra Modi, or any hint of the US federal government made an appearance – with Andy Burnham the only G7 leader in attendance. Yet, while powerful countries fight it out, ultimately it is the world’s most climate vulnerable countries who are losing out.

On Friday afternoon, Ghana's minister for environment, science and technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings did not mince her words.

Africans were being “excluded by the use of technicalities, with the use of inaccessible finance, and with the use of shifting goalposts and lack of commitment and delivery on promises… Africa is not a continent merely seeking assistance. We are asking the developed countries to keep promises that they already made.”

In what seemed to be a reference to the US, she said: “There are countries who from the onset decided not to be a part of this agreement. There, they were plain and honest… What we do not appreciate are those who choose to remain a part of the framework and yet continue to undermine the process and undermining trust and the credibility of what we do.”

There were some positives however, with organisations in some specialist areas hailing signs of success.

For example, more than 50 countries backed a new initiative pushing geothermal energy, while the UN announced that nations and oil and gas operators have delivered total cuts in methane emissions that are equivalent to taking 26 million cars off the road for a year since 2023. Turkey's drive to put waste reduction at the heart of Cop31 has also won widespread praise.

News.title: Noni Madueke rescues Arsenal and salvages point against inspired Newcastle
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Noni Madueke snatched a 2-2 draw for Arsenal after Newcastle produced a stunning second-half turnaround to claim a deserved point against the Premier League leaders.

Eberechi Eze put the champions in front and Madueke wasted a couple of chances to increase the lead before half-time, with Matthias Jaissle’s side jeered off following a listless first 45 minutes.

They rallied in stunning fashion on the resumption, with Harvey Barnes scoring Newcastle’s first goal at St James’ Park since September 19 before Malick Thiaw put them ahead after the hour from close range.

open image in gallery Malick Thiaw celebrates after equalising (Owen Humphreys/PA)

Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes underwhelmed on his return to Tyneside, his every touch booed before he was brought off after 70 minutes, but his new employers claimed a share of the spoils thanks to Madueke.

Arsenal’s five-match winning run in the league was halted, although they extended their lead at the top of the table to six points over second-placed Brighton, who could halve the deficit at Hull on Sunday.

Newcastle came into the fixture with significant concerns about where their goals were coming from and they were up against the most miserly defence in the league, with Arsenal conceding just five times in their previous 10 games.

Newcastle were given an early warning when Madueke cut inside and left England team-mate Dan Burn trailing in his wake, with the Arsenal forward’s low shot to the near post hitting the outside of it.

Arsenal’s press meant there was no let-up for Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who made a series of distribution errors, and it was a heart-in-mouth moment for the home side’s fans when Guimaraes got ahead of Barnes but the Brazilian could not direct a sliding volley on-target.

open image in gallery Eberechi Eze (second right) celebrates the opening goal (Owen Humphreys/PA)

The Magpies’ luck ran out in the 33rd minute when Kai Havertz dispossessed Lewis Hall before sliding a perfectly-weighted pass to Eze, who went in behind Amar Dedic to finish coolly past Hornicek.

Matters might have worsened before half-time as more loose play allowed Madueke to pick his pocket. Madueke bore down on goal but took one touch too many before his shot was saved by Hornicek.

Hall made partial amends to then deny Madueke’s shot while Eze’s free-kick was saved as Arsenal ended the half on top, prompting Jaissle to make a triple substitution at the break, with Jacob Ramsey, Anthony Elanga and Tino Livramento replacing Jacob Murphy and Dedic and Sean Steur.

Newcastle exploded out of the traps and needed just four minutes after the restart to draw level, with Martin Odegaard nudged off the ball by Joe Willock and the ball dropping to William Osula, who teed up Barnes to fire beyond David Raya with aplomb.

It was Newcastle’s first goal at home in 312 minutes and with the crowd now firmly behind them, they remarkably took the lead with Arsenal at sixes and sevens.

open image in gallery David Raya (left) leaves the field with an injury (Owen Humphreys/PA)

The unmarked Burn headed Hall’s corner on-target and a goalmouth scramble between Willock and Arsenal duo Gabriel and Raya led to Thiaw poking home from a yard out in the 62nd minute.

Arteta was forced into a substitution with Raya suffering a shoulder injury, while Guimaraes was also hooked alongside Eze with 20 minutes to go to the delight of Newcastle’s supporters as Kepa Arrizabalaga, Christos Tzolis and Myles Lewis-Skelly were introduced.

Newcastle continued to pile forward but were undone in the 78th minute when a fluid move forwards from Arsenal ended with Madueke cutting onto his left foot and dispatching through Hornicek’s hands and in.

Both sides had chances to claim victory in a frenzied atmosphere but neither could manage another breakthrough before Guimaraes, the first Newcastle captain to lift a trophy in 56 years following their historic 2025 Carabao Cup triumph, was cheered at full-time when he completed a lap of the pitch.

News.title: Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev set up mouth-watering ATP Finals title clash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev will clash on Sunday for the ATP Finals title.

The two standout players in Turin both successfully negotiated their semi-finals, with Alcaraz pushed by Ben Shelton before coming through a third-set tie-break, while Zverev saw off Daniil Medvedev.

The German, who is yet to drop serve, produced another very strong display in a 7-6 (0) 6-4 victory.

It will be a first meeting between Zverev and Alcaraz since a dramatic Australian Open semi-final that saw the Spaniard prevail in five epic sets despite struggling with cramp.

Zverev, though, has won both their previous matches at the ATP Finals and said on Sky Sports: “The matches that we played were always very difficult and I look forward to another difficult one. Hopefully it’s going to be entertaining.”

open image in gallery Alexander Zverev will face Carlos Alcaraz for the first time as World No 1 ( Getty )

Much has been made of Zverev’s indifferent record against top-10 players in 2026, despite winning two grand slam titles and climbing to World No 1, so victory over Alcaraz, whom he has not beaten for two years, would be a major statement.

The Spaniard, who lost out on the title to Jannik Sinner last year, extended his winning run to 13 matches with a 3-6 6-3 7-6 (1) victory over third seed Shelton.

It was another big test of Alcaraz’s fitness after knee and hamstring concerns and he revealed the limitations he is feeling may influence the way he plays when fully fit.

“Sometimes I don’t have to push myself to the limit in some movements, in some shots, in some balls,” he said. “I don’t have to run for every ball, which I’m just understanding that right now.”

Meanwhile, Britain’s Neal Skupski and American Christian Harrison were beaten 7-6 (10) 6-7 (7) (10/7) by Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic in the semi-finals of the doubles.

News.title: Moises Caicedo forced off in tears as Chelsea injury crisis worsens
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Moises Caicedo was forced off in the first half of Chelsea’s thrashing by Leeds as Xabi Alonso’s injury problems continue to mount.

The Ecuadorian lynchpin suffered a bad landing after meeting James Justin’s aerial challenge, which saw him twist in midair and land on his tailbone.

Caicedo was initially able to continue but after being troubled by his back in the following minutes, repeatedly holding the problem area, he went down off the ball, covering his seemingly tearful eyes with his shirt in dejection.

He was replaced by Jordan Henderson in the 22nd minute, but did not go straight down the tunnel for further treatment, instead taking a seat on the bench with an ice pack.

Alonso said after the 4-1 defeat that Caicedo had picked up a “knock” and that Chelsea would have to wait and see following further assessments on Sunday.

“He was in pain and let's see how bad it is,” Alonso said.

open image in gallery Moises Caicedo was replaced by Jordan Henderson ( Reuters )

The circumstances in which Caicedo’s injury was dealt with left the Chelsea dugout unhappy with referee Michael Oliver.

Caicedo agonised on the deck for a considerable period before the Blues eventually sent their medical team on to treat him, with club doctors delaying their entry onto the pitch to try and prevent him having to come off for a minute, as per a new rule introduced in the Premier League this season.

Seemingly for the same reason, Caicedo leapt up and refused treatment from Chelsea medics when they approached him, but Oliver still ordered him to the touchline, reducing Chelsea to 10 men for a minute.

Caicedo also suffered a fitness scare during the international break when he was replaced at half-time of Ecuador’s 2-0 friendly win over Bolivia in midweek after feeling unwell.

The Blues are already without a number of key members due to injury including Reece James, Maxence Lacroix and Joao Pedro, with the club struggling for form following four defeats in five.

News.title: Trump hints at ‘four or five’ finalists for White House press secretary after telling Katie Zacharia ‘you don’t need this’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump suggested in a Fox News interview Saturday that he was considering “four or five” finalists for White House press secretary.

Trump also defended Katie Zacharia, who was fired after just five days in the role following a widely panned debut briefing. The position has remained vacant since her October 16 ouster.

During the interview, host Kayleigh McEnany asked, “Do you think we’ll know who the new press secretary is before the new year?”

“Well, I have four or five people,” Trump, speaking by phone, responded. “I can tell you I have a hundred people that want that job as you can imagine. OK? A hundred people.”

He added: “We had one who’s a very good person, Katie. She’s a fantastic person ... But I saw the way she was being treated. I said, ‘Katie you don’t need this.’”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump hinted that he has 'four or five' finalists to become the next White House press secretary during an interview with Fox News on November 21 ( AP )

Zacharia, a former Newsmax commentator, drew criticism from Democrats and Republicans after her 14-minute debut briefing, during which she took questions from just three journalists and mistakenly referred to her husband as “my president.”

She also faced scrutiny for describing herself as a lawyer despite never passing a bar exam, and is now under investigation by the State Bar of California.

“She might’ve been able to fight her way out of it,” Trump continued. “But why should she be put in that position? ‘Cause I think she might’ve actually been very good. But I said ‘what do you need this for?’”

He continued: “They really came at her. I was surprised to see it. Nasty. So maybe that’s over with now and somebody else would come in and they’ll be a little bit more normalized.”

After her ouster, Zacharia defended her performance, saying she was not given enough time to prepare. Asked by The Free Press this week whether she would take the job again, she responded: “There’s just no way that I would say no to that man.”

open image in gallery Katie Zacharia was fired after just five days in the role following a widely panned debut briefing. The position has remained vacant since her October 16 ouster ( Getty )

Names floated among political analysts as potential new hires in recent weeks include Danielle Alvarez, a former senior adviser to Trump’s 2024 campaign, and Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly.

Earlier this month, Trump also offered the job to UFC president and CEO Dana White, who declined. Trump later said he had been joking.

Zacharia’s predecessor, Karoline Leavitt, served as the president’s chief spokesperson for 19 months before leaving in August to spend more time with her family.

Trump had four press secretaries during his first term: Sean Spicer, Sarah Huckabee Sanders, Stephanie Grisham and McEnany, who is now a Fox News personality.

News.title: Wales ‘frustrated’ after being brought back down to earth by Wallabies
News.content:
Wales have a spring in their step coming into their game tonight as they host Australia at the Principality Stadium. Wales pulled off one of their best wins in recent memory last weekend, ending an over 70-year with for a victory over New Zealand. Despite pulling off that shock victory, Wales sit down in fifth in the northern hemisphere standings coming into this final round of fixtures. In all likelihood, they can only improve one spot. They have made four changes from the historic win over the All Blacks, with the likes of Josh Adams and Aaron Wainwright coming in.

“We were all immensely proud to make history last week,” Wales head coach Steve Tandy said. “There is a new opportunity and challenge for us against Australia and we are looking to back up our performance this weekend. It is our last home game of this competition. The support that fans give to the players and staff has been incredible and we cannot wait to get back out at Principality Stadium.

“We made nearly 350 tackles, the ball in play time was one of the highest in Test rugby in the last three years and we have got competition. The plan was always to freshen up and we are likely to do similar for the week after, because we need to find out about players. We have fresh and hungry players coming in, which will add the energy that we need at the weekend. The training environment is getting more competitive in certain positions we have the ability to put people in and feel confident about performance.”

News.title: Whiff of arrogance as Arsenal unexpectedly implode
News.content:
Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. I think we were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press. And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

“But it wasn’t. And when it wasn’t, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

“And I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it’s game on. And from that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set piece.

“And then you have to react. And then we went back to the team that the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count.”

News.title: ‘Remarkable’ Ireland deliver perfect riposte to Erasmus mind games
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Ireland vs South Africa from the Nations Championship in Dublin, with both teams harbouring hopes of finishing the day at the top of their respective tables.

Ireland and South Africa have both won four of their five games in the group phase of this year’s inaugural Nations Championship, and come into their last match before next weekend’s finals still in contention for the overall title.

Andy Farrell’s men begin the afternoon in third in the Northern Hemisphere table, but level on points with second-placed England, who are currently hosting New Zealand, and just one point behind leaders France, who take on Argentina this evening.

The reigning world champions, meanwhile, are guaranteed to at least remain in second in the Southern Hemisphere table, but are just one point behind the All Blacks at the top of the group, so will be hoping for a favour from Steve Borthwick’s men at Twickenham.

The Springboks will be without head coach Rassie Erasmus for today’s contest in the Irish capital, with the 54-year-old facing a six-match ban because of his criticism of officials following his team’s narrow defeat by France last weekend, including asking whether they were “match-fixing”.

“He’s been hands-on with our team, and we’re in a good space,” assistant coach Mzwandile Stick said of Erasmus on Friday. “Irrespective of what has happened, we love him, we appreciate him, and no one is going to break us. I can tell you that for sure.”

In the same press conference, Erasmus predicted that Sam Prendergast would be cleared to play after being cited for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji. The Ireland fly-half escaped punishment from the independent panel and starts for Farrell’s side this afternoon.

News.title: Alonso heckled as Chelsea are humiliated by Leeds
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

“(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

“It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his new-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a big shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

“It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

News.title: England obliterate All Blacks in record win
News.content:
A nearly perfect half for England was ruined just two minutes before half-time when Ben Earl gave up a penalty from the restart, immediately after scoring the home side’s third try. New Zealand kicked to the corner and Ethan de Groot plunged over to give the All Blacks a lifeline they scarcely deserve.

Until that point, this was as dominant a half against top-tier opposition that we have ever seen from Steve Borthwick’s team. Much like they did against Australia, England have strangled the life out of New Zealand and have enjoyed a preposterous 78 per cent territory.

They have also repeatedly cut New Zealand open in midfield. The interplay between Fin Smith, Seb Atkinson and the regal George Furbank has been sumptuous to watch. England have struggled to break New Zealand down in the red zone but still have three tries to show for their efforts. Smith’s cute little poke through was grounded by Henry Slade after five minutes and then scrum half Jack van Poortvliet did his best Superman impression by diving over the top of a ruck for England’s second try.

Earl also went route one, picking off the back of a scrum and through Cam Roigard’s tackle to put England in dreamland. Not every department has functioned perfectly. New Zealand have been on top of the scrum and have stopped the English maul in its tracks, but the All Blacks have been dominated physically. When was the last time we said that about an England team?

The De Groot try has taken the wind out of England’s sails a little but a similar setback took place in the Australia game just before half-time and Borthwick’s team responded with an emphatic second-half performance.

England need to see this out too, otherwise they’ll be kicking themselves all the way through to the World Cup.

News.title: England lose to ‘Australia B team’ in thriller
News.content:
England’s white-ball tour of Australia continues as a five-match T20 series between kicks off in Melbourne at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground, with the sandpapergate saga rumbling on. The first part of the tour went England’s way, as they came from 1-0 down to win the ODI series 2-1, following wins in Adelaide and Hobart. All of that action on the field has taken place whilst there has been plenty of “he said, she said” as some, like Cameron Bancroft, David Warner and Usman Khawaja say that everyone knew about the use of sandpaper whilst Pat Cummins has categorically denied that.

The last time these sides met in a T20 series back in September 2024, the three-match series ended in a 1-1 draw, with the final match abandoned. England won the last series played down under in October 2022, claiming a 2-0 series victory. Therefore, England are unbeaten in their past three bilateral mens’s T20I series against Australia. England are currently top of the ICC T20 rankings, with Australia third.

England were last in T20 action back in September, when they beat Sri Lanka 3-0. They have won all but two completed T20Is in 2026, with their last defeat coming in the World Cup semi-finals against India in March. They have decided to rest a number of the seamers who played in the ODI series including Jofra Archer and Gus Atkinson, whilst Josh Tongue is out injured. With those seamers absent, it will likely present opportunities for Henry Crocombe and Eddie Jack. Jacob Bethell remains out with a knee injury that he is still struggling with whilst Jos Buttler continues to recover from an hamstring injury.

Australia bombed out of the T20 World Cup in the group stages earlier this year, the first time that has happened since 2009. They did though win their most recent T20 series, beating Bangladesh 3-0 in June. Australia’s fast-bowling trio of Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have all been rested for England’s white-ball tour, something that was planned long before the 2018 sandpapergate was reignited. Not only are that trio not involved but the likes of Nathan Ellis and Xavier Bartlett will also not play, therefore it will be a relatively inexperienced bowling attack for the hosts.

They will give a debut to wicketkeeper Sam Harper, who was named player of the tournament in the most recent edition of the Big Bash with the Melbourne Stars, with Josh Inglis being rested ahead of Australia’s upcoming busy Test schedule. Inglis is not the only player to sit out this series having played in the ODIs, with the likes of Travis Head, Matt Renshaw, Cameron Green and Cooper Connolly also not participating.

Play from the MCG gets under way from 8.15am GMT.

News.title: Anthropic plunges as Wall Street suffers AI sell-off
News.content:
Anthropic’s share price slump triggered a sharp sell-off on Wall Street with tech stocks closing down more than 5pc.

More than $163bn was wiped off the value of the AI giant on Friday, just a day after it touched a $2tn valuation on its stock market debut.

The decline prompted a wider flight from AI shares, with the tech-focused Nasdaq 100 down 5.6pc. It means the index has now erased all its gains year to date.

The S&P 500 fell 3.7pc at close, putting it on course for its worst week since Donald Trump’s ‘liberation day’ tariffs last year, and into correction territory.

Anthropic has endured a hugely volatile introduction to public markets, surging as much as 39pc on the Nasdaq on Thursday, before closing the day 17pc higher.

However, it fell by as much as 14pc to $83.16 on Friday, just above where it started trading on Thursday.

It started the day at $97, less than 24 hours after it hit a high of $115.

The latest sell-off has fuelled fears that the company’s record-breaking float, which raised $87bn, is not enough to dispel lingering concerns over the AI bubble.

It comes after a series of threats to the investment boom.

That includes anti-data centre Democrats taking control of Congress, the downfall of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang and tighter export controls on chips to China.

The Philadelphia semiconductor index, a grouping of the major US chip companies, dropped by as much as 9pc on Friday.

AI-linked companies dragged the Nasdaq lower, with the likes of semiconductor maker ARM losing 14pc.

CoreWeave also weighed on the Nasdaq, with its shares down 12pc.

European shares were also on track for their worst week since March amid investor concern over an AI bubble.

In a day of volatile swings on Wall Street, Nvidia also slipped behind Google parent Alphabet to become the fourth-most valuable US company.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “It’s been another hectic and negative week and one where even positive news is struggling to help the market stabilise.”

Pressure on stocks also rose after Donald Trump on Friday threatened to ban technology companies from building data centres outside of the US.

In a White House press conference, Mr Trump warned there would be “tremendous penalties” on US companies that tried to build data centres in foreign countries.

He said: “We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centres outside of our country. We’re not going to allow that to happen.”

He added: “We’re going to fight very hard for the data centres because we’re not going to let China [overtake us].”

The ban threat will raise questions for AI developers who are spending hundreds of billions of pounds building data facilities in the UK, Europe and across Asia.

It is not clear whether Mr Trump’s ban would apply to all data centre developers or just the most advanced facilities.

The sell-off came as Anthropic’s approach to copyright was slammed by news publishers, who said the company lacks “a basic moral compass”.

The News Media Association (NMA), which represents titles including The Telegraph, The Times and The Guardian, attacked the company for its policy on journalism.

Anthropic told investors it could not guarantee it would adhere to measures that prevented journalism from being used to train AI models.

The Claude maker said it took steps to abide by paywalls but that this “may not always be successful”.

News.title: New case of bird flu confirmed in US dairy farm worker
News.content:
Another person in the US has contracted H5N1, bringing the number of confirmed cases in the country this year to four.

The patient, whose identity has not been released, works on a dairy farm in the US state of Oregon, local health officials confirmed on Thursday.

Their symptoms are reportedly mild, and they do not require hospitalisation.

All four of the H5N1 cases recorded in the US this year – one of whom died – have been in dairy workers who have had close contact with sick cattle.

The virus, which experts have long warned could trigger the next human pandemic, has become endemic in US dairy cattle after ‘jumping’ from birds to cows in late 2023.

Since then, it has been detected on nearly 1,000 dairy farms across dozens of states.

The US has reported 74 human cases of bird flu since 2024, nearly all of which have been from close contact with poultry or cows.

Earlier this month, United Farm Workers (UFW), a union which represents thousands of workers across the US, released a statement on X that said many farmers were experiencing symptoms of H5N1 and were not being tested for the virus.

They said the workers’ symptoms ranged from “very mild to very severe” and that surveillance on farms had been poor.

Sports.title: France reach Nations Championship final with bonus-point Argentina win
Sports.content:
France book South Africa rematch in Nations Championship final with bonus-point victory over Argentina

Antoine Dupont was back at scrum-half and helped France to a big win

France reached the Nations Championship final after beating Argentina 45-17 with seven tries on Saturday.

England's 37-12 win against New Zealand left France needing a bonus-point victory to make the November 29 final against South Africa, who topped the southern hemisphere group despite losing to Ireland.

Already leading 21-10, Emilien Gailleton got France's fourth try for the bonus point in the 64th minute against 14 men, and moments later the yellow card for Pumas prop Mayco Vivas was upgraded to red.

France finished with three more tries. Lock Tyler Duguid charged through following an attacking lineout, centre Kalvin Gourgues showed stunning pace from near halfway to make the left corner, and Louis Bielle-Biarrey completed the rout with his 31st try in 30 tests.

France beat the Springboks 21-19 last week in Paris

In the first half lock Mickaël Guillard and try-scoring hooker Peato Mauvaka crossed for France. Returning fly-half Matthieu Jalibert cleverly set up silky centre Gourgues shortly after the break for the first of his two tries.

Argentina led briefly at 10-7 for 10 minutes thanks to a converted try from centre Justo Piccardo and a penalty from fly-half Tomas Albornoz.

Jalibert's faster than expected recovery from a torn thigh allowed captain Antoine Dupont to resume at scrum-half after wearing the No 10 jersey a week ago against South Africa.

Dupont showed his class at the end with a kick down the left flank for Bielle-Biarrey's try.

Gourdes nailed five conversions as a makeshift kicker on the night.

Tributes were held before the game for Federico Martín Aramburú, the former Argentina player who died four years ago after being fatally shot in Paris.

Debutant Kevin Doets faces three-time champion Gerwyn Price in the first semi-final before Michael van Gerwen and Gian van Veen renew their rivalry on the big stage; watch the climax of the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports

Grand Slam of Darts: Michael van Gerwen proves he is still a force to be reckoned with after reaching semi-finals

Highlights of an EPIC quarter-final between Michael van Gerwen and Tom Sykes at the Grand Slam of Darts

Michael van Gerwen has shown he is still a force to be reckoned with as he prepares to face fellow Dutchman Gian van Veen in his first major semi-final in over a year.

With Luke Littler and Luke Humphries already at home, Van Gerwen will be looking to get his hands on some TV silverware for the first time since the 2025 World Series of Darts Finals.

Van Gerwen, who threw perfection in the opening leg against Tom Sykes to record his first televised nine-darter on Sky Sports in 14 years, takes on Van Veen on Sunday, with debutant Kevin Doets going head-to-head with three-time champion Gerwyn Price in the first semi-final.

Sports.title: Wales fall short in tight defeat to Australia
Sports.content:
Nations Championship: Wales fall short in 29-26 defeat to Australia after epic New Zealand victory

Louis Rees-Zammit and Wales were narrowly beaten by Australia

Wales failed to back up their epic win over New Zealand as Australia edged their Nations Championship match 29-26 in Cardiff.

A first victory over the All Blacks since 1953 had led to week-long celebrations in Wales.

But Australia, having soaked up fierce first-half pressure, produced some fine attacking rugby after the break to prevent Wales from winning three on the spin for the first time since the 2023 World Cup.

Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau secured a try-bonus point for Australia as Ryan Lonergan and Carter Gordon added nine points with the boot.

Australia's Max Jorgensen scores a try

Wales also scored four tries through Dewi Lake's double, Blair Murray and Ryan Elias, with Sam Costelow landing three conversions, but fell agonisingly short.

Australia fly-half Carter Gordon scored ⁠a penalty in the 74th minute to give the Wallabies a 29-21 lead, which proved enough for victory despite Wales securing a fourth try ⁠through replacement hooker Elias two minutes ​from time.

Wales battled for the winning score in a dramatic close to the match but their attempt to go the length of the field was ended when the ball was ‌knocked on.

"Wales are a tough outfit. What a match," Ikitau said after he was awarded player of the match.

"It's been a tough couple of weeks for us. I know the heart's always there but when you don't get the results it's pretty disheartening. I'm proud of the boys and proud of the effort today."

Sports.title: De Zerbi compares Williams-Barnett to Lamine Yamal - who is Spurs teen?
Sports.content:
Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi was not surprised by a dazzling full-debut display from “special” talent Luca Williams-Barnett and compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal after Saturday’s 2-0 win over Ipswich.

De Zerbi turned to the highly rated Spurs academy graduate after two bright cameos and he delivered, scoring on his first Premier League start after 15 minutes before a mazy run set up Dominic Solanke at the start of the second half.

After Williams-Barnett made his senior debut at the age of 16 last season, the clamour for the teenager to play has only increased during a difficult last 12 months, and De Zerbi decided 10 days ago to include him in the starting line-up against Ipswich.

During a chat on Thursday with the skilful England U19 international, De Zerbi asked Williams-Barnett to play with freedom and work hard without the ball "like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal" before he agreed when asked if the teenager could reach similar heights.

After De Zerbi revealed Williams-Barnett prepared for the match on the team bus by watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar, he said: "Luca is a special player.

"I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top team-mates.

"I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important.

"The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

"And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

"Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur and Ipswich Town

Asked if Williams-Barnett can reach the level of Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi said: "Yes, I think so.

"And one of the best things in my career… I've seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

"I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?"

Who is Williams-Barnett?

Image: Williams-Barnett celebrates his goal for Spurs

Williams-Barnett joined Tottenham as a 10-year-old from Luton, his home town, and has been in the Spurs academy since.

There has been plenty of hype around the winger, whose talent was noticeable when he won the U18 Premier League goal of the season award for a long-range stunner against Leicester.

The teenager then began featuring in Spurs' first-team squads, but after being named on the bench for a handful of games in the 2024/25 season, Williams-Barnett was finally handed his debut in September 2025 by then-boss Thomas Frank as he came on as a substitute in the Carabao Cup third-round home win over Doncaster.

Eight days later, Williams-Barnett signed his first professional contract with Spurs at the age of 17.

His appearance against Doncaster proved to be his only first-team action last season as he hit a hat-trick against Leicester for Tottenham U21s before netting five goals in a win over Slavia Prague for Spurs' academy team in a UEFA Youth League game.

He was deservedly rewarded by De Zerbi for a fine youth season by playing a part in Tottenham's pre-season plans as he showed glimpses of his skill and quality during some run-outs.

But he has finally made his first-team breakthrough this season, and he should have had an assist on his Premier League debut in last month's win over Crystal Palace after he came on as a substitute to superbly tee up Mohammed Kudus, who somehow missed to add a third in the 2-0 win (watch below).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mohammed Kudus missed a glorious chance in the win over Palace after great work by Williams-Barnett

Ahead of the defeat to Leeds, De Zerbi admitted Williams-Barnett was ready for a full debut, and he considered it for the win at Chelsea last month, but he was again a late second-half substitute in the loss at Elland Road.

But substitute appearances are set to no longer be an option after his stunning full debut against Ipswich.

On the international stage, Williams-Barnett has represented England at all levels between U15s and U19s to date.

In September, he came on for Arsenal sensation Max Dowman to make his England U19 debut in a 1-0 win over the Republic of Ireland.

Tottenham and Arsenal have two of England's brightest prospects, and the pair could play major parts in north London derbies in the years to come.

Solanke: You have to give Williams-Barnett assist!

Image: Dominic Solanke scored Spurs' second from Williams-Barnett's cross

Williams-Barnett was denied an assist on his full debut despite his fine work to set up Solanke's goal.

Williams-Barnett terrorised the Ipswich defence from his left-wing position to tee up the striker with a low cross for a simple 51st-minute finish.

But Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton's diversion into Solanke's path meant Williams-Barnett was not officially credited with the assist.

It meant Williams-Barnett, at the age of 18 years and 51 days, just missed out on becoming the second-youngest player to both score and assist in a Premier League game (Michael Owen in December 1997 at 17y 364d).

Solanke, however, hopes the club will appeal the assist decision.

He told Sky Sports: "No, you have to give that to him! It's just a tiny touch [from Walton]. Hopefully the club can sort that out."

He added on Williams-Barnett's display: "Luca was magnificent today.

"We see him in training every day. We know what a player he is. He's such a talent, honestly, and to see him come in and do that in his first Premier League start is crazy.

"We'll be celebrating with him today, but he can bring so much to us."

Sports.title: Raya injured but Madueke rescues point for Arsenal in seesaw Newcastle draw
Sports.content:
If Mikel Arteta was delighted to see the back of Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s head coach, the bad news is that another similarly awkward technical area adversary has been installed at St James’ Park.

Arsenal’s manager never seemed to relish trips to face Howe’s old team and he certainly did not enjoy this latest trip to Tyneside, where Matthias Jaissle’s initially overwhelmed team fought back commendably to earn a point courtesy of a stellar second-half performance. At half-time the crowd had felt close to turning against Jaissle but he held his nerve and, thanks to a triple substitution and subtle tactical rejig suggested he is no mug after all.

It left Arsenal – who lost their outstanding goalkeeper David Raya to a potentially significant second-half shoulder injury – still top of the Premier League, six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City, and Arteta with a face like thunder.

View image in fullscreen David Raya is helped off the pitch with a shoulder injury. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA

Just last week Bruno Guimarães claimed he was “beloved” by Newcastle fans but the club’s former captain turned Arsenal midfielder found himself serenaded by a soundtrack of boos of the sort usually reserved for Sunderland players. Newcastle’s problem is that, despite spending about £275m this summer, they have struggled to replace last season’s departed star trio – Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.

That reality perhaps left Howe’s successor – who arrived just before the start of the season – making a not so subtle point with his team sheet here. Of Jaissle’s starting XI only the goalkeeper, Lukas Hornicek, the right-back Amar Dedic and the midfielder Sean Steur were close-season signings.

The other five new faces were either benched (Nico González and Matias Fernandez-Pardo) or did not make the 20-man matchday squad (Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Touré). Admittedly Ewen Jaouen is injured but, given Bamba and Toure cost a combined £78.5m, their omission represented quite a statement. Ditto the decision to bench González and Fernandez-Pardo and their individual £50m plus price tag.

Meanwhile the jury remains out on Hornicek. The Czech international has made some excellent saves this season but, initially here, his kicking proved pretty much uniformly poor and he was fortunate to be reprieved after hesitating too long as the impressive Kai Havertz closed in.

Jaissle’s frustration with his goalkeeper proved well apparent as Arsenal took increasing control of a first half that saw Newcastle’s lone striker, William Osula, isolated and even their normally imperious England left-back Lewis Hall given a thorough work out by Noni Madueke.

Much to Arteta’s chagrin, Lewis Miley, preferred to González in the midfield holding role, endeavoured to slow the tempo but the red tide could only be stemmed for so long.

When Havertz dispossessed Hall after the latter miscontrolled a long ball, he cut inside and slid a highly intelligent, beautifully calibrated, pass across to the on-rushing Eberechi Eze. Without breaking stride, Eze exhibited perfect balance and unleashed a gorgeous first-time shot that arrowed, inexorably, past Hornicek.

Quick Guide Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: key facts Show • Arsenal ended a 21-game run of Premier League games without a draw (W18 D3) since a 2-2 draw with Wolves back in February. • Since the start of last season, all five of Newcastle’s Premier League draws at St James’ Park have been a 2-2 scoreline. • Eberechi Eze’s opener for Arsenal (pictured) was his first Premier League goal since April, which also put the Gunners 1-0 ahead against Newcastle. Opta Photograph: Lee Smith/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

As the home fans fell eerily silent, Arteta and his staff celebrated a goal sufficiently special to rebuke suggestions that his side are all about efficiency at the expense of artistry these days.

With Declan Rice always available to reinforce his defence and smother any flickering home attack it proved a struggle to recall Newcastle making a meaningful attacking touch inside Arsenal’s box. Fans stationed near the home dugouts told Jaissle what they thought of it all.

Arsenal’s pressing was initially so good that Newcastle were left almost incapable of playing short passes and, instead found themselves reduced to aimless long balls. With Rice and Martin Ødegaard apparently operating on a different midfield planet an equaliser felt like a distant dream.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Yet that seemingly ambitious vision was something Harvey Barnes proved fully capable of buying into. When, early in the second half, Ødegaard made an uncharacteristic error, his heavy touch sliced the ball in Osula’s direction and the Dane played it into Barnes’s path.

All that remained was for the left winger to take a single, steadying, touch before an assured finish left the hitherto redundant David Raya picking his shot out of the net.

Jaissle’s second-half introduction of Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey and Anthony Elanga – all at Newcastle last season – at the expense of Dedic, Steur and Jacob Murphy was paying dividends. Suddenly, almost astonishingly, Arsenal were the team in danger of being pressed into submission.

The home side were closing their guests down far higher up the pitch and had morphed into an infinitely more menacing team. Soon, they were ahead when a Hall corner was headed down by Dan Burn, allowing Malick Thiaw to stab the ball beyond Raya.

View image in fullscreen Malick Thiaw roars his approval after giving Newcastle a second-half lead. Photograph: Harvey Murphy/Danehouse/Getty Images

Shortly afterwards Arsenal’s goalkeeper was helped off the pitch in evident pain after sustaining a nasty left shoulder injury during an ostensibly benign collision with Osula. On came Kepa Arrizabalaga in a triple substitution also featuring Guimarães’s exit.

Madueke though was still around and he reminded everyone of his presence by meeting the counterattacking Ødegaard’s fine pass, dummying two defenders and watching his slightly deflected shot evade Hornicek’s grasp.

No matter; Jaissle had done enough to win plenty of hearts and minds. Not least the chair, Yasir al-Rumayyan, over from Riyadh to watch his first match of the season and reportedly “take the club’s temperature”.

Sports.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.

It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.

Farke’s side were tactically superior against flimsy opposition. For Chelsea, who were jeered off after their fifth defeat in 11 games, the indignities piled high. Records are falling, but not in a good way. This is the first time in 67 years they have lost grudge matches at home to Leeds and Tottenham in the same season, leaving Alonso on shaky ground with supporters, and there was further alarm when Cole Palmer appeared to clash with Willie Isa after the side’s “cultural architect” urged Chelsea’s No 10 to acknowledge the crowd at full-time.

Palmer cut a disgruntled figure throughout and did nothing to make Thomas Tuchel rethink his decision to leave him out of the England squad. The one mitigating factor is that few players will thrive in a directionless team. What does Alonso want Chelsea to be? No one knows. There are no patterns of play and the main takeaway from this surrender is that the only sign of an identity was an addiction to calamitous defending.

Calvert-Lewin followed the lead of Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey by tormenting Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana. Alonso was appointed in the summer but the pressure is mounting already. The Spaniard’s control even let him down when a ball dropped towards the technical area in the second half.

View image in fullscreen Emmanuel Emegha (right) celebrates scoring Chelsea’s goal with teammates. Photograph: Toby Melville/Reuters

It was some turnaround from the visitors, who trailed when Emmanuel Emegha marked his full debut by scoring his first goal since joining Chelsea from Strasbourg last summer. Farke continues to excel. The best that can be said of Alonso is that he needs time. Losing Moisés Caicedo early on was a blow. Even then it is impossible to understand Alonso’s intended style of play. There is an emptiness to Chelsea. They faced 21 shots and failed to up the physicality after crumbling against Sunderland.

Admittedly Alonso is dealing with João Pedro’s absence in attack. He has toyed with a false nine in recent weeks, but used a target man this time and the early signs were promising. Emegha gave Chelsea a focal point and finished well when an error from James Justin allowed Rogers to send the striker through on goal.

Leeds were on top when they conceded. Chelsea had lost Caicedo, who made way for Jordan Henderson after injuring his back in a collision with Justin, and were already wobbling. Calvert-Lewin spurned three excellent headed chances and Leeds levelled after 28 minutes.

View image in fullscreen Noah Okafor holds off the Chelsea defence to score a 28th-minute leveller. Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty Images

Chelsea had no defensive leaders. Fofana is too easily ruffled in the air and was involved in the equaliser. He sent a routine header back into dangerous territory and Chelsea panicked. Josh Acheampong mistimed his jump as the ball bounced around and Calvert-Lewin was able to find Okafor, who cut inside and slipped a low shot past Emiliano Martínez.

Farke was rightly disappointed that Leeds were not ahead at half-time. Tarik Muharemovic charged forward from defence, away from Palmer’s feeble challenge, and crossed for Calvert-Lewin to flick wide. Ethan Ampadu ran midfield, outshining Henderson and Romeo Lavia, and the Leeds wing-backs were wonderful. Ao Tanaka went close and Muharemovic grimaced after having a goal disallowed for offside.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Alonso looked bewildered. Colwill, low on confidence since returning from a knee injury, kept misplacing simple passes and Estêvão Willian was ineffective on the right. Chelsea were jeered off and made a dreadful start to the second half. Martínez should have conceded a penalty for a challenge on Calvert-Lewin. Michael Oliver then pointed to the spot when Rogers was adjudged to have handled Jayden Bogle’s shot.

Quick Guide Chelsea 1-4 Leeds: key facts Show • Leeds have won their first game against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in all competitions since December 1999, ending a run of 10 away games against the Blues without victory (D2 L8), while they’ve scored 4+ goals away at Chelsea for the first time since January 1970 (5-2). • Leeds have won their first Premier League game in London since May 2022 (2-1 against Brentford), ending a run of 15 matches in the Capital without victory (D4 L11), while it’s their biggest winning margin in London since April 2003 (6-1 against Charlton). • Leeds’ Ao Tanaka (pictured with Cole Palmer) committed three fouls inside the first six minutes against Chelsea; no player has ever fouled more often inside six minutes in a Premier League game on record (since 2003-04). Opta Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

It looked harsh given Rogers’ arm was close to his body and the ball hit him close to the shoulder but the decision was upheld after a VAR check. Calvert-Lewin stepped up to score and the result was never in doubt once Leeds led. Chelsea, who were mentally fragile, crumbled. Leeds were rampant. Chelsea could not cope with Ampadu’s long throws. One was half cleared but Sean Longstaff worked the ball back to Ampadu, who crossed for Okafor to make it 3-1.

“We are in a fragile moment mentally,” Alonso said. “When we receive a punch we didn’t recover. The fans were disappointed because the expectations are high. I understand their disappointment. There were moments that we were not competing at the level required.”

The closing stages were miserable for Chelsea, who have already conceded 20 goals. Leeds cruised and completed the humiliation when Aaronson, a late substitute, turned past Malo Gusto before sliding a shot through Martínez’s grasp.

The home sections had already emptied out. Those who stayed soon made their displeasure clear.

Sports.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
Sports.content:
New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.

Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”

Sometimes football is simply a bit daft, a series of events linked by very little discernible pattern – and that’s how it was before the break. Perhaps that’s just what happens when two of the three teams with the lowest possession stats in the league meet up; they can’t both not have the ball and so at least one side ends up having to do something they’re not used to. The second half was rather less frenetic and rather more coherent, as Palace’s full-backs played more conservatively.

View image in fullscreen Thomas Frank shows his frustration during his first game in charge at Crystal Palace. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

“There are more positives than negatives from the game,” said Frank. “Offensively we looked like a threat. The effort and mentality I was extremely happy with. Defensively we conceded the first goal in a situation we 100% should have defended better, then an individual mistake. We’ll keep working on it, keep reinforcing the message in terms of what we want to do.”

In itself, playing without the ball is not a problem; absorbing pressure and striking on the break is a perfectly legitimate tactic and Lampard’s side have done it well at times this season. Palace are a slightly different case, given the obvious disconnect between their possession figure and Pierre Sage’s insistence he wanted to defend by holding the ball. That disparity, the sense that Palace’s players were unable to play as he wanted them to play, was probably the strongest argument in favour of cutting their losses quickly.

View image in fullscreen Tatsuhiro Sakamoto restores Coventry’s lead with their second goal. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Frank abandoned the back three that had been the default not merely under Sage but also under Oliver Glasner, preferring a 4-3-2-1 with Anan Khalaili returning at right-back. It’s fair to say the Israel international is rather better going forward than at defending; playing at full-back rather than wing-back looked a real struggle for him – although he may feel there was mitigation in the way he was repeatedly left exposed. It took just five minutes for Coventry to open Palace up on that flank, three players converging on Yann Gboho as he backheeled a return pass to Jack Rudoni, who swept it across the box for Taiwo Awoniyi to stroke in.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Quick Guide Coventry 3-2 Crystal Palace: key facts Show • Coventry have won four of their last seven Premier League games (L3), with no side scoring more goals in the competition since the beginning of October (12, level with Bournemouth). • Crystal Palace have conceded 27 goals in the Premier League this season; only in 1927-28 in the Third Division South have they conceded as many or more after 11 games in a league campaign (28). • Only Brighton (6) have scored more goals from outside the box than Coventry City (4) in the Premier League this season, with 31% of the Sky Blues’ goals this term being scored from distance (4/13) – only Spurs (33% - 4/12) have a higher such share. • In what was his 115th Premier League game as a manager, Frank Lampard (pictured) has been booked for the first time, while he also didn’t receive a single yellow card in any of his last 31 Premier League games as a player. Opta Photograph: Hannah McKay/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

It soon became clear, though, that this was never a game of only one goal. It was startlingly, thrillingly, almost disconcertingly open, with chances at either end. Yéremy Pino levelled, thrashing in after Jørgen Strand Larsen had laid off Daichi Kamada’s overhit cross with an outstretched heel. Then Khalaili missed his tackle, allowing Rudoni to surge forward and square for Tatsuhiro Sakamoto who, from just outside the box, lashed the bouncing ball into the top corner. Palace’s second equaliser was the result of a complete defensive breakdown. Pino’s initial cross was blocked and when he dinked in a second attempt, the only player even close to marking Strand Larsen was his teammate Kamada.

Coventry’s threat had seemed diminished in the second half, partly as Palace looked less skittish and partly because Awoniyi aggravated an ankle injury and was unable to continue after the break. But those late substitutions gave them new impetus and, after a very silly first half, the game was won with a pretty silly goal.

Sports.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
Sports.content:
For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.

Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.

“I am trying to select the players I think that are ready to play and the selection is thinking for the best of the team,” said Emery, who was again reluctant to blame the empty North Stand as a factor behind their disappointing home form, a sharp contrast to their 11-game winning run here last season. “In my experiences here and in Spain, when they [stadiums] are in works like we are in now, it’s a small sacrifice, but it’s not an excuse,” Villa’s manager added. “We have to play with this situation and next year it will be better.”

Villa’s frustration was underlined by a moment on the verge of half-time, when Emery gave Sunderland’s kit man, Luke Purcell, a gentle shove on the sidelines in an attempt to speed up a Villa restart. “We have increased our demands a lot, our level, but still there are favourites in front of us, to reach the top six, top four,” Emery said. “We are now again in a new construction with some new players who are sharing their qualities and we are trying to mix different players, young players to build our structure as fast as possible.”

View image in fullscreen Chemsdine Talbi of Sunderland shoots under pressure from Boubacar Kamara of Aston Villa. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images

With 90 minutes and 25 seconds showing on the big screens, Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched victory for Sunderland, the Moroccan winger shaving the upright of Zion Suzuki’s goal with a spell-bending strike. Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka, comfortably eliminating the defender, before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to the post. For Villa, a first clean sheet in the league here since March, but this draw extended their winless run to five matches in all competitions.

For Sunderland, this may not have been the dopamine hit of beating Chelsea, but it was was another gutsy showing, and without two key players in Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey, both of whom were absent through injury. It was a big team performance, another feather in the cap of Jules Ahoka, the 20-year-old midfielder who shone on his first Premier League start. Ahoka started last season playing on sandy pitches in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second division. “He is getting better game after game,” Le Bris said.
