Sunderland were happy to soak up the Villa pressure. Emery introduced the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, who trained with England under-21s during the international break, but in place of Nicolas Jackson rather than to join him in attack. By which point Mbaye had entered and combined with McGinn to fashion another nearly moment. Disbelief reigned in the stands, but had Talbi located the top corner, things could have felt a lot worse at the final whistle.

Sports.title: Pochettino needs New Manager Bounce to break torrid Manchester United turnover | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation.

Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager.

With hindsight, Michael Carrick’s dismissal was probably inevitable from the moment Manchester United lost at Hull on the opening weekend, just as Ruben Amorim was doomed from the moment cameras picked him up fiddling with magnetic counters on a tactics board in the rain at Grimsby. The message for Mauricio Pochettino is clear: don’t go playing badly on the east coast.

It’s generally acknowledged that Carrick, while he may not have been the ideal manager for United, was a long way down the list of the biggest problems at the club. So what was the point of sacking him? As Pochettino begins his United career at Anfield on Sunday, what realistically can any manager hope to achieve?

Sackings have become almost ritualistic. Football demands blood sacrifice. How else can the harvest be guaranteed but by the torching of the wicker man? How else can Crystal Palace stay up but by the sacking of Pierre Sage? Once, when the manager defined the club, bought the players, decided the tactics, set the mood, that perhaps made sense. When managers were messiahs, it requires only a slight tweak to the underlying theology to see a logic in sacrificing them.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino – a far more ebullient and charismatic figure than Michael Carrick – enjoyed Champions League success at Tottenham. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

But managers now, at least at the majority of Premier League clubs, are part of a wider structure. In one of his meltdowns at Spurs, Antonio Conte made the point that it made little sense for him to be answering questions about the broader future of the club when he had so little power compared with the tiers of executives. Why sack the manager rather than the head of recruitment or the sporting director or the chair?

The answer to that perhaps goes back to the emergence of the English idea of the manager, which began in the 1930s and blossomed in the post-war golden age of Matt Busby, Bill Shankly, Don Revie and Brian Clough. As Barney Ronay argues in The Manager, at least part of the reason he became a figure of such pre-eminence was that it was useful for the board to have a hapless ashen-faced figure standing out on the touchline to take the blame. A handful of geniuses aside, the manager was essentially a convenient scapegoat.

But does the sacrifice work? It was one of the shibboleths of football’s early data wonks that the new manager bounce was a myth. What was being witnessed when form improved after a sacking was nothing more than regression to the mean. Which sounds sensible: squads make games and are determined by finance. There is a wealth of evidence that the biggest single factor in determining league position is the wage bill.

And yet there is also evidence that new manager bounce does exist. A lot of early data analysis in football ignored the fact that those involved are human and respond emotionally to circumstance. More recent studies, though, suggest that, while around a quarter of clubs experience no improvement, the first five matches under a new manager show a 41% improvement in points per game, although the impact wears off after around 10 games.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That feels intuitively true and is readily explicable. A manager under pressure can become embattled, lashing out at enemies real and imagined, their capacity to make lucid decisions impaired as confidence ebbs, creating a doom spiral. Replacing him breaks that pattern and permits a psychological reset.

In a world where everything is studied endlessly, a new manager should make a team less predictable. It’s possible, of course, that as those early analyses suggested, performances would have turned anyway as part of a regression to the mean, but it is curious how often the uptick in form coincides with the replacement of the manager.

Anthropologists are yet to determine precisely why United sacrifice managers so frequently, although there does appear to be some sense of deflecting blame. There is also a sense that it has become routine, that reasons that once probably did exist have been forgotten over time.

Sacking the manager is just what the club do a few months into the season, the ritual now as divorced from its original purpose as modern Hallowe’en customs are from their origins in the Christian commemoration of All Hallows’ Eve.

Will the arrival of Pochettino help? He is a far more ebullient and charismatic figure than Carrick, whose status as a dead man walking for most of this season perhaps meant players did not take him as seriously as they might have an incumbent who appeared to be there for the long term, or had them beginning to ponder moves away from United.

But this remains a mismatched hotchpotch of a squad assembled over six previous managers. If there is some style of play that would suit most of them it has yet to reveal itself.

It will take time for Pochettino to instil in a side that are habitually outrun the levels of conditioning that characterised his Tottenham, and perhaps even longer to get them playing in a coherent pattern. There will probably have to be five or six new signings (and at least as many departures). Probably most difficult of all, there is the entire culture of the club to overhaul, which may not be possible without a change of ownership.

Given United came back from two goals behind three times in their final two games under Carrick, these are not usual circumstances: beleaguered managers rarely inspire such defiance, and the fans never turned against him. In that sense, there will not be the immediate benefit that comes when toxicity is removed.

Some sort of bounce, though, is probable under Pochettino, if only because a negative pattern has been broken. The question is how long it can be maintained.

Sports.title: WSL roundup: Chelsea thwarted by Liverpool keeper, London City move to third
Sports.content:
Khiara Keating’s resilient performance in goal denied Chelsea, the Women’s Super League leaders, and earned Liverpool a point, while London City Lionesses moved to within four points of the top by beating Crystal Palace 6-2.

After hard-fought 1-0 wins against Manchester City last Saturday and Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night, Chelsea drew a blank. Against Gareth Taylor’s side, Chelsea’s lack of cutting edge was clear a week after they beat City to go top. The calf injury picked up by Melvine Malard against City, the absence of Lauren James, who has a thigh injury, and the form of Aggie Beever-Jones, who scored her first WSL goal in more than a year in the 6-0 defeat of Charlton, have left Chelsea’s attack short.

Despite almost 70% possession and 47 touches in the box to Liverpool’s 12, Sonia Bompastor’s side amassed only 19 shots to Liverpool’s 13 and seven on target to their opponents’ four. Although the Blues remain unbeaten in the WSL, their third draw in five games in all competitions means City can leapfrog them at the top if they beat Tottenham on Sunday.

Liverpool had chances, particularly in the first half, but were hanging on after the break and Keating helped them to a fourth clean sheet, a tally bettered only by Bompastor’s side.

“It was a bit stressful; we don’t want to sit back but in games like this you have ‌to ride it out,” Keating told Sky Sports. “A clean sheet is ​always on our minds every game. We knew the mission. It was such a close game, it could have gone either way.”

The January transfer window will give the Blues an opportunity to strengthen their attack, but with three games before the winter break they need to step up in the final third, starting with their tricky fixture against London City Lionesses on 12 December after the international break.

London City came out on top in a thrilling end-to-end encounter with Palace. Having earned five of their nine points from losing positions this season, Palace did not cower when Eder Maestre’s team took the lead in Bromley. They twice came from behind to level the score before London City put the game beyond them.

The hosts had to weather some early Palace pressure, with Lexi Lloyd-Smith testing Elene Lete in the opening minute, with the goalkeeper starting in place of Mary Earps.

London City then took control and were rewarded in the 14th minute, when Daniëlle van de Donk turned in Isobel Goodwin’s cutback from close range. Palace were carved open, but they were not down and out against the team with ambitions of earning a place in next season’s Champions League.

View image in fullscreen Daniëlle van de Donk, who scored twice for London City Lionesses, celebrates with teammates. Photograph: Isabel Falle/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Jo Potter’s side drew level via an Abbie Larkin volley into the bottom corner to stun the home team, with the visiting fans in full voice telling Alexia Putellas what she could do with her Ballons d’Or.

It felt fated that the three-time winner of the trophy would have the last laugh and within six minutes of the restart she restored her team’s lead, the ball falling kindly for her to turn into an empty net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

London City’s third came three minutes later and the scenario was similar. Shae Yañez failed to deal with a cross and Van de Donk swept it goalwards. Molly Bartrip was there to hook it away but the referee deemed it to have crossed the line.

The home team’s lead was cut to one in style by Palace when Fuka Tsunoda’s reverse pass was met by Annabel Blanchard and her side-footed volley looped over Lete and in. It was a stunning move and a stunning finish.

London City’s squad depth and fresh legs eventually helped them stretch the game beyond the stubborn visiting team, with Alanna Kennedy heading them back into a two-goal lead 15 minutes after coming on.

They killed the game off four minutes later, this time Goodwin rising highest to head in from another set piece, and Putellas put the cherry on top with her second at the death, looping the loose ball in after a big save from Yañez.

There were positives for Palace, despite remaining a precarious three points clear of Birmingham City, who play Manchester United on Sunday, but big-spending London City are just a cut above.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership roundup: Dundee left reeling after 8-0 mauling by Hearts
Sports.content:
Wouter Vrancken said Hearts’ remarkable 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kaboré both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal completing the rout. Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

“Our best performance? Of course,” he said. “When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence. You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

“It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet. But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.”

Steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and Dundee’s performance, saying: “It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

“I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that. We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and shows grit. We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that. I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.”

View image in fullscreen Callum McGregor scores Celtic’s fourth against St Mirren. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

The recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1. The champions brushed off the loss of midfield pair Mika Baur and Benjamin Nygren to injury to consolidate their place at the top of the Premiership.

The centre-forward Camilo Duran was also on target as Celtic killed the game late in the first half with three goals in nine minutes. Callum McGregor grabbed his first league goal of the season before Killian Phillips scored a consolation from the spot.

With Baur facing up to 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Nygren nursing a heel problem, Martin O’Neill would have been delighted with how his midfield functioned.

Oxlade-Chamberlain made his fifth start of the season and McCowan his second. The pair had never started a game together before. O’Neill also introduced the former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joël van den Berg for a debut in the second half and the 19-year-old showed some good touches.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ryan Naderi hit a deflected 88th-minute winner at Fir Park as Rangers stayed four points behind Celtic by beating Motherwell 2-1. Naderi’s effort went in off the unfortunate Motherwell defender Martin Moorman as Rangers finally made the most of some late pressure to win.

The visitors looked as if they might be held to a third draw in four away games after Jake Girdwood-Reich had cancelled out an early opener from Rangers defender Emmanuel Fernandez. Rangers had 29 shots at goal but found Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen in top form and the New Zealand international pulled off one of the saves of the season to deny Dujon Sterling with five minutes left.

However, they netted after a corner when Naderi’s shot from eight yards went in off Moorman after the Austrian had blocked a shot from Badredine Bouanani.

Mario Frick enjoyed a dream start to life as Aberdeen manager by edging a six-goal thriller with a 4-2 win at Kilmarnock. Kevin Nisbet’s double along with Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall strikes secured three priceless points to leave the Rugby Park side rooted to the bottom

The visitors climbed to eighth spot after a remarkable afternoon where the Pittodrie side hit a much-needed scoring streak. Aberdeen opted to dispense with the services of Stephen Robinson after a run of one win from seven which saw them sink to second bottom and Frick was appointed as his replacement last Sunday.

Dundee United recorded their biggest ever win at Easter Road with an impressive 4-0 thrashing of Hibernian. Zac Sapsford’s first-half double laid the foundations before Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall found the net after the break.

The visitors were well worth the three points as they cemented their place in the top six and picked up their first win in Leith since 2021. It was a humbling afternoon for Hibs, who thought they had turned a corner under their new head coach, Marink Reedijk, after back-to-back victories before the international break.

Falkirk clung on to clock up six top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1966 with a 2-1 home victory against St Johnstone. John McGlynn’s team scored early in each half to remain third.

Jacob Murrell’s eighth goal of a superb debut season sent Falkirk on their way inside six minutes. Finley Barbrook’s second goal in as many games on 48 minutes doubled the advantage. Josh Campbell nodded in a late reply to serve up a scare but the hosts held firm.

Sports.title: European football: Doué carried off for PSG while Kane vows to return fresh
Sports.content:
Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as Paris Saint-Germain beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1.

Doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. The match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doué to receive treatment to his right knee before he was carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doué looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too.

“We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG’s coach, Luis Enrique, told the broadcaster Ligue 1+.

Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a video assistant referee (VAR) check for a handball.

Doué – who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break – put PSG ahead a minute later, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions.

His replacement, Ferran Torres, scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season – but first in two months. Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce.

Lazio will continue their surprise stay at the top of Serie A for at least another week after thumping Lecce 3-0, while a red-hot Donyell Malen scored four at Parma to lift Roma up to second.

Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio are two points ahead of their local rivals thanks to goals in each half from Tijjani Noslin and a late Davide Frattesi strike. Inter would close to within a point of Lazio with a win at struggling Atalanta on Sunday.

“I am proud of the mentality and the hunger shown today,” said Gattuso to Dazn. “It’s all down to the players, they have the right mentality, hunger and team spirit. What they are doing is incredible.”

Malen took his tally in all competitions for Roma this season to 16 before Wednesday’s daunting Champions League clash at Paris Saint-Germain. The Netherlands forward opened the scoring six minutes before half-time with a brilliant touch and finish, and put Roma, also unbeaten in the league, back in the lead in the 68th minute. Rodrigo Mora added Roma’s third moments later and then Malen capped another superb display with two more expert finishes.

Scott McTominay’s second-half strike gave Napoli a hard-earned 1-0 win over Torino to ease the pressure on manager Massimiliano Allegri, while Como stayed six points behind the leaders in fourth with a 2-0 home win over Cagliari.

In Spain, Kylian Mbappé’s third miss in his last six penalty attempts for club and country did not prove costly as ⁠Carlos Espi’s late winner helped Real Madrid to a 2-1 home victory over Celta Vigo. Real have 33 points from ⁠13 La Liga games, level ⁠with leaders Barcelona, ​but have now played a game more. The Catalans are in action on Sunday at home to Villarreal.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé reacts after he misses from the penalty spot. Photograph: Susana Vera/Reuters

Mbappé’s wastefulness from 12 yards had already ⁠cost Real a point earlier in the season and this time it was almost two as he lifted his effort well over the crossbar. He also ⁠missed a penalty when the Madrid side lost 1-0 at Real Betis in September, and for France ​against Morocco in the World Cup. On both ‌those occasions he shot ‌low and saw his effort saved, which perhaps might explain why he tried to go high ‌this time.

Celta took the lead inside six minutes when Pablo Durán scored from close range as he turned in Williot Swedberg’s low cross. Real had the chance to pull level when Mbappé had his arm pulled by Celta defender Javier Rodriguez and the referee pointed to the spot, but the Frenchman could not convert.

Real were level on 66 minutes when Jude ‌Bellingham drilled the ball low into the net from just inside box. It looked as though they would be frustrated before Espi’s initial header was saved by ​goalkeeper Ionut Radu, but he turned in the rebound.

Kike Salas equalised in added time at the end of the game as Sevilla earned a 1-1 draw with Real Betis in the Seville derby. Antony netted for the visitors early in the second half with his first goal of the season ⁠but Betis were denied a place in the top three by the equaliser.

Deportivo ​Alaves ended an eight-game winless ​streak with a 3-1 home victory ​over Deportivo La Coruna. Angel Perez opened the scoring for the hosts, but ​they were pegged back ‌to 1-1 by ​an own goal from ​Nahuel Tenaglia. Lucas Boye, who earlier missed a penalty, scored Alaves’ second and the points were made safe when Denis Suarez netted in added time. Valencia moved out of the bottom three with a 1-0 away win at Rayo Vallecano thanks to Jose Copete’s first half headed goal.

In Germany, Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha fired his side to the top of ⁠the Bundesliga table as they won 1-0 at bottom side Borussia Mönchengladbach. After Bayern Munich ⁠were held to ⁠a ​1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, Dortmund capitalised to take a two-point lead at the summit.

The home side played far better ⁠than their position would suggest, ​withstanding waves of pressure ‌from the visitors, ‌but Gladbach finally cracked in the 80th minute when Nmecha picked ‌up the ball on the edge of a packed penalty area and let fly. Unsighted by the thicket of bodies in front of him, the goalkeeper Daniel Batz misjudged the trajectory of the ball, and it flew over his right shoulder ‌and into the net.

View image in fullscreen Felix Nmecha fires home Borussia Dortmund’s winner against Borussia Mönchengladbach. Photograph: Christopher Neundorf/EPA

Gladbach created a number of chances, but Gregor Kobel came to the rescue ​with several fine saves for Dortmund, and once the goal went in, there was no way back for the hosts. Dortmund have 24 points after 10 games, two ahead of Bayern and third-placed Freiburg, who ⁠beat Elversberg 1-0.

Meanwhile, FifPro said it was “deeply concerned” by public comments from Bayern’s leadership about Jamal Musiala’s contract, accusing the German ⁠champions of putting pressure on the midfielder while he recovers from health problems. The global players’ union was responding to recent remarks by senior Bayern officials, including ⁠honorary president Uli Hoeness, ⁠chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen ​and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, about Musiala’s future at the club.

Hoeness this month questioned whether the 23-year-old Germany international could return to his ⁠previous level after being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. Dreesen later backed those remarks, saying Bayern would evaluate Musiala’s progress and discuss his future with his representatives. Rummenigge subsequently defended ⁠the comments, saying the club’s consideration of Musiala’s health and contract situation was both responsible and normal.

“Bayern’s honorary ​president, chief executive and former chief executive ‌have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract ‌in quick succession,” Fifpro said in a statement. “In FifPro’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put ‌pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.”

Musiala signed a contract extension with Bayern until 2030 in February last year. He has endured a difficult run of injuries and health setbacks in recent months. He broke his leg at the Club World Cup in July 2025, missed half of last season and collapsed twice within a ‌few days in August before being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. In September, he suffered a hamstring injury.

After September’s injury, Musiala returned as a substitute in Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday in which Harry Kane sustained an injury that may mean months of rehabilitation. On Saturday, Kane said he was looking to come back improved for “the business end of the season”. Kane tore a ligament in his left ankle and Bayern said the Ballon d’Or winner had undergone “successful surgery overnight” having earlier said that Kane would be out for “the next few months”.

Kane posted a photo on Instagram of himself smiling broadly, while sitting on a hospital bed after the surgery, with his leg encased in a medical boot. “The highs and lows of life!” the 33-year-old wrote. “Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.”

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle instantly apologises for X-rated Arsenal gaffe
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle gave an explicit assessment of Arsenal during a post-match gaffe after his Newcastle United side drew 2-2 with them.

The Magpies restricted the Premier League holders to just one point at St. James' Park on Saturday evening in an entertaining affair.

2 Jaissle was quick to apologise for the language he used when describing how good Arsenal are Credit: Getty

Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw hit back after Eberechi Eze opened the scoring, although Noni Madueke salvaged a draw for the champions late on.

Arsenal managed to avoid losing a league match for just the second time this season and remain at the summit with 11 played.

They also have the joint-best defence with Brighton having conceded just seven goals, and Jaissle is clearly impressed by their quality.

Jaissle apologises for swearing

During his post-match press conference, the Newcastle head coach was asked about how good this Arsenal team are.

"F****** good," he replied, before swiftly apologising for his coarse language as members of the press laughed at the comment.

Newcastle have only one league win from their last five, but the draw has taken them four points clear of the bottom three.

Arsenal on the other hand missed the chance to go eight points clear of Brighton at the top of the table with the Seagulls in action against Hull City on Sunday.

They will also be concerned over goalkeeper David Raya, who went off injured during the second half.

Raya went down holding his arm after an accidental collision with William Osula inside his area.

Kepa Arrizabalaga was brought on as his replacement in the 70th minute of play.

2 Arsenal were unable to beat Newcastle, but are still top of the league and on course for another title Credit: Getty

"We don't know, unfortunately," manager Mikel Arteta Arteta said on the severity of Raya's injury.

"Obviously he had to come off. We are worried, but we don't know. Tomorrow [Sunday], he will have an MRI."

The injury has come three days before Arsenal return to Champions League action with a home clash against Borussia Dortmund.

As it stands, Arrizabalaga looks set to start between the sticks on Tuesday night.

He has featured in the competition on just one occasion for Arsenal since signing from rivals Chelsea in 2025.

That appearance came in their last league phase match at home to Kazakhstan-based FC Kairat last season, which ended in a 3-2 win for Arsenal.

Sports.title: ‘Deeply concerned’ – Bayern Munich accused of ‘coordinated strategy’ against Jamal Musiala
Sports.content:
FIFPRO has criticised members of the Bayern Munich hierarchy after their comments on Jamal Musiala and his contract situation.

Musiala was diagnosed with temporary episodes of absence, caused by a neurological condition, this summer after fainting twice during matches.

3 Bayern chiefs have come under fire for their comments on Musiala and his contract amid his health issue Credit: Getty

The 23-year-old came off the bench for Bayern on Friday night in the 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln as he returned from a muscle injury.

However, former club chief Karl-Heinz Rummenigge expressed their concerns over his contract, which runs until 2030.

Rummenigge claimed that financial aspects of his deal are 'no longer feasible' amid Musiala's health issue.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness also previously questioned whether Musiala can 'regain the performance level he once had', whilst chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen warned of talks over his future.

Musiala backed in FIFPRO statement

FIFPRO, the international representative body of professional players, have now hit back at their comments in a strong statement.

"FIFPRO is deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from FC Bayern Munich's leadership calling into question the contract of Jamal Musiala as he returns from injury," it read.

"Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession.

"In FIFPRO's view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.

"Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure.

"Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

3 Bayern boss Vincent Kompany returned to the dugout during their 1-1 draw with FC Koln on Friday after his collapse last month Credit: Getty

"Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.

"Clubs, leagues and player unions have agreed at FIFA level that contractual stability is a core principle of the game. It protects clubs as much as it protects players.

"FIFPRO stands with Jamal Musiala and with all players who honour their commitments. We expect their employers to do the same."

What next for Musiala?

According to reports in Germany, Musiala's contract includes a release clause that becomes active next year.

This opens the door for a possible move away from Bayern and to the Premier League.

Liverpool have previously been interested in a move, with rivals Manchester City also being a speculated destination in the past.

3 FIFPRO reminded Bayern of their duty of care with Musiala and sided with the player in a strong-worded statement Credit: Getty

Chelsea, where the attacking star played academy football from 2011 to 2019, are another club to have had links.

Musiala has scored two goals and assisted one other in five matches this season.

This has come in just 233 minutes of action amid his fitness issues.

Sports.title: Manchester United-linked Calvin Bassey responds to rumours as Fulham boss compares him to all-time great
Sports.content:
Manchester United-linked Calvin Bassey responds to rumours as Fulham boss compares him to all-time great

Fulham captain Calvin Bassey has confirmed he is in negotiations over extending his contract at the club.

Bassey's current deal with the Cottagers is set to expire at the end of the season.



2 Bassey has been with Fulham since July 2023 Credit: Getty

However, Fulham hold the option to extend it for an additional 12 months.

What has Calvin Bassey said about his Fulham future?

But Bassey looks poised to remain in the capital.

"We are negotiating, we are still talking," Bassey told TNT Sports after Fulham's 1-1 draw with Manchester City.

"It's an amazing place to be, I have settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me.



"It's nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations."

Talks of a new contract to remain at Fulham comes amid rumours linking Bassey with a surprise switch to Manchester United.



The Red Devils are reported to be in the market for a centre-back in January after heavily investing in their midfield during the summer.

And Bassey, who has stepped up his game under Cottagers boss Alvaro Arbeloa, is reportedly being monitored by United.



Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa likens Calvin Bassey to Paolo Maldini

But Arbeloa will be extremely reluctant to lose his skipper, especially after a commanding display against City on Saturday.

"I told Calvin and David [Affengruber], 'You were like Maldini and Baresi today,'" Arbeloa told talkSPORT.

2 Arbeloa has Fulham on a five-match unbeaten run in the league Credit: Getty

"They are leaders and they are performing so well.

"We wanted to take the victory, but not a bad point."

Manchester City 1-1 Fulham

Rodrigo Muniz sparked hope of an unlikely victory at the Etihad Stadium when he struck in the 16th minute.



However, Elliot Anderson's goal just before the hour mark ensured the spoils were shared.

City thought they'd gone level earlier in the contest when Erling Haaland pounced on what appeared to be an error from Bernd Leno.

However, VAR decided Leno was in control of the ball, sparking a furious reaction from Haaland.

The result marked the first time Fulham avoided a loss to City in all competitions since September 2011.



As for City, they slumped to a fourth consecutive match without a win, leaving them six points behind league leaders Arsenal.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino dealt blow with key Man United player to miss Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford is not fit enough to play for Manchester United this weekend against Liverpool, talkSPORT understands.

The winger has not played since October 13 due to a hip injury and is not expected to return to action at Anfield on Sunday.



2 Rashford will not feature for United against Liverpool due to injury in a blow to Pochettino ahead of his first match Credit: Getty

This comes as a blow to new United head coach Mauricio Pochettino as their injury list remains packed.

Manuel Ugarte, Benjamin Sesko, Luke Shaw and Carlos Baleba are all set to be sidelined for the match as well.

Rashford first sustained his injury during the 2026 World Cup with England and struggled to shake it off since.



His last appearance came in the 2-0 Champions League defeat away at Atletico Madrid.

The 29-year-old was then benched for the 1-1 Premier League draw with Leeds United.



Rashford struggles at United continue

With his latest setback, Rashford continues to endure a difficult first season back at United following his loan spell in Barcelona.

He hit 14 goals and 15 assists in a campaign that saw him return to his best form and win LaLiga at Camp Nou.



Barcelona had the option to buy him permanently for £26million, but they did not activate it and instead brought in Anthony Gordon.

This is despite Rashford revealing that he wanted to stay at the club given his success on loan.

United welcomed him back for the 2026/27 campaign and now wears the no. 9 shirt, having previously donned 39, 19 and 10.

2 Pochettino faces a gruelling start to life on the United touchline with a trip to their historic rivals Credit: Getty



However, he is yet to score or assist in any eight matches across all competitions this season.

Rashford has started six of those fixtures, four of which have come in the Premier League.

A January move to Everton has been speculated as he continues to refind his feet.

It would see him follow a similar path to Jack Grealish, who has done well for the Toffees after a dip at Manchester City.



Rashford has also missed the last two England camps despite being part of their World Cup squad.

He is on 78 caps and 19 goals with the Three Lions since making his debut in May 2016.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta worried about David Raya as update on Arsenal star’s injury given
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta worried about David Raya as update on Arsenal star’s injury given

Mikel Arteta confirmed David Raya will undergo an MRI after he sustained an arm injury in Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Newcastle.

Raya exited the contest midway through the second half after what appeared to be an innocuous collision with Magpies striker Will Osula.

3 Raya's teammates were quick to console him following his arm injury Credit: Getty

The Spaniard briefly fell to the turf and then quickly got back to his feet, only to clutch his arm in serious pain.

It quickly became clear Raya could not continue and he made his way off with his left arm placed in a makeshift sling.

Raya was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Mikel Arteta gives update on David Raya injury

Arteta now faces a nervy wait as to whether Raya will be fit to feature for the Gunners against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Speaking to media following the contest, the Arsenal boss admitted he was unsure how serious Raya's injury was.

"We don't know, unfortunately," Arteta said.

"Obviously we had to come off. We are worried, but we don't know.

"Tomorrow, he will have an MRI."

How Arsenal's draw with Newcastle unfolded

It was far from a vintage performance for the Gunners, who took the lead courtesy of Eberechi Eze.

Eze was slipped in behind Newcastle's defensive line and coolly slotted home with a first-time effort from close range.

3 Arteta's side will finish the weekend with a minimum three-point buffer to second-placed Brighton Credit: Getty

But a rare mistake from Martin Odegaard allowed the hosts back into the contest.

The Norwegian mis-kicked a throw-in from the left and sent the ball straight to Osula, who drove towards goal from the right before he laid it to Harvey Barnes.

Barnes, who was in plenty of space, gratefully slid the ball home past a diving Raya.

Newcastle then took the lead in bizarre fashion courtesy of Malick Thiaw.

3 Thiaw thought he'd scored the winner, but it was not to be Credit: Getty

A Dan Burn header towards goal landed into Joe Willock, who was being closely marked by Gabriel on the goal-line.

Thiaw was first to the loose ball and lashed it into the net, sparking wild scenes from the Toon faithful.

A VAR check for offside followed, but Thiaw's goal remained.

However, the hosts could not hang on for just their fourth league win of the season as Noni Madueke rescued a point for the Gunners in the 78th minute.

The winger capped off a blistering counter-attack when he cut in from the right flank onto his left foot and unleashed a strike that squirmed under Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

Sports.title: Premier League player leaves stadium on crutches after freak injury coming out of tunnel
Sports.content:
Premier League player leaves stadium on crutches after freak injury coming out of tunnel

Coventry City were dealt a blow when Taiwo Awoniyi picked up a bizarre injury just before the second half.

The striker was on the score sheet for the Sky Blues in their impressive 3-2 win over Crystal Palace on Saturday.



2 Awoniyi got the Sky Blues on their way to a huge three points Credit: Getty

And Awoniyi may have scored more, only to hurt himself when he re-emerged for the final 45 minutes.

As he ran out of the tunnel, Awoniyi fell to the turf and clutched his leg, with two Palace players helping him off the ground.

The strange incident prompted Coventry boss Frank Lampard into an unplanned substitution as Sidiki Cherif was brought on in place of Awoniyi.



After the game, Awoniyi was filmed leaving the CBS Arena wearing a protective boot round his right foot and on crutches.

Frank Lampard gives update on Taiwo Awoniyi's injury

Lampard then confirmed following the match Awoniyi had felt his ankle in the first half, with the club to now fully assess the extent of the damage in the coming days.



"He hurt his ankle," Lampard said. "I don't know what the diagnosis is of that yet.

"He felt he could go and give it a try. Quite clearly, straight away he felt he couldn't."



How Coventry's win over Palace unfolded

Awoniyi got Coventry off to a dream start when he slotted home from close range in the fifth minute.

Sky Blues ace Jack Rudoni drove into the box on the left side and squared it to Awoniyi, who directed his effort past a diving Dean Henderson.

It was Awoniyi's second league goal this term for Coventry following his summer switch from Nottingham Forest.

2 Lampard has Coventry slowly creeping up the table after a difficult start Credit: Getty



Palace's Yeremy Pino equalised just eight minutes later, only for Tatsuhiro Sakamoto to restore the hosts' advantage on the half-hour mark.

But the two sides went into the break at 2-2 courtesy of Jorgen Strand Larsen, who lashed home from close range.

Yet there was one final twist to come in the 89th minute.

A long Coventry throw eventually found Brandon Thomas-Asante, who powered a header straight at Dean Henderson.

However, his save rebounded into a retreating Dwight McNeil and into the back of the net, sparking wild scenes among Sky Blues supporters.



The result marked Coventry's fourth league win this season and moved them up to 13th with 12 points.

As for Palace, who had Thomas Frank at the helm for the first time following his appointment, they remain rooted to the bottom of the ladder following their eighth defeat from 11 league games.

Sports.title: ‘Rotten’ – Shell-shocked Jason Cundy gives Xabi Alonso Chelsea sack warning as fans turn on manager
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy was a despondent man on the talkSPORT airwaves after watching his beloved Chelsea get thumped by Leeds United.

Leeds were 4-1 winners on Saturday in what was their first victory at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League since December 1999.



3 Leeds ended their 27-year wait to win at Stamford Bridge with a deserved victory against a dreadful Chelsea Credit: Getty

Noah Okafor scored two for the visitors, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson also netting against a woeful Chelsea side.

Cundy was at the Bridge and rushed to talkSPORT towers at the full-time whistle to join a gleeful Jamie O'Hara on the GameDay Phone-In.

'Disgusting' Chelsea leave Cundy worried

"We are rotten," he explained. "We were so bad, it was so bad... I'm in disbelief at what I've just witnessed."



The former Blues defender also expressed his concerns for manager Xabi Alonso amid a run of one win in five across all competitions.

A handful of fans were also heard chanting 'You don't know what you're doing!' to the Spaniard once Malo Gusto came on in the second half.



"That was a worrying performance, worrying. If that carries on, Alonso won't keep his job, I'm telling you that for nothing," Cundy added.

"You can't do what you did against Sunderland (1-0 loss), you can't do what you did against Leeds today and lose those two games."



"We were disgusting today, absolutely disgusting," Cundy continued. "I'm still trying to find the words... as every minute ticked by, we got worse, and Leeds got better."

Chelsea have dropped to eighth in the Premier League after losing for the fifth time this season, and Cundy thinks the next few months look bleak.

"It's almost disbelief at how bad we were, seriously, I'm not even joking. I'm worried... I'm worried about how this season is going to go," he said.

3 Cundy looked a broken man on the GameDay Phone-In and raised his concerns over how Chelsea will fare this season Credit: talkSPORT



3 He also warned Alonso that he could face the sack if their dismal run of form continues across the next few weeks Credit: Getty

"Genuinely now, I'm worried... I am worried about what this season looks like for us.

"I'm being completely honest here, I don't know whether we're going to finish... we look like bottom half fodder, easily bottom half fodder."

Later in the show, Cundy stated that Chelsea would have lost against Championship opposition with a similar performance.



"I actually think Lincoln could've beaten us today… anyone could've beaten us, we were that bad," Cundy said.

"I'm really struggling to work out how we could've been that bad."

Leeds also poked fun at Cundy on social media by giving him a taste of his own medicine with his famous 'Has anyone seen?' joke.

Alonso: Chelsea in a 'fragile moment'

Speaking to talkSPORT afterwards, Alonso detailed how Chelsea, who saw Moises Caicedo go off injured in the first half, struggle to bounce back from adversity.

"It was a tough one, a tough game, tough result to deal with," Alonso said. "My feeling is that we are in a fragile moment, when we get a setback, we are not able to recover quick enough to this competitive level required against a team as Leeds.



"The first half an hour we were good, we conceded the 1-1, and after that, the substitution, we lost total momentum. Leeds started believing more than us and we were not able to turn it our way."

Alonso added: "Leeds have their qualities and they do good. There are more reasons than just the physicality of the duels.

"I think that we could have done better, even that we lost a little bit of confidence to do the right things, how to keep the ball, how to be able to go through this first pressure of Leeds.

"The first half an hour we were able to play much more on the half, but the rest of the game we didn't progress that well."

Sports.title: ‘Where’s the fight?’ – Ian Holloway restrained by stewards as Swindon fans fume before slamming his players
Sports.content:
‘Where’s the fight?’ – Ian Holloway restrained by stewards as Swindon fans fume before slamming his players

Swindon Town boss Ian Holloway was 'bitterly disappointed' in his players following a 2-0 loss to Newport County.

Newport midfielder Aaron Lewis' first-half double condemned the Robins to a tenth loss in their last 15 fixtures.

2 Holloway did not hold back in his assessment following Swindon's latest defeat Credit: Getty

And Swindon supporters were not afraid to vent their frustrations at Holloway, with a clip of the frosty exchange shared on social media.

Ian Holloway clashes with Swindon fans

As Holloway approached the fans, he removed his cap and began walking towards the tunnel, but stopped in his tracks to bite back at one supporter.

The Robins boss then had to be led away by security.

An 'absolutely fuming' Holloway later ripped into his own troops in his post-match interview.

What did Ian Holloway say in his post-match interview?

"They've (Newport) improved, they put you under pressure and get balls in your box," Holloway said.

"Two of the softest goals I've ever seen in my life, absolutely killed us.

"And it's been coming. It looked like they didn't care. The rest of it was a waste of time. We ended up creating chances, but anyone can do that when you're 2-0 down.

"Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.

"It's not very nice in there."

Holloway continued: "You need to win your header, and you need to win the knockdown, get your foot through it.

2 Holloway has been in charge at Swindon since October 2024 Credit: Rex

"They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

"Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us."

It is not the first time Holloway has strongly criticised his own players, having described some as 'imposters' during pre-season.

When is Swindon next in action?

The loss to Newport leaves Swindon in 17th on 19 points, six clear of the relegation zone in League Two.

However, the Robins remain only four points away from the play-off positions in the fourth tier.

Swindon will look to avoid a third consecutive defeat in the league next Saturday when they host promotion hopefuls Chesterfield.

Sports.title: Frustrated Cole Palmer shares frosty exchange with Joao Pedro after upsetting Chelsea staff member before walking off down the tunnel after 4-1 drubbing by Leeds
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I said, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

Sports.title: Arsenal face nervous wait with David Raya set for scan after being forced off against Newcastle... as club legend Ian Wright admits he's 'petrified' of losing the keeper
Sports.content:
Arsenal will be keeping everything crossed ahead of goalkeeper David Raya undergoing tests on what appeared to be a shoulder or arm injury sustained against Newcastle. The Gunners' No1 went off in the second half in the 2-2 draw at St James' Park, supporting his arm or shoulder before he was replaced by back-up Kepa Arrizabalaga. It leaves everyone associated with Arsenal nervous, as they face potentially a sustained period of time without a key part of their impressive defence. Raya appeared to pick up the injury by running into Newcastle's Will Osula after claiming the ball from a cross. As he attempted to run forward to start an attack, he collided with the striker and hit the ground in pain. After a brief period of treatment on the field, he was substituted, supporting his arm, and replaced in the game. "I'm petrified!" Ian Wright and Jamie Redknapp on why David Raya coming off injured vs Newcastle is a massive worry for Arsenal 🧤 pic.twitter.com/F5uAgjFdp0 — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 21, 2026 Arsenal face a nervy wait to find out the extent of David Raya's injury picked up against Newcastle on Saturday Manager Mikel Arteta has been left sweating at the idea of being without his No1 for a busy Christmas period. 'Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news,' Arteta said: 'He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don't know. 'It was a knock, I don't know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment. We have to wait and see tomorrow. 'We know how important David is for us. Tomorrow we will have more news.' The Gunners will play nine more games before the end of the year as they look to push forward in both the league and Champions League. That challenge has just got harder, though, and Arsenal fan and former forward Ian Wright has expressed his concern. 'That's a massive worry,' he said on Sky Sports. 'I don't want to say I'm petrified simply because Kepa is in goal, he's the guy who has got to try and keep the goals out for us now. 'But yeah, that is a massive blow. Someone like him, Declan Rice, Gabriel, it is very tough to replace those guys.' Arsenal are next in action against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday, before a crunch clash with Manchester City in the Premier League next Sunday.

Sports.title: Shaking fists, smacking knees, heart-rate checks and a lot of Diet Coke - TWO HOURS in a hotel with rugby's most divisive figure but Rassie's watchalong echoed largely to the sound of... silence
Sports.content:
Shaking fists, smacking knees, heart-rate checks and a lot of Diet Coke - TWO HOURS in a hotel with rugby's most divisive figure but Rassie's watchalong echoed largely to the sound of... silence

It’s easier to chat when we’re winning. So says Rassie Erasmus as we tune into his livestream of South Africa’s clash with Ireland.

After England’s tanking of the All Blacks, the Springboks only needed a bonus point to make the Nations Championship final, but Rassie admits the best thing was to try and win the match.

Unfortunately for him, that’s not how it ends. And a bonus point is all they come away with after Jesse Kriel’s knock-on brought the match to an end.

A disgusted Erasmus shakes his fists in frustration, almost knocking his Diet Coke onto the laptop in front of him.

Rassie Erasmus, banned for six games by World Rugby, is a picture of calm in his Dublin hotel as he launches a watchalong for Ireland's clash with South Africa

In fairness he does manage to share a smile with what looks like a member of the hotel staff, who has been keeping the South Africa coach in ice for his drink as the previous two hours unfolded.

He shakes his head to whatever the camera operator asked, and removes the ear buds. If we’re going to hear from Rassie, we’re going to have to wait along with everyone else.

He closes the laptop, puts on some lip balm in between checking his wrist.

‘I’ll show you my heart-rate after,’ he had half-promised beforehand.

If it was his heart rate he was checking, he wasn’t going to share the results with his viewers after this defeat. We got a few words beforehand and a few upbeat lines at half-time. But apart from that, all picture, no sound.

When 20 minutes in, Robert Baloucoune dotted down for his second try, Erasmus slumped back a bit, with an almost resigned look on his face.

A block appeared across the screen, declaring ‘SOUND WILL REMAIN OFF UNTIL RASSIE WANTS TO SPEAK’.

All did not go to plan, not least for those who signed up in the hope of a running commentary from the South Africa coach.

Ear buds in, the match started with Erasmus’s hand over mouth as he talked into his laptop or whatever devices he had lying around the table.

South African fans show their loyalty outside Aviva Stadium ahead of the clash with Ireland

Lipreaders would be disappointed.

Soon after Baloucoune opened Ireland’s account, a comment from Philip in Buckingham spoke for us all: ‘Please say something.’

Erasmus may have kept schtum, but his body language could not keep any secrets.

The award of an early penalty sparked his first bout of applause. His Boks cap spent a few moments on backwards, was then straightened, then back on and off again.

A shake of the head greeted a contentious penalty to Ireland, the laptop on the table quivering after Ireland were given a scrum penalty on 26 minutes before moving his head in disgust.

An Irish knock-on from a Sam Prendergast cross-kick was greeted with a smack to his knee and a shout.

It was a barren enough scene in front of the camera. An empty hotel conference room, with Rassie watching Virgin’s coverage on a screen above the camera position.

He stood for the South Africa national anthem, though the camera hilariously had to adjust to get the head of his tall frame back into shot.

Unsurprisingly, the comments on the stream suggested almost 100 per cent support for Rassie’s Boks.

South Africa outside centre Jesse Kriel cuts a frustrated figure following the 20-17 defeat

From Antwerp to Austria, Bettystown to Botswana over 150,000 had signed up by the time Rassie appeared about ten minutes before kick-off.

The livestream had gripped the rugby world since Erasmus announced it on Thursday with a social media post, intriguingly adding it was for adults only.

Soccer Saturday never needed an 18+ tag.

Sports watchalongs are not new – how many times have viewers had to answer ‘yes, we are watching four people watching lots of football matches now go away’ as people questioned their viewing habits in the early years of Jeff Stelling’s Sky show?

But WatchwithRassie promised to elevate it to a whole-new level – his initial social media message stated that he could ‘sit and moan or make the best of it’…. and while we got no audible moans, only he can decide whether the stream did indeed result in him making the best of it.

The ‘18+’ set minds racing. Rugby is a physical game – and nobody likes the on-pitch battle as much as South Africa and their bomb squads – but still … according to the Irish Film Classification Office, this is what you can expect from programmes certified over 18s: ‘In addition to strong language, sexual content, violence, horror and harmful behaviour, films classified as 18 can contain material and themes that can have a strong impact on viewers.’

Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast celebrates with two-try hero Robert Baloucoune

Dan Sheehan and Marco van Staden get yellow cards for a croc roll and dangerous clear-out

We could confidently rule out sexual content; Erasmus himself explicitly banned bad language so that just left violence, horror and harmful behaviour.

The mind wandered to the opening scene of Goodfellas, a classic from the 18+ certificate category.

You’d imagine that great lost Italian back-row of Liotta, Pesci and de Niro would not have waited for the Feds to refer the murder of Billy Batts to the video referee.

Though if it had been a rugby ‘incident’ some pundits would argue the trio’s greatest offence was not painting a positive enough picture of the ‘infringement’.

Perhaps the most contentious ’rugby incident of yesterday’s game came in the 72nd minute when Dan Sheehan and Marco van Staden both picked up yellow cards and South Africa were eventually awarded a crucial penalty after some lengthy discussions.

When the incident happened, Erasmus was nowhere to be seen and eventually returned, fixing his belt.

Even Springbok managers need their comfort breaks. All that Diet Coke presumably had to go somewhere.

Sports.title: Now the Daily Mail bans F1: We boycott coverage after our reporter is barred from races - as decision is branded 'an abuse of power'
Sports.content:
The Daily Mail will boycott Formula One after motor racing correspondent Jonathan McEvoy was handed a draconian ban for the rest of the season by the sport’s governing body.

There will be no reporting on races or press conferences for the final three races of the 2026 season in the wake of the remarkable decision to revoke our reporter’s accreditation over an article criticising Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc.

McEvoy labelled the Monegasque racer a ‘sneaky little b*****d’ for his role in a contentious, opening lap collision with Scuderia teammate, Britain’s seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, at last month’s Mexican Grand Prix. The incident cost Ferrari a chance of a race victory.

McEvoy, who has covered nearly 400 races across 21 years of working for the Daily Mail, went on to reveal details of a tense post-race debrief between the drivers and Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur.

The FIA’s decision to withdraw McEvoy’s accreditation has been condemned by news industry leaders. Top drivers, past and present, as well as a host of other leading figures in the sport, have also offered their private support.

Leclerc suggested McEvoy was doing his 'job' in his column - and confirmed that his report of 'tension' in post-race talks with Vasseur and Hamilton was correct.

'I was quite surprised by the choice of words when I saw the article. Then on the sanction itself, obviously,' Leclerc said. 'I've got absolutely nothing to do with it, and I don't have much to say about it.

Jonathan McEvoy has been handed a draconian ban for the rest of the season by the sport’s governing body

'As a Formula 1 driver, I think we are used to this kind of criticism in general and to critics, and it's definitely the job of journalists to kind of ask the bad questions and do some of the tough headlines sometimes. But I was surprised with the choice of words.'

Andrew Moger, chief executive of the News Media Coalition (NMC), called on the FIA to ‘reinstate McEvoy so he can continue to do his professional best and rejoin the dedicated group of experienced journalists who serve F1, fans and the business of motor racing through their independent reporting including opinion-forming insights’.

The NMC champions journalist access to major organised news and sports events around the world and Moger said the McEvoy case was alarming.

‘Like it or not, freedom of expression such as the ability to share viewpoints, and press freedom, remain vital to informed societies, debate and conversation - including about the behaviour of F1 drivers and evidently the sensitivity of teams’.

The Society of Editors also threw its support behind the Daily Mail, calling on the FIA to reverse its decision with immediate effect.

Chief executive Dawn Alford said: ’The FIA was wrong to withdraw Jonathan McEvoy’s accreditation. He has covered Formula One for more than 20 years. The point of an opinion column is to give readers the considered view of someone who knows the sport. He should be free to write what he thinks, even when that makes for uncomfortable reading in the paddock.

’Accreditation gives journalists the access they need to do their jobs. Using it to punish a correspondent for what he writes is an abuse of that power. It sets a precedent that should concern every journalist covering Formula One and anyone who cares about independent sports reporting.

’Formula One fans want to know what is really going on in the sport. They rely on experienced reporters to ask awkward questions and tell them plainly what they make of the answers. That coverage suffers if journalists have to think about whether their next column might cost them their pass.

‘The FIA should reverse this decision immediately and reinstate Jonathan McEvoy’s accreditation in time for the next race.’

The Daily Telegraph described the ban as ‘the latest example of the FIA’s thin-skinned and overzealous policing of the media’.

In a stinging rebuke, McEvoy suggested Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur may be behind the decision

McEvoy, pictured with George Russell, has covered nearly 400 races in 21 years working for the Daily Mail

On Thursday, FIA general manager Alberto Villarreal wrote to McEvoy to inform him of the impending ban. The letter stated: ’The FIA considers that your article falls short of the standards of professionalism expected of media representatives accredited to cover the FIA Formula One World Championship.

‘Accordingly, the FIA has decided to exercise its discretion under the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship Accreditation Guidelines to withdraw your media accreditation for the remainder of the 2026 season, with immediate effect.’

The decision was labelled as ‘crazy’ by former F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone, who added: ’I don’t know why the FIA would ever do that.

’Apart from the fact I like Jon, he is doing a fantastic job.

‘I look forward to reading what he’s writing. I don’t have to, it’s my choice to do that. I think it’s completely mad.’

Chris Dean, the Daily Mail’s head of sport, echoed those feelings in a strongly worded statement on Thursday.

He said: ’This is an unprecedented and outrageous attack on the freedom of the Press.

’We are in dangerous territory when the FIA react in such a heavy-handed way to some mild and fair criticism of one driver.

’Jonathan McEvoy is a fearless and first-rate journalist who takes readers behind the curtain of F1’s shiny exterior. The FIA should reinstate his accreditation immediately.'

The FIA’s latest attack on press freedom comes after an incident at the Japanese Grand Prix in March involving Max Verstappen and the Guardian journalist Giles Richards.

The Dutchman refused to participate in a press conference until the reporter had left the room.

It came after the final race of the 2025 season in Abu Dhabi, when Richards quizzed Verstappen on whether he regretted his driving after a collision with title rival George Russell in an earlier race.

The incident cost Verstappen nine points and he went on to lose out in his quest for a fifth consecutive title to Lando Norris by two points.

Sports.title: Wales fall short of another landmark result against Australia, but disappointment at the near miss is a measure of their recent progress, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
Wales fall short of another landmark result against Australia, but disappointment at the near miss is a measure of their recent progress, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

There was a giant sign over Cardiff bus station on Saturday evening that carried a warning for Australia: ‘The Dragon Has Awoken'. Turns out a wounded wallaby is more resistant to fire than a kiwi.

If last weekend’s win over the All Blacks supplied the greatest afternoon in the history of Welsh rugby, then this eight-try thriller was the dip that followed the highest of highs.

But there was no shame in defeat. No need for inquests and dark nights of the soul. Not in the slightest. Against a nation that had run up three straight wins over Wales, Steve Tandy’s team could measure their recent progress with a performance that carried them within a whisker of another landmark result.

For a nine-minute period in the second half, they even led, built on two tries from Dewi Lake, a better one from Blair Murray and more of those defensive heroics that we saw a week ago.

But the Southern Hemisphere breeds big boys, which includes this crop of Australians, who have been desperately poor this autumn. They had a point to prove about their mettle and just about succeeded.

To the Welsh, some regret will trace to the first half. Against New Zealand, they were a try ahead inside two minutes; here, they were a man down when Max Llewellyn was shown a yellow for going high on Tom Wright.

Wales fell short of backing up their win over New Zealand by suffering defeat to Australia

The hosts regularly went deep into Australia territory without capitalising and were then hit by sucker punches

Wales can still could measure their recent progress with a performance that carried them within a whisker of another landmark result

What followed was a series of surges with 14-men that set a theme for going deep into Australian territory without capitalising. They had countless chances.

Naturally, the sucker punches weren’t long in coming. First, tight-head Taniela Tupou broke the line for 5-0, the try unconverted, and then Brandon Paenga-Amos pushed through on the drive for the second. Ryan Lonergan added the two.

Wales, twice held up on the line in the first half, were paying for not matching slick moves with clinical finishing but they finally found a way with the last attack of the period.

In keeping with the growth in Welsh confidence, Sam Costelow could have kicked for an easy three but opted for position. This time Lake led the drive and crossed near the corner. After Costelow kicked the extras, Australia’s advantage was down to five. That Welsh lineout has burned hot in autumn.

Max Jorgensen kicked off the second half with a neat try, converted by Lonergan for 19-7, but the Welsh response was strong. Lake initiated the fightback by thundering over for his second of the match, before the lead was secured by the try of the night when Rees-Zammit destroyed Harry Potter and combined with Josh Adams to open a road for Blair Murray. Costelow kicked Wales into a two-point lead.

Excellent tackles by Eddie James and Archie Griffin preserved the advantage for the briefest of moments, echoing the defensive effort against the All Blacks, but Len Ikitau picked a nice line for the try. Carter Gordon kicked the Wallabies five ahead. A Gordon penalty then gave them daylight, but Ryan Elias bundled over to make it tight again. Not tight enough, it transpired, but disappointment at a near miss is a luxury Wales have had in recent years.

Sports.title: England dominated every area in complete performance: The lineout was formidable and the attack purred as Lewis Moody staring down the haka set tone for crushing win over New Zealand, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
England dominated every area in complete performance: The lineout was formidable and the attack purred as Lewis Moody staring down the haka set tone for crushing win over New Zealand, writes NIK SIMON

From the moment Maro Itoje embraced Lewis Moody’s and escorted him into the middle of the Twickenham pitch, everyone knew it would take something formidable to break England’s resistance.

Moody, or Mad Dog as he was known when he won the 2003 World Cup, anchored England’s players as they walked into a V formation against the All Blacks’ haka. It was a moment of rugby history, sending chills down every spine in the stadium.

Moody is battling motor neurone disease and his remarkable, unbreakable spirit pumped through English veins. His presence set the tone as England secured their first back-to-back wins over the All Blacks since – rather fittingly – 2003.

England dominated every area but the lineout was particularly formidable. It is Steve Borthwick’s specialist subject and on days like this, with Jamie George at hooker, their set-piece drills look like the best in the world. They move quickly across the floor, with jumpers soaring like eagles, firing into the maul like a pumping assembly of pistons.

Their attack purred. Thanks to Lee Blackett, England’s set-piece strike play was unstoppable. The 10-12 axis between Fin Smith and Seb Atkinson cut through like an angle grinder. There were razor-sharp running lines and an industrious ability to find space faster than the labouring All Black defence. And at the grand old age of 33, when many had written him off, Henry Slade is again showing the best version of himself in an England shirt.

Slade scored after just five minutes and Jack van Poortvliet followed suit. This was the complete performance. There was a time when it felt like the entire All Black team could be cast as 007. They had an aura that made you think they would never die. Here, they were uncloaked. Ben Earl ran through Cameron Roigard like a wet paper bag to score the try that handed England a 19-0 lead after 36 minutes. James Bond? These Kiwis would not stand a chance against Robert Pattinson.

Lewis Moody (England, fourth right) took to the field before England's win over New Zealand and fronted the haka response

England's attack purred as they dominated every area - with the lineout particularly formidable

‘The most important thing is how you start the game against New Zealand,’ said England skipper Maro Itoje. ‘Teams have done different things against the haka, different formations.

‘Having Lewis and his family gave us an extra lift. The idea was floated about him potentially joining us for the haka and our senior guys gave overwhelming support.

‘I remember watching England play, particularly around 2011, and I remember his heroic performances for England, throwing his body around. The way he played was inspirational. He was one of the guys I looked up to as a young boy. To be able to welcome him onto the field was a memory that will live with me for the rest of my life.’

On Friday night, Moody and his 2003 teammates enjoyed a glamorous reunion at the Dorchester on Park Lane. Everyone from Sir Clive Woodward to Jonny Wilkinson were there. At one point, Mike and Zara Tindall even got on the microphone for a singalong.

The ‘03 lot are a patriotic bunch but even they could not reach a consensus about how Borthwick’s team would fare against the Kiwis. England had beaten Fiji, Argentina, Australia and Japan but, on paper, none of those teams were in the same division as the All Blacks.

This was the litmus test of the Class of 26’s progress and they excelled from the start. They suffocated the Kiwi attack, tackling in packs, forcing the most basic of handling errors from Damian McKenzie, Will Jordan and Jordie Barrett. The All Blacks’ world famous attack mustered just two linebreaks across 80 minutes. Credit there must go to defence coach Richard Wigglesworth.

England enjoyed 74 per cent of the territory. The Kiwis were turned over, lacked linespeed and were void of accuracy. It was so bad that by the end of the night, coach Dave Rennie was being asked if he feared for his job.

‘We were miles off,’ said Rennie. ‘We were well short. If you look at the stats, we were well beaten in almost every number. I’m not going to hide from he fact we weren’t good enough and I’m a big part of that. Against Wales, the only thing we lacked was our finish. Last week I said that we let the country down but we were way worse tonight. We need to work out why.’

Ben Earl made 20 carries in the first half - by full-time, he had beaten eight defenders and made 138 metres

The All Blacks have averaged more than 250 running metres per half under Rennie. In the first half here at Twickenham, they managed just 74. In contrast, Earl made 20 carries alone in the first half. By full-time, he had beaten eight defenders and made 138m single-handedly. He compensated for the absence of England’s front-line wingers, with Tommy Freeman pulling out shortly before kick-off with a thigh injury.

Cadan Murley joined Will Joseph on the wing. Murley delivered one of his best England performances and Joseph showcased the depth that is quietly building for next year’s World Cup.

England’s lineout clinic continued into the second half. Alex Coles stole Codie Taylor’s throw and Ollie Chessum scored down the left flank.

After losing to Wales last week, there were fears of a New Zealand backlash. ‘Born to Dare,’ read the All Black  outside Twickenham train station. Beauden Barrett’s breakaway try in the 52nd minute oozed class but it was a standalone moment.

Throughout the second half, Borthwick unloaded his smash and bash bench. Ellis Genge, George Martin and Greg Fisilau injected a level of power that the All Blacks could not live with.

Fin Smith limped off with cramp but Marcus Smith picked up the baton. He kicked penalties and sent Atkinson over to score. He ran his thumb across his throat in celebration as England turned the show into a blood opera.

Second to Moody’s appearance, the late sight of Chessum dump tackling Scott Barrett into the Twickenham turf summed up the performance. The All Blacks were well and truly buried.

Sports.title: New system, same problems: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in defeat despite tactical switch... but Coventry are up to 13th
Sports.content:
New system, same problems: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in defeat despite tactical switch... but Coventry are up to 13th

Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.

There were, however, some noticeable improvements. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent plan for creating chances.

But the same problem that plagued his predecessor Pierre Sage persisted: Palace cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue to ship sloppy goals.

Frank will be able to address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a new manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace

His in-game management worked to a degree as Palace conceded two goals and defended frantically in the first half before looking much more solid and organised in the second period before finally conceding the decisive goal in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel issues in January but they currently sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next Sunday.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

New boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank said. ‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

‘That was the big positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’

Defensively, this was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide — including Disasi, who was miles out of position — allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s first assignment.
