World.title: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate".

He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsula it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use.

"There are facts, not just the words of Putin. We can see," he said.

The Ukrainian president pointed to images online of tanks and other Russian military hardware using the route from Russia into occupied Crimea as a supply line and for logistics.

"If Putin used the internet, he could see that."

The Ukrainian president added that Russia had carried out attacks with missiles and drones on bridges in Ukraine.

This week's combined missile-and-drone strikes by Ukrainian forces destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge, collapsing part of it together with one of the two support arches into the sea and rendering the structure unusable for road traffic.

Russian attacks on Ukraine continued on Friday evening and overnight: a seven-year-old boy was killed in missile and drone strikes on Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih in the central Dnipropetrovsk region. Local officials say he had been in a playground at the time.

A 20-year-old female medic was also killed. A local official added that when rescuers rushed to the scene, the same site was targeted again with jet powered drones. Another 58 people were injured in the city.

Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS said 11 people were also injured in the north-eastern Kharkiv region, and one person in Rivne, in the north-west.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

World.title: Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
World.content:
A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say.

The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.

"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."

Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used, based on preliminary information, and there was "no threat" to the territory's supplies.

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.

Finland's coast guard said it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.

This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials said.

Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".

A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad's governor wrote on Telegram, adding: "The crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and plans to continue on its way."

The Finnish Border Guard later said the crew had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was now already en route to Russia. The Russian rescue vessel had remained at the location of the stricken ship.

It added that no environmental damage had been detected and that there was no danger to maritime traffic or people.

Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.

World.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
World.content:
Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock and have been suspended for the night, after running more than a day over time, as countries have been unable to agree on a new global climate deal.

The EU and Pacific island nations are amongst a group pushing back against the latest draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels.

A second sticking point involves a push from the Africa Group to get commitments on more money for adaptation - but the EU has previously said it would not support this.

Negotiating teams due to fly out on Sunday morning are now moving their flights to Monday in a sign that a deal is not yet in sight.

If countries cannot reach consensus - which is required by the UN's climate talks process - the negotiations could be suspended.

In that case the summit would end with no deal and be reconvened next year. This has only happened once before since countries started holding COP climate meetings in 1995.

World.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
World.content:
A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.

Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.

Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added.

Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition.

Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House.

Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile.

World.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
World.content:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue.

The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks.

It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US. The agency did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

When asked about the breach in a Fox News interview on Saturday, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the hack. "I will say that it's not good. I don't like that," he said.

"But maybe we'll learn things that we would've never learned otherwise," Trump added.

This apparent breach of FBI database comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyber-attacks, but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers.

White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week, with Trump saying he was not good enough.

Dan Lorhmann, a former analyst for the National Security Agency (NSA), told the BBC News Channel that the NCIC's data included "critical information relating to nationwide criminal activity" and needed to be protected.

He added that while US security agencies including the FBI have "an amazing ability" to keep such information safe" and are "globally respected", the level of cyber-attacks is rising globally.

"There's a lot of different reasons why that's happening but I do have faith in our experts in government," Lorhmann said.

In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed it had stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people.

After that hack, one former FBI agent told the BBC he feared for the safety of current employees, whose personal information could soon become available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.

In a separate development, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture (USDA).

Employees were informed on Thursday that its farm payment system had been targeted, NBC said.

The USDA has not publicly commented on the issue.

World.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
World.content:
Denmark has accused Russian intelligence services of plotting to assassinate a Ukrainian-American near Copenhagen, saying they had "planned" and "initiated" the attempt.

Denmark's security and intelligence agency (PET) said it had stopped individuals who were intending to kill the person, named by Danish media as rapper Kyivstoner, at a concert in September. Two people were charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service, and pleaded not guilty.

Denmark's foreign minister said Russia's defence attachÃ© will now be expelled.

Russia's embassy in Denmark called the allegations "unsubstantiated" and said Copenhagen failed to provide evidence of Moscow's involvement.

In a statement, the embassy claimed a "Danish model" had emerged, which it described as a "Russian trace" allegedly being discovered and "exploited for a propaganda spectacle". It accused Denmark of "provocations" intending to "frighten the Danish population in order to justify... a prolonged confrontation with Russia".

Russian state media cite the foreign ministry in Moscow as saying it will respond to the expulsion of its official "accordingly".

In a statement on Saturday, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said: "I strongly condemn the assassination attempt against a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, orchestrated by Russian intelligence services.

"This was an attack on EU soil. And it is unacceptable," she said, adding that "Russia's hybrid threats are becoming less and less hybrid, and more and more real."

The rapper's real name is Albert Vasiliev.

PET said the individuals who allegedly tried to assassinate him were associated with a banned Danish gang named Loyal to Familia. The group is "known for extensive, serious and violent criminal activity", according to the agency.

PET, which worked with police on the case, said three individuals were stopped while travelling by car near the music venue where Kyivstoner was set to perform on 25 September.

Firearms and knives were found in the vehicle, PET said.

Since then, two people linked to the case have been charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

Both individuals pleaded not guilty to the charges, local media reported.

In July, Russia's FSB security service accused Vasiliev and the Ukrainian authorities of organising a "terrorist attack" on military facilities and personnel in Russia. The rapper denied this allegation on social media.

In a statement on Friday, Danish Foreign Minister Lars LÃ¸kke Rasmussen said the alleged assassination attempt was Russian "intimidation" and an attempt to make Denmark "waver" in its support for Ukraine.

Russia's defence attachÃ© must leave the country within seven days, Rasmussen said.

He also said Denmark wants the EU to restrict the ability of Russians to travel throughout Europe, saying even though Copenhagen was already very reluctant to issue visas, Russians could still get a Schengen visa in another country and travel to Denmark.

Copenhagen wants these visas to apply only in the country that has issued them, he added.

World.title: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
World.content:
Rinderknecht was found guilty of lighting a fire on 1 January last year which burned undetected deep in root systems before flaring back up six days later.

One of the charges was for starting the original brush fire, while the other centred on the damage caused when it reignited into a catastrophic blaze.

"We were determined to hold him accountable, and today's guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended," said Bill Essayli, who leads the US Attorney's Office for the Central District of California.

Rinderknecht is a Los Angeles resident and former ride-share delivery driver.

Defence attorney Steve Haney had argued at trial that prosecutors lacked sufficient physical evidence or records to prove their case.

Lawyers for the defendant said they were "disappointed" by the verdict but respected the jury's decision.

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, who was widely criticised for her handling of the fires, said in a statement that "no verdict can bring back the lives lost or erase the pain families have endured".

"So many are still struggling to rebuild," she said. "For those still displaced, the devastation remains a daily reality."

Prosecutors had argued that Rinderknecht was driven by revenge, anger and loneliness because he had nowhere to go for the holiday.

They cited geolocation data from his iPhone, security camera footage that showed his car's location and witness testimony from passengers.

They alleged that Rinderknecht had a "deeply entrenched belief that the wealthy were destroying the world" and in turn purposely started the blaze in the affluent neighbourhood.

The fire was one of several that ignited back-to-back across the LA region in January, which in total left 31 people dead and destroyed 16,000 structures.

World.title: Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
World.content:
A framed lock of hair from America's first president, George Washington, has been sold at auction for $4,000 (Â£3,058).

The hair once belonged to John Gadsby, who entertained Washington in 1799 just before the latter's death the same year, and was later obtained by a collector called John K Lattimer from a descendent of Gadsby's, according to Richmond Auctions, which sold the item.

Its new owner has not been named.

Saturday's sale is not the most expensive for Washington hair at auction. Three strands thought to have been removed from him close to or after his death stored in a locket sold for nearly $40,000 in 2021.

Gadsby, a resident of what in 1799 was the town of Alexandria in Virginia, entertained Washington for dinner shortly before his death later that year, according to a testament given in 1928 by Gadsby's granddaughter, Julia Ten Eyck McBlair, and which was posted on the Richmond Auctions website.

McBlair stated that her grandfather came into possession of Washington's hair "in view of the friendship and association with his last days" and had it framed and hung "under General Washington's portrait in our home in Washington City, there I have seen it all my life".

Gadsby hosted Washington's two birthday celebrations in 1798 and 1799, Richmond Auctions states.

Washington led American forces to victory against the British in the War of Independence and helped draft the US Constitution before becoming the country's first president in 1788. He stepped down in 1797 after serving two terms.

Several locks of Washington's hair have been preserved, including at least 50 examples that are in a collection at his former residence, Mount Vernon, which is now a museum.

"Public displays of hair from friends or loved ones peaked in the 19th century, but had long been popular among affluent families like the Washingtons," a blog on the Mount Vernon website states.

As well as lockets of his hair, other items associated with Washington have also done well at auction.

In July, a signed letter by Washington from 1776, in which he asks for soldiers for the Continental Army to fight the British, sold for $109,800.

World.title: Naija Farmed Fish campaign moves to bring locally raised catfish to more Nigerian tables
World.content:
Nigeria’s love for fish is well established. The next opportunity is to get more Nigerians eating fish produced locally. A new consumer campaign, Naija Farmed Fish, is setting out to do just that, bringing Nigerian farm-raised catfish closer to consumers through a fresh approach to food, culture and everyday consumption.

Featuring the product brand Naija Catfish and the campaign platform “It’s Catfish O’Clock,”the initiative aims to make locally farm-raised catfish an appealing, accessible and more frequent choice for Nigerian households while highlighting the economic opportunities within the country’s aquaculture industry.

Fish is a familiar feature of Nigerian cuisine, from pepper soup and grilled catfish to everyday stews and family meals. Yet the opportunity extends beyond what is already on the menu. Stronger consumer demand for locally farmed fish can help create markets for producers, support businesses across the supply chain, and contribute to Nigeria’s domestic food production ambitions.

According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Nigeria consumes approximately 3.6 million metric tonnes of fish annually, while domestic production is estimated at 1.2–1.4 million metric tonnes. The gap points to the scale of the opportunity to strengthen local production and expand the market for Nigerian fish. Nigeria is also recognised as the world’s largest producer of African catfish, giving the country an important foundation on which to build.

However, expanding production is only part of the equation. Farmers also need consumers who recognise the value of their products, choose them regularly and create dependable demand. Naija Farmed Fish seeks to help close that gap by bringing farm-raised catfish closer to consumers through education, food experiences and engaging communications.

Speaking ahead of the campaign, Sofolabi Sofela, an aquaculture specialist with extensive experience in fish farming and industry development, said: “Growing Nigeria’s aquaculture industry is not just about producing more fish; it is also about getting more people to choose the fish our farmers produce. Nigerian farm-raised catfish is part of our food culture, and there is an opportunity to make it even more relevant to everyday meals. By encouraging consumers to discover, enjoy and choose locally farmed fish more often, we can help create stronger markets and opportunities for businesses throughout the value chain.”

The campaign will engage consumers across Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan, Enugu and Port Harcourt, using public relations, media engagement, consumer education, culinary storytelling and experiential activations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Through “It’s Catfish O’Clock,” consumers will be encouraged to think of catfish beyond traditional occasions and discover new ways to enjoy it, whether at home, with friends, at a family gathering or simply when it is time for a satisfying meal.

The campaign will also address consumer questions about farm-raised fish, including nutrition, handling and preparation, while celebrating the people behind the industry: farmers, feed producers, processors, distributors, traders, food vendors and restaurants.

Recent research and interventions within Nigeria’s catfish value chain have demonstrated the potential of improved farm management, training and data-led practices to strengthen productivity and efficiency. Yet production gains are most sustainable when matched by viable markets and growing consumer demand. Nigerian consumers should expect to see quality and affordable catfish on the market as farmers continue to adopt improved management techniques and quality soy-based feeds.

As Nigeria seeks to strengthen domestic food production and build more resilient agricultural value chains, Naija Farmed Fish aims to make consumer choice part of the solution. Ultimately, the ambition is to make locally farm-raised catfish not simply available, but actively sought after, to connect the work of Nigerian fish farmers with the choices consumers make every day.

ABOUT NAIJA FARMED FISH

Naija Farmed Fish is a consumer-focused initiative promoting awareness, appreciation and consumption of Nigerian farm-raised fish, particularly catfish. Through consumer education, food experiences, communications and engagement, the initiative seeks to celebrate locally farmed fish, inspire new consumption occasions and strengthen demand for Nigerian aquaculture products.

ABOUT NAIJA CATFISH

Naija Catfish is the product brand under Naija Farmed Fish, celebrating the appeal, taste and versatility of Nigerian farm-raised catfish and encouraging consumers to enjoy it across a wider range of occasions.

World.title: Tinubu campaigns in Ibadan, says Nigeria on path to prosperity
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu, on Saturday in Ibadan, said the sacrifices Nigerians had made during a period of difficult economic reforms would soon give way to greater prosperity.

The president spoke at Samuel Ladoke Akintola Airport, where traditional rulers and political leaders from the South-west received him ahead of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the historic Mapo Hall.

Addressing the monarchs, led by the Olubadan of Ibadan, Oba Rasheed Ladoja, Arusa 1, the president thanked them for their support and prayers for the nation.

He urged them to “stay the course for the sake of progress and prosperity of our country, for you, for your children and great-great-grandchildren. Our children will benefit from what we are doing.”

He told the monarchs that one indicator of greater things to come in Oyo State was the recent agreement signed with the world’s largest bus manufacturer, Yutong China, to reopen the old Leyland Automobile Bus Assembly plant for vehicle assembly, which will stimulate economic activity in the state.

The Olubadan commended the President for his administration’s willingness to tackle issues previously considered difficult to address, including establishing state police.

He said Mr Tinubu’s performance in office, particularly in infrastructure development, has become the major selling point for other candidates seeking election on the party’s platform.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He specifically mentioned the Ibadan-Ife, Ibadan-Abeokuta and other road projects, saying the ongoing interventions had significantly reduced travel time and improved connectivity across the state.

He expressed optimism that the president would consolidate his achievements if given another term.

He said the traditional institution is also interested in securing a constitutional role, urging the president to give the matter serious consideration.

At the rally, President Tinubu called for a moment of silence in memory of those who died in the boat accident in Bayelsa State.

He said Vice-President Kashim Shettima would visit the state to commiserate with the victims’ families and the affected community.

He thanked the people of Oyo State for their support in the 2023 elections, urging them to continue voting overwhelmingly for the APC at all levels.

President Tinubu acknowledged the contributions of prominent APC leaders and stakeholders in the South-west, including former Osun State Governor Bisi Akande, former Ogun State Governor Segun Osoba and other party elders.

He urged the electorate not to be distracted by opposition parties, accusing them of wanting to take away what Nigerians had worked hard to acquire.

“There is a party out there parading themselves. Please don’t mind them and don’t listen to them. They are only interested in clearing what you have. Vote for APC from top to bottom,” he said.

President Tinubu also inspected 800 vehicles procured by the Southwest Development Commission to boost the region’s security architecture.

In his remarks, Ekiti State Governor Biodun Oyebanji, speaking on behalf of APC governors, appealed to the South-west people to unite behind Mr Tinubu and other party candidates.

Mr Oyebanji said the South-west has an important role in determining the outcome of the presidential election and urged voters to support Mr Tinubu, the Oyo APC governorship candidate, Sarafadeen Ali, and other APC candidates in the senatorial, House of Representatives, and House of Assembly elections.

Adams Oshiomole spoke about strikes interrupting academic sessions before President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

“For a long time now, a lecturer will teach you for two days, strike for three days. Is that not the truth? For four years, your academic calendar has not been interrupted.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has deliberately decided that those who pave the way for tomorrow are the lecturers in our universities, and he has increased their pay substantially,” he said.

Mr Oshiomhole questioned how Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), would change the administration’s education policies under his proposal to reset Nigeria.

“Does Makinde want to reset the Tinubu policy on education? Does he want to reduce lecturers’ salaries? When you pay lecturers very well, intelligent minds will return to the teaching profession, a noble profession. Is that what Makinde wants to reset? What does he want to reset?”

The event had in attendance the Vice President, Kashim Shettima; First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu; wife of the Vice President, Nana Shettima; Senate President, Godswill Akpabio; Deputy Senate President, Barau Jibrin; Senate Majority Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele; governors of Ogun, Osun, Kwara, Imo, Ekiti, and Ondo; Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe; Chairman, Nigerian Revenue Service(NRS), Zacch Adedeji; Oyo APC Chairman, Moses Alake; among other dignitaries.

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information & Strategy)

November 21, 2026

World.title: Makinde’s campaign organisation criticises Tinubu over turnout at Ibadan rally
World.content:
The presidential campaign organisation of Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally in Ibadan, claiming that the event exposed the president’s declining support in the South-west.

In a statement on Saturday, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) described the rally as a “disgraceful flop” and said that residents of Oyo State and other parts of the region had shunned the event.

The organisation said the turnout showed that the South-west had rejected Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid and was increasingly backing Mr Makinde as an alternative in the 2027 presidential election.

“Burdened by failure and rejection, President Tinubu could not articulate any meaningful message to the people of Oyo State, but ironically accepted an empty scorecard by saying, ‘I will not be able to speak much to you. I just want to greet you.”

However, the campaign’s claim of poor attendance contrasts with a report by The ICIR, whose reporter at the venue described the gathering at Mapo Hall as a “mammoth crowd,” with supporters filling the main stage, backstage areas and surrounding streets.

The rally was also reportedly scaled down following a directive by Mr Tinubu that it be held without much fanfare in honour of victims of Friday’s boat accident in Bayelsa State. The president had expressed condolences to the bereaved families and directed federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts.

The MDPCO, however, argued that the rally’s turnout was evidence of Mr Tinubu’s waning popularity, contrasting it with the crowds that attended Mr Makinde’s presidential declaration on 14 May 2026, under the Allied Peoples Movement (APM).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It also accused the president of resorting to insults, mudslinging and unfulfilled promises instead of presenting his administration’s record to voters.

“Instead of presenting his stewardship in government, President Tinubu is making another list of fake promises, including the provision of electricity, the same promise he made three and half years ago,” the statement said.

The campaign’s reaction followed Mr Tinubu’s remarks at the rally, where he appeared to take a swipe at the APM, describing its members as a group with nowhere to go.

Mr Tinubu at the event also publicly endorsed the APC’s governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states: Sharafadeen Alli, Solomon Adeola and Obafemi Hamzat.

World.title: Niger village attack sparks deadly reprisals
World.content:
A dawn attack in which many people were reportedly killed in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State has triggered a wave of violence in neighbouring communities, including deadly reprisal attacks targeting Fulani residents and refugees.

Suspected terrorists reportedly killed at least 11 people, including a village head, his wife and children, in the attacks on Saturday in Lumman-Ba’are and Gada-Oli communities, according to a report by Daily Trust.

The newspaper stated that the assailants also burnt houses, abducted residents and rustled cattle.

The spokesperson for the Niger State Police Command, Wasiu Abiodun, confirmed the attack on Lumman-Ba’are.

In a statement quoted by Daily Trust, Mr Abiodun said the police received a report at about 5 a.m. on Saturday that armed men had invaded the village and killed about five people.

“Joint security teams have been deployed to the location, efforts to apprehend the suspected perpetrators ongoing. Further development will be communicated,” he said.

The newspaper reported that the village head and his wife were among those killed. Their bodies were reportedly buried in New Bussa, the headquarters of Borgu LGA.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A resident told the newspaper that the attackers opened fire on worshippers during morning prayers and set the village head’s palace ablaze.

Another source said the attackers also invaded Gada-Oli community at about 2 p.m. while residents were observing afternoon prayers, killing an unspecified number of people.

The newspaper reported that several residents fled their homes following the attacks.

SaharaReporters, quoting a resident, also reported that at least 11 people were killed in Luman Ba’are, including children under five. The source said some victims were burnt and several residents abducted.

According to PREMIUM TIMES’ findings, the attackers in Luman Ba’are targeted members of the Kambari community.

The community had been engaged in a violent conflict with Fulanis following a series of terror attacks attributed to a Boko Haram franchise terrorising the area.

Some locals allege that Fulani collaborators aided the insurgents, a suspicion that has further fuelled tensions (both offline and online) between the communities.

Following Boko Haram attacks on villages like Pisa, Kaduna Daji and Kabe among others, Kambari militias launched a reprisal campaign against Fulanis, forcing many of them to seek refuge in garrison towns such as Wawa, Agwara and neighbouring Kebbi State.

Sources, whose identities have been protected for safety reasons, confirmed to PREMIUM TIMES that armed men killed the village head of Lumma Ba’are and some other residents in the early hours of Saturday and that the assailants also set houses ablaze.

“The village was attacked while heading to the mosque for prayers around 5:00 am,” a community youth leader said, adding the deceased was thrown into a flaming fire.

The community is predominantly Kambari

Reprisal

By late morning, Kambari militias had gathered in their numbers, and launched reprisal attacks on Gada Oli, Wawa, Tunga Ibrahim and other villages where Fulanis were either residing or taking refuge.

In Wawa, a Niger community housing two military bases, the militias, riding on motorcycles, launched targeted attacks on Fulanis, killing them on sight.

“We thought they were terrorists,” said an eyewitness and businessman whose shop premises became a bloody site (two Fulanis killed there).

“They told us not to run,” he continued. “They said they were after the Fulanis.”

The reprisal attacks spread across about four villages, with the assailants spending roughly an hour in Wawa without encountering security personnel, according to eyewitnesses.

The scale of the casualties remains unclear. However, two eyewitnesses said they counted about 20 bodies in Wawa alone.

Footage and images from the attack are too gory for publication.

The violence in Wawa followed the withdrawal of Mobile Police (Mopol) officers from the town.

The Mopol, sources said, were deployed to Wawa about two months ago.

A simmering war

For weeks, PREMIUM TIMES has monitored social media posts and videos which pointed to mounting tensions in parts of the Borgu emirate, with some Fulani residents alleging killings of their kinsmen, while other videos captured individuals identifying as Fulanis threatening reprisals.

Online tensions escalated last week with the alleged killings of some Fulani travelers around Ibbi and Zugurma.

Recent attacks in Niger

The latest killings add to a series of attacks on rural communities in Niger State.

On 15 October, PREMIUM TIMES reported that suspected bandits killed five farmers, abducted 18 people and burnt houses and shops in separate attacks on Fanga community in Mashegu LGA and Kigbere and Kokani communities in Borgu LGA.

The attacks, which occurred between 9 and 12 October, forced residents to flee their homes. A resident told Daily Trust that the armed men had repeatedly imposed levies on Fanga community and attacked it after residents failed to meet their latest demand.

In another incident reported in the same period, residents of Rukukuje community in Rijau LGA fled their homes following reports of armed men moving into the area from neighbouring Zamfara State.

The recurring attacks have heightened concerns about the safety of rural communities, particularly farmers and residents who depend on access to their land and local markets for their livelihoods.

World.title: 2027: We’re not part of opposition coalition against Tinubu  –  Wike-backed PDP
World.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has said it is not part of the coalition seeking to unite opposition parties behind a single presidential candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election.

The opposition party said the only coalition arrangement it is committed to is the Rainbow Coalition, promoted by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to support Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid. Mr Wike is a PDP member.

The PDP National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Mohammed, stated this in a statement on Saturday, distancing the party from the opposition coalition arrangement being promoted under the Coalition for Democracy by Salihu Lukman, a former member of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The Coalition for Democracy emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on 31 August. Its founding members include the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP).

The parties are reportedly exploring the possibility of fielding a single presidential candidate to challenge Mr Tinubu of the ruling APC in 2027.

At that Abuja meeting, representatives of six opposition parties discussed a framework for cooperation. They agreed to establish leadership, publicity and legal committees and five working groups to develop a national covenant for democratic renewal, single four-year transition government, national reform programme, framework for opposition unity and roadmap to a common presidential candidate

The coalition was scheduled to hold its second opposition summit on 23 November but later announced its postponement to 30 November to allow interested opposition parties to conclude their scheduled campaigns.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, Mr Mohammed insisted that the PDP was not part of the coalition and that its members would not attend the summit.

“The PDP wishes to categorically state that it is not part of the said coalition, will not participate in the proposed summit and has not authorised any individual or group to represent or commit the party to the arrangement or any other political engagement of that nature.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the only coalition arrangement to which the PDP has expressed political commitment is the Rainbow Coalition, in accordance with the political direction and directives of our National Leader, His Excellency, Nyesom Wike. No other political coalition arrangement should be attributed to the PDP or presented as its official political position,” he said.

The PDP’s declaration is coming even though it is presenting its own presidential candidate, Sandy Onor, a former senator, in the 2027 election.

PDP threatens legal action

Mr Mohammed said the PDP members who had indicated interest in representing the party at the summit are not legitimate members, claiming that they had been expelled.

He said the coalition would not achieve its objectives if its organisers continued to associate the PDP with individuals who, according to him, are no longer legally recognised as members of the party.

“We wish to make it abundantly clear that this arrangement is dead on arrival, particularly insofar as its promoters seek to associate the PDP through individuals who have no lawful authority to represent the party. Nigerians should not be deceived by what appears to be a political project built on misrepresentation, questionable representation and a lack of sincerity,” he said.

The PDP spokesperson warned the organisers against involving the party in their political activities, threatening legal action if they continued to associate it with the coalition.

“Furthermore, the PDP hereby issues a stern warning to Mr Salihu M. Lukman, his associates and all promoters of this Kangaroo Coalition for Democracy to immediately desist from using the name, identity and institutional authority of the Peoples Democratic Party in furtherance of their political activities. The party will not hesitate to pursue appropriate legal action against any person or group that continues to unlawfully associate the PDP with this arrangement,” he said.

The PDP also urged members of the public, political stakeholders and its supporters to disregard claims that the party was involved in the coalition.

Background to opposition coalition

The latest effort to unite opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general election follows an earlier agreement reached at the National Summit of Opposition Political Parties held in Ibadan, Oyo State, on 25 April.

At the meeting, attended by prominent opposition figures, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi, participants adopted a communiqué known as the Ibadan Declaration.

Among other resolutions, the opposition leaders agreed to resist the ruling APC attempts to establish a one-party state, defend multiparty democracy and work towards presenting a single presidential candidate to challenge President Tinubu in 2027.

They also demanded the removal of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Chairman, Joash Amupitan, over alleged bias, and called on the National Assembly to review provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 that they considered capable of undermining electoral credibility.

However, the proposed opposition alliance subsequently faced setbacks following disagreements among its leading figures and defections from the ADC, which had emerged as a major platform for the opposition realignment.

In May, Mr Obi and Mr Kwankwaso, who were among the prominent figures at the Ibadan summit, left the ADC and joined the NDC, due to internal crises, legal disputes and uncertainty surrounding the party.

Their departure raised fresh questions about the opposition’s ability to agree on a common presidential candidate, particularly amid competing presidential ambitions among its leading politicians.

Meanwhile, disagreements over the legitimacy of party representatives at the Ibadan meeting also prompted the Wike-backed faction of the PDP, some ADC factions, the Labour Party and the Accord Party to distance themselves from the summit and its resolutions.

World.title: Many die in Bayelsa boat mishap, Tinubu orders federal agencies to join rescue effort
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has directed federal disaster response agencies to join rescue operations following a boat accident in Bayelsa State.

Police say four people were killed, but community sources told PREMIUM TIMES that the death toll could be higher.

The accident occurred around 11 a.m. on Friday at the Oweikorogha/Otuan river junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, involving a passenger boat conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony.

In a statement posted on X on Saturday, the Nigerian Presidency said Mr Tinubu was saddened by the incident and had directed relevant federal agencies to work together to ensure successful rescue and recovery operations.

The president also ordered that the APC presidential campaign rally scheduled for Saturday in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who died.

Police spokesperson in Bayelsa, Musa Mohammed, a deputy superintendent of police, in a statement posted on the Facebook page of the Command said preliminary investigations indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways.

He said some passengers reportedly urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank, but he allegedly refused before the boat capsized.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to the police, four bodies, comprising two adults and two children, had been recovered and deposited at the Federal Medical Centre mortuary in Yenagoa.

Twenty-four survivors were rescued. Nineteen were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five injured passengers were conveyed to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa.

However, community sources told PREMIUM TIMES that more than four people died in the accident, raising questions about the actual casualty figure.

The police said the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, was taken into custody for investigation.

The Commissioner of Police, Ajao Saka Adewale, directed the Marine Police and local divers to intensify search and rescue operations to account for everyone aboard the boat.

Mr Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, Governor Douye Diri and the people of Bayelsa State.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu promises to halve out-of-school children, recruit 20,000 teachers by 2031
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has promised to halve the number of out-of-school children in Nigeria by 2031 as well as recruit and train 20,000 additional teachers, setting measurable targets for a sector still grappling with poor access, inadequate facilities and weak learning outcomes.

The president’s promises are contained in the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s 2027–2031 manifesto, “From Reforms to Prosperity,” which was presented on 10 November in Abuja.

The Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Jumoke Oduwole, who presented an overview of the document on behalf of the president, outlined plans to expand school access, improve retention, strengthen teacher capacity and make learning environments safer.

Under the section titled “We Will Guarantee School Access, Safety, And Educational Retention,” the president says it will “scale HOPE-EDU nationwide to halve the number of out-of-school children by 2031.”

He also promised to extend the Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment (AGILE), which currently operates in 18 states, to other states with high numbers of girls excluded from education.

He further proposed “dedicated return-to-school pathways for teenage mothers,” recognising the barriers that often prevent young mothers from continuing their education

On teacher recruitment, President Tinubu said he will build on the 80,284 teachers already certified and licensed by recruiting and training another 20,000, with priority given to female educators and underserved rural communities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also pledged to enforce safe-school standards, expand access to water and sanitation facilities and publish an annual education dashboard tracking enrolment, dropout and completion rates.

Nigeria’s out-of-school children

The proposed reduction in out-of-school children comes against the background of a long-standing national education challenge.

A 2024 UNICEF report estimated that 10.2 million primary-school-age children and 8.1 million children of junior secondary school age were out of school in Nigeria.

The federal government has also provided a different estimate. In April 2026, the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, reportedly put the figure at 15 million, while the ministry said nearly one million children had been mapped for reintegration into formal schools and alternative learning pathways.

The different estimates make it necessary for the government to establish a clear baseline for its 2031 target. Although the president promised an annual education dashboard, he did not state the precise number of out-of-school children against which the proposed 50 per cent reduction will be measured.

He did not also provide annual targets showing how many children the government expects to enrol or retain in school each year.

The challenge also extends beyond getting children into classrooms. UNICEF has reported that 74 per cent of Nigerian children aged 7 to 14 lack basic reading and mathematics skills, highlighting the need to assess learning outcomes alongside enrolment figures.

How the new promises compare with the 2023 manifesto

Education was also a major component of Mr Tinubu’s 2023 manifesto, Renewed Hope: Action Plan for a Better Nigeria.

The earlier document promised improvements in school infrastructure, teacher training, curriculum development, digital learning and girls’ access to education. It also proposed stronger accreditation standards, professional development for teachers and improved learning facilities.

Several of those priorities remain in the 2027 document, particularly teacher development, girls’ education, technical training and the use of technology in schools.

The new manifesto, however, attaches specific numerical targets to some commitments. These include halving the number of out-of-school children by 2031 and recruiting and training 20,000 additional teachers.

The 2027 document also promises an annual education dashboard to track enrolment, dropout and completion rates, creating a proposed mechanism for monitoring progress.

What the government says it has achieved

The manifesto presents several figures as evidence of progress under the Tinubu administration.

It reports that 3.7 million girls have been enrolled in secondary schools across 18 states through the AGILE programme, while more than 10,000 schools have been rehabilitated.

The document also says 80,284 teachers have been certified and licensed, about 978,000 teachers have received training and 10,000 classrooms have been renovated nationwide

These are figures reported by the government in the manifesto. They do not, on their own, establish whether the interventions have improved learning outcomes or significantly reduced the number of children excluded from school.

The manifesto acknowledges that the next phase must ensure that children can enrol, learn effectively and complete their education safely.

It states that the immediate priority is “ensuring every child can enrol, learn effectively, and complete their education safely,” supported by more trained teachers, stronger school protection and modern learning environments

Beyond access and retention, the president proposes measures to improve the quality and relevance of education, particularly in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and digital learning.

The manifesto says the government will “prioritise foundational learning, science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and digital capabilities across all educational levels.”

It also promises stronger partnerships with industries to provide practical, work-linked training and align courses with labour-market needs.

On technical and vocational education, the president proposes expanding training programmes, building on the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) initiative. The manifesto reports that the initiative has enrolled 117,152 verified trainees, while monthly stipends increased from ₦22,500 to ₦30,000

He says the success of these programmes will be assessed through graduate employment, business survival and workplace productivity.

At the tertiary level, the manifesto promises to scale the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), expand the National Smart Learning Initiative and extend the Student Venture Capital Grant and Diaspora BRIDGE to more institutions [p. 42].

The document reports that NELFUND had processed 1,659,853 applications and paid ₦355.87 billion in student loans. Of the amount, ₦192.89 billion went towards institutional fees for students in 319 institutions, while ₦162.98 billion was paid as upkeep allowances [pp. 37–38].

It also says the Renewed Hope Energising Education Programme has provided electricity to 37 federal universities and seven teaching hospitals.

However, the manifesto leaves unanswered how the government intends to address the financial and social pressures that keep children out of school, particularly in communities where poverty, distance to schools and other barriers affect attendance.

The annual education dashboard could provide a basis for public scrutiny, but its usefulness will depend on whether it publishes verifiable, state-level data and tracks actual learning outcomes.

For a country still struggling to get millions of children into classrooms, the success of the proposed education plan will depend on whether the commitments translate into sustained enrolment, improved teaching and better learning outcomes.

World.title: Three killed, 13 injured in attack on Gombe community
World.content:
Residents have demanded justice after an attack on Friday night, allegedly by personnel of the Nigerian Air Force (NAF), left three people dead and 13 others injured in Lawanti community in Akko Local Government Area of Gombe State.

The community accused personnel attached to the Air Force’s 109 Combat Reconnaissance Group (109 CRG) in Gombe of shooting and beating residents during a confrontation over suspected theft of armoured cables.

Speaking to journalists on behalf of the community, the Programme Officer of Lawanti Foundation, Idris Maigari Lawanti, called on the federal and state governments to identify and prosecute those involved for the attack.

“Our families deserve to know what happened, who gave the orders and who carried them out,” Mr Lawanti said.

He said no allegation of criminal wrongdoing could justify the use of excessive force against civilians.

“We call on the Gombe State Government and the Federal Government to ensure a prompt, independent investigation into allegations that personnel of the Nigerian Air Force’s 109 Combat Reconnaissance Group were involved,” he said.

Mr Lawanti named the three deceased residents as Yayaji Alhaji Abdul Kura, Hamma Magaji, and Inna Anttu Umar Bello.

He said Mr Kura was received in the hospital dead after sustaining gunshot wounds, while Mr Magaji allegedly died following a beating.

According to the community, Mr Bello died during the incident due to what residents attributed to shock.

The exact medical causes of the deaths have yet to be established.

Mr Lawanti said 13 residents sustained injuries, with 12 taken to the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe, for treatment.

He named Sale Abubakar, 30, as one of the injured persons, saying he was taken to the operating theatre for emergency surgery.

Another victim, Paul Simple, was reportedly taken to the Cottage Hospital in Amada after allegedly being beaten.

The community called on the Gombe State Government to settle the medical bills of the injured and provide financial and other assistance to the families of those who died.

“Lawanti is a peaceful community. If any resident is accused of wrongdoing, that person is entitled to answer the allegation before a court,” he said.

“An accusation against an individual can never justify opening fire on residents or beating anyone as punishment.”

The community demanded that investigators obtain evidence from survivors, eyewitnesses, hospital officials and relatives of the deceased.

It also insisted that the findings of the investigation should be made public.

“Where the evidence establishes wrongdoing, those responsible must face the full consequences of the law,” Mr Lawanti said.

He appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid taking the law into their own hands.

“We appeal to our people to remain calm and to continue looking after one another as we seek justice,” he said.

Meanwhile, Governor Yahaya has condemned the incident and ordered an investigation.

In a statement issued on Saturday by his Director-General of Press Affairs, Ismaila Uba Misilli, the governor described the incident as deeply distressing.

The government acknowledged preliminary reports of three deaths and 13 injuries, with some victims receiving treatment at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe.

Governor Yahaya directed a delegation led by the Secretary to the State Government, Ibrahim Njodi, to visit Lawanti, meet affected families and assess the situation.

He also ordered an investigation to determine the circumstances of the incident and ensure appropriate action under the law.

The governor assured residents that his administration would work with relevant security agencies to address the matter.

He also promised government support for the injured and bereaved families, while appealing to residents to avoid reprisals or actions that could escalate tensions.

Efforts to obtain the Nigerian Air Force’s reaction to the allegations were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

Repeated telephone calls to officials of the 109 Combat Reconnaissance Group in Gombe and the Nigerian Air Force Headquarters in Abuja, including attempts to reach the unit commander and the Force’s spokesperson, went unanswered.

Consequently, the military’s account of the confrontation and its response to the allegations against its personnel could not be obtained.

Another resident, Musa Haruna, said the community wanted more than expressions of sympathy, stressing that the circumstances surrounding the deaths must be established and those found culpable held accountable.

He urged the authorities to make the investigation’s findings public and ensure that affected families receive appropriate assistance.

World.title: ABBACARE: How Kano is expanding healthcare access for the most vulnerable
World.content:
Gov. Abba Yusuf

By Hassan A. Karofi

Access to affordable healthcare remains a major challenge for millions of Nigerians, particularly low-income households and vulnerable groups who often delay or forgo treatment because of the cost. In Kano State, the ABBACARE Initiative is one of the interventions aimed at addressing this challenge through social health insurance.

Implemented by the Kano State Contributory Healthcare Management Agency (KSCHMA), ABBACARE is designed to provide healthcare coverage for vulnerable groups, including pregnant women, persons living with sickle cell disorder and emergency patients. Its focus is on reducing the financial barriers that prevent people from accessing essential medical services.

According to figures provided for the initiative, ABBACARE has enrolled 28,721 beneficiaries and extended service delivery to 13 hospitals across Kano State’s three senatorial zones. These figures point to an effort to widen access to healthcare, although the programme’s long-term impact will depend on the quality of services available, the regularity of funding and the ability to sustain coverage as more people are enrolled.

The initiative also highlights the role state governments can play in advancing Universal Health Coverage through social health insurance. While national policies provide an important framework, state-level programmes such as ABBACARE can help address local healthcare needs and extend financial protection to people who might otherwise struggle to pay for treatment.

The programme is part of a wider set of health interventions under Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s administration. Another is the Gida-Gida Lafiya Project, which focuses on hypertension and other non-communicable diseases through the distribution of customised digital blood pressure monitors.

The devices are intended to help beneficiaries monitor their blood pressure, identify possible health risks early and seek medical attention when necessary. Their adaptation to provide guidance in local languages also reflects the importance of making health information accessible to people in their communities.

Although ABBACARE and Gida-Gida Lafiya address different aspects of healthcare, they speak to two related challenges. The former seeks to reduce the financial burden of accessing treatment, while the latter encourages prevention, regular monitoring and early intervention. Both approaches are relevant in a health system where the cost of treatment and late presentation at hospitals can worsen health outcomes.

However, the success of such interventions should not be measured by enrolment figures or the number of devices distributed alone. Their value will ultimately depend on whether beneficiaries can consistently access the services promised, whether participating hospitals have the capacity to provide quality care and whether the programmes are adequately funded over time.

The Kano State Ministry of Health and the leadership of KSCHMA therefore have important roles to play in ensuring that the initiatives deliver their intended benefits. Dr Rahila Mukhtar, whose role in the agency’s operations and healthcare financing efforts has been noteworthy, is among the key figures associated with the implementation of approaches such as ABBACARE.

The agency’s work in administering the initiative underscores the importance of effective health insurance management. Enrolling vulnerable people is an important first step, but maintaining reliable access to care requires proper coordination with healthcare providers, transparent management of funds, regular monitoring and accountability to beneficiaries.

For Kano, the next task is to consolidate the gains made through ABBACARE and ensure that the programme remains accessible and sustainable. Expanding coverage will also require attention to the capacity of participating hospitals and the experiences of beneficiaries, particularly those who depend on the scheme for maternal care, treatment of sickle cell disorder and emergency services.

Other states can draw useful lessons from Kano’s experience, especially in using social health insurance to protect vulnerable populations. However, the model’s wider relevance will depend on evidence of its outcomes, affordability and sustainability.

As Nigeria pursues Universal Health Coverage, initiatives such as ABBACARE show why state-level action matters. The real measure of progress will not simply be the number of people enrolled, but whether they can obtain timely, affordable and quality healthcare when they need it.

•Karofi writes from Abuja and can be reached at [email protected].

World.title: ASIWAJU: Why I support 2nd term for President Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu

By Moriamoh Ojikutu

A friend asked me recently, “Do you think Asiwaju is working?” My answer was simple: “Yes. He is doing his job.”

Let me be clear about where I stand. I strongly support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his administration, and I want him re-elected for a second term.

I believe in his leadership and the direction of his administration. I want him to complete the work he has started and deliver the lasting improvements I believe are possible.

That does not mean I think everything is perfect. It certainly does not mean I am unaware of the difficulties Nigerians are facing.

I live here. I run businesses here. I employ people, pay bills, buy fuel and deal with rising costs. I know what it means to reconsider spending, adjust plans and keep going when doing business becomes more difficult.

My support exists alongside that reality, not outside it.

When I say he is doing his job, I mean that I believe he is confronting difficult problems rather than leaving them for someone else.

But taking difficult decisions is not the finish line. Delivering results that Nigerians can see, touch and feel is.

Reform Is Rarely Comfortable: I do not believe Nigeria’s economic difficulties began with this administration, nor do I believe every problem can be resolved within a few years.

My view is that some difficult decisions had been postponed for too long.

President Tinubu’s administration has pursued major changes, including the removal of petrol subsidies and reforms to the foreign exchange system.

I support the decision to confront those structural problems. But I also recognise the hardship Nigerians have experienced during this period.

Families are making difficult choices. Businesses are adjusting their operations. People are working hard and still worrying about what they can afford.

Those experiences deserve to be heard, not dismissed with political slogans.

For me, acknowledging the pain does not mean rejecting the need for reform. It means asking how reform can be implemented more effectively and how people can be better protected through the transition.

A policy can have a sound objective and still need adjustments. I want the government to listen, respond and improve what needs to work better.

That is part of making reform succeed.

We Should Acknowledge Meaningful Interventions:

Alongside discussing the hardship, I believe we should recognise interventions intended to help people.

NELFUND provides interest-free loans to help eligible students overcome financial barriers to higher education, with support for institutional fees and/or upkeep. These are loans with repayment obligations, not grants.

For a student facing the possibility of leaving school because of money, access to financial support can make a meaningful difference. Education is one of the areas in which I want government intervention to open doors.

MAMII is another initiative I welcome. It focuses on reducing maternal and newborn deaths through measures that include improving access to care, strengthening referral systems and helping services respond to complications during pregnancy and childbirth.

As a country, we should care deeply about whether mothers can access care and whether students can continue their education.

These programmes deserve attention, alongside honest questions about whom they are reaching, how effectively they are operating and what results they are delivering.

I want them strengthened and delivered well. Recognising their value does not mean declaring the work complete. It means making room for a fair assessment of the administration.

Accountability at Every Level: I expect leadership from the president. I also expect governors, local government chairmen, legislators and ministers to fulfil their responsibilities.

Holding the presidency accountable should be the beginning of a wider demand for good governance, not the end of it.

When communities lack functioning schools, healthcare, drainage or clean water, citizens should ask which institutions are responsible, what resources they have received and what they have delivered.

We should ask these questions consistently, regardless of party affiliation. What is happening in our states? What is happening in our local governments? What are the people representing us doing with the responsibilities entrusted to them?

I want this presidency to succeed, and I want every other level of government to do its part.

Nigeria needs more than one office working. It needs public institutions and officials taking their responsibilities seriously.

Public Money Must Deliver Public Value: Government must be able to explain what citizens’ sacrifices are achieving. Where revenues and allocations increase, people deserve to know how those resources are being used.

How much was received? What was budgeted? What was spent? What was completed? And how has it improved people’s lives?

These should be normal questions, not uncomfortable ones. I want to see public money translate into better schools, accessible healthcare, reliable infrastructure and essential services.

I want clear reporting that allows citizens to judge performance beyond speeches and announcements.

Public funds are not personal gifts from politicians. They are resources held in trust for the people.

That trust must be respected at every level of government.

Security Must Remain a Priority: Security is central to the Nigeria I want to see.

Our farmers should be able to work without fear. Families should be able to travel safely. Communities should be protected, and businesses should be able to operate with confidence.

These are not partisan expectations. They are basic expectations of government.

I want the administration’s economic ambitions to be matched by sustained improvements in security.

Progress must be felt in people’s confidence that they can travel, earn a living and go about their daily lives safely.

That is an essential part of the success I want for this presidency.

Support Should Not Require Blindness: I sometimes find our political culture exhausting.

Apparently, you must either support everything a government does or oppose everything it does. There seems to be little room for thoughtful disagreement.

I reject that thinking.

I can support President Tinubu and question how a policy is being implemented. I can acknowledge progress and ask for greater urgency elsewhere. I can support the APC and still expect its public officials to explain their decisions and account for public resources.

There is no contradiction in that.

My questions do not come from uncertainty about where I stand. They come from wanting an administration I support to succeed.

Loyalty should not mean silence. Criticism should not automatically mean opposition.

We need room for honest conversations about what is working, what is not and what must happen next.

That is the kind of political participation I believe in: committed, constructive and willing to speak honestly.

Why I Support a Second Term: I want President Tinubu re-elected for a second term because I believe in his leadership and want him to complete the work he has begun.

I believe continuity offers an opportunity to build on these reforms, improve their implementation and turn policy changes into improvements people can feel.

That is my conviction, not a belief that time alone will solve our problems.

Nigerians need relief today. People need affordable food, access to healthcare, reliable electricity, security and opportunities for their children.

They need an economy in which hard work offers a reasonable chance of a decent living.

Those expectations are fair, and I want this administration to meet them with greater urgency.

For me, a second term should be an opportunity to build on what is working, correct what is not and deliver more widely.

I want stronger businesses, functioning institutions, better infrastructure and genuine opportunities for young Nigerians.

I want the sacrifices of this period to lead somewhere meaningful.

And I want a government that understands that the patience of the people must never be taken for granted.

Hope, With Its Eyes Open: So, why Asiwaju? Because I believe in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s leadership, I support his administration, and I want him re-elected for a second term. I want him to complete the work he has started and turn the promise of these reforms into lasting improvements in the lives of Nigerians.

I do not dismiss the hardship people are facing, and my support does not mean silence when something needs to improve. I want this presidency to succeed and I want that success to be felt in our homes, our businesses and our communities.

That is where I stand: firmly in support, clear about my expectations, and hopeful for Nigeria.

Hope, with its eyes open.

World.title: Why construction could become Africa’s key technology, investment opportunity
World.content:
By Jimoh Razaq

For years, Africa’s technology ecosystem has concentrated much of its entrepreneurial energy, investment capital and innovation around fintech, e-commerce, mobility, telecommunications and entertainment. These sectors have produced remarkable companies, attracted international investment and demonstrated that African businesses can build technology products capable of scaling across borders.

But there is another industry with enormous economic significance, deeply entrenched inefficiencies and a largely untapped opportunity for technological transformation: construction.

It is an industry that builds our homes, roads, hospitals, schools, factories, power infrastructure and cities. It employs millions of people, supports extensive manufacturing and distribution networks, moves significant volumes of capital and sits at the centre of economic development.

Yet much of its operational infrastructure remains fragmented, manual and inefficient.

While technology has transformed how people transfer money, order food, book transportation and access entertainment, the processes through which buildings and infrastructure are planned, financed, procured and delivered remain remarkably difficult to coordinate.

This is not simply an operational inconvenience. It is a massive economic opportunity.

The next generation of transformative African technology companies may emerge from solving the problems of the industries that physically build Africa.

The industry technology has overlooked

Construction is one of the world’s largest economic sectors. Global construction output was approximately $13 trillion in 2023, with projections suggesting it could reach $22 trillion by 2040.

Yet its productivity performance remains disappointing.

McKinsey’s 2024 research found that global construction productivity grew by approximately 0.4 per cent annually between 2000 and 2022, compared with around 2 per cent for the broader economy. This represents a productivity improvement of only about 10 per cent over more than two decades.

The implications are significant.

Projects experience delays. Budgets become unreliable. Material procurement remains fragmented. Labour productivity is difficult to measure. Project information is scattered across emails, spreadsheets, paper documents and messaging applications. Developers, contractors, consultants, suppliers, artisans and investors often operate without a shared information environment.

These challenges are particularly visible in emerging markets, where informal transactions, inconsistent data, financing constraints and infrastructure limitations compound existing industry inefficiencies.

Africa’s infrastructure ambitions make the opportunity even more important. The OECD’s Africa’s Development Dynamics 2025 estimates that investing approximately $155 billion annually in infrastructure could significantly accelerate the continent’s economic growth.

The question is not whether Africa needs more construction. It clearly does.

The question is whether the industry can deliver the volume of housing, infrastructure and commercial development required without fundamentally changing how it operates.

That is where technology founders should pay attention.

Construction is not just an engineering industry. It is a technology ecosystem waiting to be connected.

One of the biggest misconceptions about construction technology is that innovation is primarily about drones, robotics, 3D printing or sophisticated building design software.

Those technologies matter, but they represent only a fraction of the opportunity.

Construction is also an industry of financial transactions, procurement networks, logistics, labour coordination, data management, risk assessment, asset management and complex workflows.

Every construction project creates multiple interconnected problems that technology can solve.

Consider what happens when someone decides to build a house.

They need to verify land ownership, develop architectural and structural drawings, estimate project costs, secure financing, identify qualified professionals, procure materials, engage artisans, manage construction activities, monitor expenditure and verify completion.

Each stage involves multiple stakeholders, financial commitments and operational decisions.

In many African markets, these activities are still managed through disconnected systems.

There is an opportunity to build technology infrastructure that connects this entire process.

Opportunities that could redefine construction in Africa

AI-powered construction cost intelligence: One of the most persistent problems in construction is inaccurate project costing. Material prices fluctuate. Labour rates differ by location. Transportation costs change. Exchange-rate movements affect imported materials, while poor historical data makes reliable forecasting difficult.

An intelligent construction cost engine could combine material prices, labour rates, geographical information, historical project costs and market conditions to generate more reliable estimates.

Imagine a developer being able to estimate the cost of constructing a residential building in Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan or Accra using current market information rather than relying entirely on outdated rate books.

This is an opportunity for AI engineers, data scientists and construction professionals to build genuinely useful products.

Digital construction material marketplaces: The procurement of cement, reinforcement steel, roofing materials, electrical fittings, plumbing components and other construction products remains highly fragmented. Buyers frequently depend on personal contacts, multiple quotations and informal supplier relationships.

A verified digital marketplace could connect manufacturers, distributors, suppliers, contractors and developers through transparent pricing, product verification, digital payments and delivery tracking.

Beyond convenience, such a platform could improve price discovery, reduce procurement fraud and create a more accountable supply chain.

Save-To-Build financial technology: Millions of people want to build houses but cannot finance the entire project at once. Traditional construction financing is often inaccessible, while informal savings arrangements do not necessarily provide the structure or safeguards required for long-term building projects.

A Save-To-Build platform could allow individuals to accumulate funds towards clearly defined construction milestones. For example, a customer could save towards land documentation, architectural design, foundation construction, roofing and finishing.

Funds could be released against verified milestones, supported by appropriate financial safeguards and partnerships with regulated financial institutions.

This creates an opportunity to connect personal finance, construction delivery and financial inclusion.

AI-powered site supervision and project intelligence: Construction sites generate enormous amounts of information, but much of it is not systematically captured or analysed. Artificial intelligence, computer vision and mobile technology could help monitor construction progress, identify deviations from approved designs, track material consumption, record labour attendance and flag potential safety issues.

A project owner could receive a digital site performance report without having to depend exclusively on periodic manual updates.

The goal is not to replace professional site supervision or engineering judgement. It is to equip professionals with better information to make faster and more informed decisions.

5. Skilled labour and artisan marketplaces

Africa’s construction industry depends heavily on skilled and semi-skilled workers, many of whom operate within informal employment networks. Finding reliable masons, electricians, plumbers, tilers, welders, carpenters and other artisans can be difficult.

A structured digital marketplace could provide verified profiles, skills assessments, ratings, work histories, location-based discovery and protected payment arrangements.

Such platforms could also create opportunities for professional training, certification and workforce development.

Technology can help formalise an important part of the construction economy without excluding the people who already work within it.

Digital property development and off-plan sales platforms: Property developers frequently sell units before construction is completed. However, buyers may struggle to obtain reliable information about construction progress, payment schedules, contractual obligations and project delivery.

A digital off-plan platform could provide verified developer profiles, interactive property models, payment tracking, digital contracts and construction progress updates.

This would improve transparency and help restore confidence in property development markets.

Modular and industrialised construction technology: Construction technology should not be limited to software. There is a significant opportunity in developing prefabricated building systems, modular housing components, standardised structural elements and rapid-assembly construction solutions.

Combining digital design, manufacturing automation and efficient project logistics could reduce construction time, material waste and repetitive site activities.

This is particularly relevant to affordable housing, student accommodation, healthcare facilities and standardised institutional buildings.

Construction logistics and material tracking: Materials and equipment move continuously between manufacturers, warehouses, suppliers, transport operators and construction sites. Poor coordination leads to delayed deliveries, unnecessary transportation costs, material losses and idle equipment.

Internet of Things technology, QR codes, GPS tracking and logistics management software could provide greater visibility across the supply chain.

Developers could know what has been ordered, what has been dispatched, what has arrived and what has actually been consumed on site.

Digital building approvals and regulatory platforms: Building approval processes can involve several agencies, professional submissions, inspections and compliance requirements.
