Defensa said the operation followed intelligence coordination with US agencies. It described Meza Flores as head of the Beltrán Leyva organisation, a long-running Mexican trafficking network, and an ally of the Mayos, a faction of the Sinaloa cartel.

The capture took out three roles at once: the alleged leader, his second-in-command and his financial operator, according to Defensa. Whether that weakens the group or sparks a fight over who leads it is not yet known.

What Is Not Known

Neither Defensa nor federal prosecutors have published charges, a court date or an extradition request.

Two checkpoints matter next: the detainees’ first appearance before a federal judge, which has no public date, and any extradition request from Washington. Until a court rules, Meza Flores and the others are suspects, not convicts.

What It Means for US Readers

The clear gain is for US prosecutors, who now have a Ten Most Wanted fugitive in Mexican custody. The clear risk is for travellers and residents in Sinaloa, where the raid brought deadly fighting.

The State Department already tells Americans not to travel to Sinaloa, a Level 4 warning, its highest. Mazatlán, a Pacific beach resort popular with US visitors, lies in the same state, so anyone with plans should check the current advisory first.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people died in the Chapo Isidro raid?

Eleven, according to Defensa: four soldiers and seven suspected gunmen. Eight people were detained.

Who is Chapo Isidro?

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, alias “Chapo Isidro”, is a cartel leader on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list, with a US reward of up to US$5 million. He is a suspect until a court rules.

World.title: Two Dominicans Sent to US on Murder Charges
World.content:
The Attorney General’s Office says the handovers followed executive decrees and Supreme Court rulings, and that both men had been held since their arrests in September and October.

Photo: Mariordo (Mario Roberto Durán Ortiz) / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Crime: Dominican Republic

The Dominican Republic handed two of its citizens to US officials, with US Marshals Service support, on 21 November 2026 to face murder charges in New York. The Dominican Attorney General’s Office says one man is wanted in a federal drug-trafficking murder case and the other for a killing under New York State law.

Felicito Celestino Mercedes, 63, and Ramón Romero, 48, were flown out on a commercial flight from Las Américas International Airport, near Santo Domingo. Both are suspects, and neither has been convicted of anything.

Key Facts Who. Felicito Celestino Mercedes, 63, and Ramón Romero, 48, also known as Ramón Joaquín Romero Bastardo.

What. Extradited to New York on murder charges; one case is tied to cocaine trafficking.

Where. Handed to US officials at Las Américas airport, Santo Domingo.

As of. 21 November 2026, 23:30 GMT.

The Attorney General’s Office says the handovers followed executive decrees and Supreme Court rulings, and that both men had been held since their arrests in September and October.

The Attorney General’s Office and the national drug control agency, the DNCD, carried out the operation with the US Marshals Service, the federal agency that moves wanted people. The men were held under heavy security until they were formally handed over at the airport.

Mercedes was arrested in October 2026 in Villa Riva, in Duarte province in the north-east. He is wanted in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York, the federal court in Manhattan, on a charge of intentional murder, including counselling, ordering, inducing and causing a killing, in connection with a drug-trafficking conspiracy.

He also faces a charge of conspiracy to distribute, or possess with intent to distribute, five kilograms or more of mixtures containing cocaine. The prosecutors’ summary uses several aliases for him, among them “Pito” and Winston Peralta.

Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. (File photo)

Romero was captured in September 2026 in the Cambelén area of Higüey, in La Altagracia province, where the Punta Cana resorts are located. New York State law is the basis of his case: second-degree murder, first-degree manslaughter, first-degree gang assault, second-degree assault and fourth-degree criminal possession of a weapon.

Dominican prosecutors have not described the victims, the dates or the places of the killings in either case. The charges are as stated by the Dominican prosecutors; the US court papers were not available.

Two Legal Tracks, One Flight

The two cases run on separate tracks in New York. Mercedes faces a federal case in the Southern District, while Romero faces charges brought under New York State penal law.

Each handover rested on an executive decree and a resolution of the Second Chamber of the Supreme Court, the chamber that reviews extradition requests. The Attorney General’s Office said the case reflects close cooperation and intelligence sharing with the United States on fugitives.

Mercedes was arrested in October and Romero in September, and the authorities have not given exact arrest dates. They have not said when either man will first appear before a US judge.

For US readers, the cases show how the Dominican Republic, a major destination for American travellers, works with US agencies on violent crime and drug trafficking. The charges concern the suspects’ alleged conduct in each case, and the prosecutors’ announcement does not mention any risk to tourists.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who are the two men?

They are Felicito Celestino Mercedes and Ramón Romero, who is also known as Ramón Joaquín Romero Bastardo. Dominican authorities arrested them in October and September.

What are they accused of?

Mercedes faces murder and cocaine conspiracy charges in a federal court in Manhattan. Romero faces second-degree murder and related charges under New York State law.

World.title: Peronists Name Máximo Kirchner Congress Head
World.content:
The post goes to Kirchner under a deal he struck with Governor Axel Kicillof, who has led the provincial party since April.

Imágenes de íconos de la ciudad: vista de Obelisco y 9 de Julio desde el Hotel Panamericano

Politics: Argentina

Máximo Kirchner, a national deputy and the son of former president Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, became president of the Buenos Aires provincial Peronist party’s Congress, its governing assembly, on Saturday 21 November 2026. The party named him in a hybrid session held from its headquarters in La Plata, the provincial capital, with other delegates joining remotely.

The Peronist party, officially the Partido Justicialista (PJ), is the movement founded by Juan Perón. The vote shares out the top posts of the provincial party between Kirchner and Governor Axel Kicillof ahead of the 2027 presidential race.

Kirchner led the Buenos Aires provincial party until 24 April 2026, when Kicillof, the province’s governor, took over the presidency. Kirchner skipped the party council’s first meeting under Kicillof and was at a political meeting in Santa Fe province that day.

The two men sealed an agreement in February under which Kicillof would preside over the party and Kirchner would chair its Congress. On 3 November they met privately, and the party council chaired by Kicillof then called Saturday’s session on Wednesday 4 November.

“We have been saying that Máximo will chair it,” Kicillof told reporters after the council meeting, adding that it was important for the party to be “absolutely within the rules”. The two leaders met after days of tension over the 2027 candidacies.

The wider backdrop is a fight over how Argentines pick candidates. President Javier Milei’s government has proposed abolishing the PASO, the open primary elections held before national votes, through the national Congress, the country’s legislature.

Kicillof told the party council that Peronism is “trying to defend people’s electoral rights” by keeping the primaries. He also accused the national government of using funds and budget talks to win governors’ political support.

The Congress then filled the rest of the party’s provincial leadership, alongside the party council that Kicillof chairs. Pablo Zurro, the mayor of Pehuajó, a town in Buenos Aires province, became first vice-president, followed by Carlos Bianco, the provincial government minister and a Kicillof ally, then Cristina Álvarez Rodríguez, an adviser to the governor, and Federico Achával, the mayor of Pilar.

Jorge Ferraresi, a Kicillof ally, took the post of secretary general. Leonardo Nardini, the mayor of Malvinas Argentinas, continues to chair the party’s electoral board.

A Seat for the Governor in the National Party

The session also named four delegates to the national Congress of the PJ, the party’s nationwide assembly: Kicillof, Kirchner, Teresa García, a lawmaker, and Vice-Governor Verónica Magario. Kicillof’s inclusion gives the governor a direct seat in the party’s national Congress, a separate body from the provincial one.

That matters because the party’s internal balance will shape its 2027 choice. The party has not named a 2027 presidential candidate, and nothing in Saturday’s vote settles that question.

What Prediction Markets Say Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, priced Argentina’s presidential election winner at about 44% for Javier Milei and 30% for Axel Kicillof on 21 November 2026 (6:35 p.m. ET), with about US$1.6 million traded across all candidates. These prices are bets, not polls. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Máximo Kirchner?

He is a national deputy and the son of former president Cristina Fernández de Kirchner. He is a leading figure of La Cámpora, a youth movement within Peronism.

Does the new post make him the party’s leader in Buenos Aires?

No. Axel Kicillof, the province’s governor, has been president of the provincial party since April 2026. Kirchner chairs its Congress, a separate body.

Has the Peronist candidate for 2027 been chosen?

No. The party has not announced a presidential candidate, and Saturday’s vote did not decide one.

At 11:58 a.m. on Thursday 19 November, GPL says, staff restarting supply at the Canefield substation, the power-distribution station for East Berbice, saw a flash coming from one of its switchgear cubicles, the metal housings that route and protect electricity. GPL then found damaged parts, replaced them, and hit a second fault in the busbar, the heavy conductor that feeds the lines out to customers.

On Friday evening GPL said it was still working to establish the overall cause, and some feeders, the lines that carry power to customers, had also gone offline. GPL called a social media post giving a 22 or 23 November restoration date an altered “fake” of its own notice and said it had issued no such timeframe.

GPL named an insulation failure in the panel housing the substation’s grounding transformer, equipment that helps protection systems spot and isolate faults, as a fault. On Saturday it first promised restoration by 1 p.m., then said at 12:58 p.m. that it could not meet that target.

Later in the day its deputy chief executive for strategic operations, Bharat Harjohn, said in a video that an arc, a sudden electrical discharge, had appeared under the ducting of a power cable between a transformer and the switchgear room.

In a statement at about 6:48 p.m. GPL said works at Canefield were complete, that New Amsterdam, the main town of East Berbice, had been repowered and that restoration was proceeding in phases. The accounts of the cause differ because GPL has described several faults in turn, and the utility has not explained how they relate.

Neither the government nor GPL had held a news conference by Saturday evening and instead posted updates on social media.

Weeks After a Widespread Blackout

The cut follows a widespread blackout on Friday 30 October 2026, when GPL said it strongly suspected someone had deliberately interfered with a high-voltage line. In that case the utility said it had inspected the line the day before and found it clear, and GPL said it would pass any evidence of unlawful activity to the authorities.

Ali’s statement promised a full and thorough review of the circumstances behind the failure. No date has been given for the review or for publishing its findings.

A wooden house on stilts in Guyana. (File photo, unrelated to the outage)

What It Means for Residents and Visitors

GPL has said restoration will continue in phases until every affected area is back on supply. For residents and businesses in East Berbice-Corentyne, the practical question is how soon the remaining feeders are live.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long did the Region Six outage last?

Local reports put it at more than 45 hours as of Saturday 21 November 2026. GPL began restoring supply in stages that evening.

What caused it?

GPL has pointed to damaged switchgear, a busbar fault, a cable arc and an insulation failure in a grounding transformer panel. It has not said how these relate.

What happens next?

Ali said a full and thorough review will examine the circumstances that led to the failure. No date for the review has been announced.

World.title: Dominican River Sweeps Away Truck, Kills 3
World.content:
The truck went in at a temporary ford at the site of a bridge still under construction, and the river covered it in the dark.

Disaster: Dominican Republic

A flooded river swept a pickup truck off a crossing in the east of the Dominican Republic on the night of Friday 20 November 2026, killing three men. Rescuers were still searching on Saturday for a woman who, according to people at the scene, was travelling with them.

The crossing lies on the road between the town of Hato Mayor del Rey and the district of El Puerto. Local media had begun naming some of the dead by Saturday evening, but officials had not confirmed the identities or nationalities of all three men.

Rescuers found the sunken vehicle around midday on Saturday and pulled out three bodies, although early reports on Saturday counted only two. Rescuers from Civil Defence, the national disaster-response agency, firefighters and local volunteers are searching the riverbanks downstream for a fourth occupant. Accounts gathered in the community describe her as a woman, but officials have not confirmed who she is or whether she was in the truck.

Residents told rescuers that the group had dined earlier in the El Puerto area and was driving home when the truck lost its footing. That account has come from residents rather than from officials, and the authorities have not described how the truck entered the water.

Local reports described heavy rain on Friday afternoon and night in the mountains where the river rises, but no rainfall figures were available on Saturday. Hato Mayor is a province in the east of the country, and the road to El Puerto links its capital town to a smaller district.

Who Is Searching and What Comes Next

The search continues along the river, and the identification of the three men is the next public step once forensic checks are finished. The authorities have not said whether the temporary ford will be closed or when the new bridge is due to open.

Because the bridge is still being built, drivers on this road use the temporary crossing, which the river can cover when it rises.

Frequently Asked Questions

Were any foreigners among the dead?

Officials have not confirmed nationalities.

Is the missing woman still being sought?

Yes. Civil Defence, firefighters and volunteers were searching the Casuí downstream on Saturday for a woman believed to have been in the truck.

Why was the truck on a ford and not a bridge?

A new concrete bridge is under construction at the site, and the authorities had opened a temporary ford for traffic. The river covered it after dark.

World.title: Singer Rarara Attacked at Abuja Mosque
World.content:
Nigeria: Politics

Dauda Kahutu, a Hausa-language political singer known as Rarara, was attacked by an angry crowd at the National Mosque in Abuja, Nigeria’s capital, on Friday 20 November 2026. Videos shared online, reported by Blueprint and Legit.ng, show people hitting him and tearing his clothes around the Jumu’ah, the Friday congregational prayers.

Rarara is an outspoken supporter of President Bola Tinubu. Blueprint, Legit.ng and Naija News, three Nigerian news outlets, report that he wore a cap with the president’s insignia and removed it during the attack.

Key Facts Who. Dauda Kahutu, “Rarara”, a Hausa-language political singer and supporter of President Bola Tinubu.

What. A crowd hit him and tore his clothes; security operatives escorted him away.

Where and when. National Mosque, Abuja, Nigeria’s capital, on Friday 20 November 2026, around Friday prayers.

Status. As of 21 November 2026, 23:17 GMT: injuries, arrests and motive are unconfirmed.

A pro-Tinubu singer was beaten at Abuja’s main mosque about a week after the president was reportedly booed at another, and the record on why remains thin.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Abuja (Nigeria) Email address Follow

The assault came about a week after worshippers reportedly booed Tinubu at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque in Garki, another part of Abuja, and objects were thrown at his convoy, according to TheNiche and Blueprint. Blueprint reports that protesters there chanted “Ba mayi, ba ma so”, Hausa for “We don’t want you; we don’t support you”.

Abuja, Nigeria’s capital, seen from above. (File photo)

Blueprint says the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command announced 78 arrests after that earlier incident, while Naija News says about 75. Both outlets report that Tinubu later ordered the suspects released as an act of clemency.

No official link between the two incidents has been confirmed. Nigeria holds a presidential election in 2027, and the National Mosque is the capital’s main mosque.

Blueprint reports that plain-clothes and uniformed security operatives, including police personnel, were with Rarara and tried to hold the crowd back. Naija News, citing a video seen by Daily Trust, a Nigerian newspaper, and Legit.ng describe worshippers helping to pull him away before he was escorted off for his protection.

Reports differ on whether he was entering or leaving the mosque, so the timing is best described as around the prayers. His injuries, any arrests and the immediate reason for the attack were not established in the Saturday 21 November reports, and Blueprint and Naija News say the reason has not been officially stated.

Paul Ibe, a media adviser to opposition figure Atiku Abubakar, wrote on X that despite heavy security for the prayers “worshippers could still not be protected”, Legit.ng reported. He added: “Violence against anyone, including political opponents, is unacceptable and must be condemned without reservation.”

Ibe also told the singer directly that his support for Tinubu “is your democratic right” and “should never make you a target of violence”. The message came from a critic of the government, which makes the appeal for restraint broader than one camp.

Prince Kennedy Ahanotu, convener of the Renewed Hope Alliance of Labour Party Youth Leaders, a pro-Tinubu group, spoke in an Abuja statement on Saturday 21 November, TheNiche reported. “Our restraint must never be mistaken for weakness,” he said, adding that “Nigeria must remain a country where political differences are settled through the ballot box”.

Ahanotu demanded that the Inspector-General of Police and the FCT Police Command investigate and arrest those involved. He also urged supporters to stay peaceful and avoid retaliation.

For readers in the United States, the episode matters because Nigeria is Africa’s most populous country and has a large diaspora in America. A prominent political figure attacked at the capital’s main mosque, about a week after the president was reportedly booed at another, comes ahead of the 2027 vote and raises questions about security for worshippers and visitors in Abuja.

Blueprint and Naija News reported no statement so far from the FCT Police Command or National Mosque management, so the account rests on videos and outlet reports rather than on officials. No official next step has been announced, and no date for any investigation has been given.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Rarara?

Dauda Kahutu, known as Rarara, is a Hausa-language political singer who openly backs President Tinubu.

Has anyone been arrested?

Not in the reports available on Saturday, and neither the police nor mosque management had commented. A pro-Tinubu youth group has demanded arrests.

Is the attack linked to the earlier booing of the president?

No official link has been confirmed. Outlets only note that the two incidents happened days apart at Abuja mosques.

World.title: Why the Bank of Canada Raised Rates to 2.5%
World.content:
CANADA · ANALYSIS

Canada’s central bank has raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years, and the move reaches US investors through energy prices, tariffs and the Canadian dollar. The Bank of Canada lifted its overnight rate, the rate banks charge each other for one-day loans, by 0.25 points to 2.5% on 28 October 2026.

Canada is the United States’ northern neighbour, and its central bank sets the cost of borrowing for Canadian households and companies. This analysis explains why the Bank moved, what Governor Tiff Macklem said and what comes next, building on the USA & Canada Intelligence Brief.

Free daily brief — no card needed Get every Analysis story in one morning email We build you a personalized brief around the topics you follow — free for 7 days. Love it? Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time.

Key Facts What happened The Bank of Canada raised its rate by 0.25 points to 2.5% on 28 October 2026.

Why It wants to stop high energy prices spreading to other prices as US tariffs slow growth.

Inflation Statistics Canada, the national statistics agency, put October inflation at 3.1% a year.

What to watch The next rate decision is on 9 December 2026.

Prediction markets Polymarket bets: December hold 58.5%, 0.25-point hike 40.5% (21 Nov 2026, 5:15 p.m. ET).

The Bank hiked because energy-driven inflation is proving stubborn, and it says it will now decide one meeting at a time.

How the Bank of Canada Reached a Hike

On 28 October 2026 the Bank of Canada raised its overnight rate target by 25 basis points (0.25 percentage points) to 2.5%. The overnight rate is what major banks charge each other for one-day loans, and the Bank Rate, which is the rate at which the Bank lends to financial institutions, moved to 2.75% while the deposit rate, which the Bank pays on commercial banks’ deposits with it, moved to 2.45%.

The Bank had held the rate at 2.25% before the move, and it was the first hike since July 2023. The Bank’s reasoning was that inflation is running higher, and proving more persistent, than its July report assumed.

The hike aims to reduce the risk that high energy prices spread broadly to other goods and services. Tiff Macklem, Governor of the Bank of Canada, tied the energy problem to the war in the Middle East.

He said global oil prices have increased and are expected to stay higher for longer, and the Bank’s release describes a conflict now in its eighth month with no clear resolution.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Bank of Canada Email address Follow

The Numbers That Matter

Inflation is the centre of the decision. Macklem said consumer price inflation, known as CPI, has been around 3% since April and is expected to rise to about 3½% by the end of 2026.

Statistics Canada, the national statistics agency, reported on 16 November that October 2026 CPI was 3.1% year on year, unchanged from September.

Overnight rate target: 2.5% (Bank of Canada, 28 October 2026)

CPI excluding gasoline: 2.2% in September 2026 (Macklem, 28 October 2026)

CPI excluding energy: 2.0% in October 2026, from 2.1% in September (Statistics Canada, 16 November 2026)

GDP growth: 3.3% in the second quarter of 2026, with about 2% estimated for the third (Bank of Canada)

Bank growth projection: 1% in 2026 and about 2% in 2027 and 2028

Bank inflation projection: an average of 3% in 2027, returning to 2% by mid-2028

Canadian dollar: around 71 US cents (Bank of Canada release, October 2026)

The pattern points to energy rather than broad demand. CPI excluding energy sits at 2.0%, and the Bank describes core measures as close to 2%, so the pressure is concentrated in fuel.

The labour market shows no sign of overheating, and the Bank sees some excess supply in the economy. According to Statistics Canada’s monthly Labour Force Survey of jobs, unemployment rose to 6.7% in October from 6.5% in September, while employment fell by 4,700.

The garden court inside the Bank of Canada headquarters in Ottawa (file photo).

Who Is Who in the Decision

The Bank of Canada is the country’s central bank, responsible for monetary policy and price stability. It is led by Governor Tiff Macklem, whose term ends on 2 June 2027.

Macklem announced on 16 November 2026 that he will not seek a second term, and the search for a successor is under way. The new governor would take office on 3 June 2027, appointed to a seven-year term by the Bank’s Board of Directors, subject to approval by the Minister of Finance and federal Cabinet.

The Governing Council is the Bank’s decision-making body, and Macklem held the press conference with its Senior Deputy Governor, Carolyn Rogers. The federal government in Ottawa sets fiscal policy and takes part in approving the governor’s appointment, while the Bank alone sets the policy rate.

Statistics Canada publishes the inflation and jobs data that the Bank reads. The United States government is the source of the new tariffs that the Bank cites, though the sources reviewed for this analysis do not give their details.

The Stakes for US Investors and Latin America

The Canadian Dollar

The Bank of Canada put the Canadian dollar at around 71 US cents in its October 2026 release. The currency traded at about 1.43 Canadian dollars per US dollar on 21 November 2026 (RT, a financial data provider), or about 70 US cents.

The sources reviewed do not show how the currency reacted to the hike itself. It would be wrong to assume the hike alone supports the currency, since trade news and growth concerns also move it.

Trade Tension and the Trade Pact

Macklem said that developments in the Middle East and in Canada-US trade relations both “remain fluid”. The Bank’s release speaks of considerable uncertainty and cites new US tariffs and counter-tariffs that add to costs and inflation expectations.

Uncertainty over the trade pact is part of the picture, and CUSMA, the Canada-US-Mexico Agreement, is the pact that governs trade among the three countries. The sources reviewed could not confirm the status of any review of it, and the Bank’s release does not mention it.

Oil and Latin America

Macklem tied higher oil prices to the Middle East war, yet the sources reviewed hold no benchmark price for November. US investors in energy companies or Canadian firms should check current WTI and Brent quotes, the two main oil price benchmarks, before drawing conclusions.

The sources reviewed contain no figures that link this decision to Latin America. The channel to watch is global energy prices, which Macklem expects to stay high, and the Bank’s global growth forecast of 3.1% for 2026 and 3.2% for 2027 and 2028.

What Prediction Markets Say On Polymarket, a platform where users bet real money on outcomes, traders put the odds of no change at the 9 December 2026 decision at 58.5%. A 0.25-point increase stood at 40.5%, and a cut at 0.1%, on US$305,682 of volume (read 21 November 2026, 5:15 p.m. ET). These prices are bets, not polls or forecasts by the Bank. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Three Scenarios for the Next Moves

These are scenarios, not forecasts. In a stabilising scenario, energy prices ease, CPI excluding energy stays near 2.0% and the Bank pauses at 2.5%.

The Bank’s own projection fits that path, with CPI averaging 3% in 2027 and returning to 2% by mid-2028. A pause would depend on high energy costs not spreading to consumer prices more broadly, which is the risk Macklem named.

In a tightening scenario, energy costs keep passing into consumer prices and the Bank raises again. Macklem described the option in his opening statement of 28 October: “There could be a need to raise the policy rate further, but given the uncertainties, we will proceed carefully.”

A third scenario is a growth scare. If new US tariffs weigh on activity harder than expected and unemployment keeps rising from 6.7%, the case for holding would strengthen.

The Bank already expects growth to slow in the fourth quarter and projects 1% growth for 2026. This risk is therefore part of its thinking, even though it chose to raise rates.

What It Means for You

If you hold Canadian bonds, shares or a Canadian dollar position, the hike shows the Bank sees inflation as the larger risk for now. The currency was near 1.43 per US dollar on 21 November 2026 (RT), so returns in US dollars depend on asset prices and the exchange rate together.

If your business trades with Canada, the Bank’s release cites US tariffs and counter-tariffs as adding to costs and inflation expectations. Cross-border supply chains may therefore face cost pressure into 2027, a judgement that depends on how trade policy develops.

If you follow interest rates, the Bank’s stance is cautious rather than committed. It has not promised more hikes and will decide one meeting at a time, so 9 December is the next test.

The inflation problem looks narrow today, with CPI excluding energy at 2.0%. That explains why the hike came with nerves about spillover rather than a sense of a broad price surge.

What Is Not Known

The sources reviewed do not show how the Canadian dollar or Canadian bond yields reacted on 28 October. They also contain no analyst forecast for the 9 December decision.

The details of the new US tariffs and the status of the CUSMA review were not confirmed. The Bank’s own current exchange rate was not confirmed, so the market rate above comes from RT.

Benchmark oil prices for November were not found in the sources reviewed. The next governor is also unknown.

Macklem will not seek a second term, and the sources reviewed name no successor.

What to Watch

The nearest test is the next rate announcement, and the Bank has said it will take decisions one meeting at a time. The dates below come from the Bank of Canada and Statistics Canada calendars.

9 December 2026: Bank of Canada rate decision

14 December 2026: Statistics Canada November CPI

27 January 2027: rate decision with the Monetary Policy Report

3 March 2027: rate decision

28 April 2027: rate decision with the Monetary Policy Report

Watch gasoline inflation, CPI excluding energy near 2.0%, the unemployment trend from 6.7% and any news on US tariffs. The Monetary Policy Report, the Bank’s quarterly forecast document, of 27 January 2027 will update the Bank’s projections of 1% growth in 2026 and 3% average inflation in 2027.

Macklem’s term ends on 2 June 2027, and recruitment for his successor is expected to finish by spring 2027.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did the Bank of Canada raise its rate?

The Bank raised its overnight rate target by 25 basis points to 2.5% on 28 October 2026. It said inflation is higher and more persistent than in its July report, and it wants to stop high energy prices spreading to other goods and services.

What is the Bank of Canada rate now?

As of 28 October 2026 the overnight rate target is 2.5%, the Bank Rate is 2.75% and the deposit rate is 2.45%. It was the first hike since July 2023.

When is the next Bank of Canada decision?

The next rate announcement is on 9 December 2026. The following one, on 27 January 2027, comes with the Monetary Policy Report.

Will the Bank of Canada raise rates again?

Governor Tiff Macklem said there could be a need to raise the policy rate further, but the Bank will proceed carefully and decide one meeting at a time. No decision has been made, and the sources reviewed hold no analyst forecast for 9 December.

What is Canada’s inflation rate now?

Statistics Canada put October 2026 CPI at 3.1% year on year, unchanged from September. CPI excluding energy was 2.0%, and the Bank expects about 3½% by the end of 2026.

How does the hike affect the Canadian dollar and US investors?

The Bank put the Canadian dollar at around 71 US cents in its October 2026 release, and the currency traded near 1.43 per US dollar on 21 November 2026 (RT). The sources reviewed contain no data on the immediate market reaction to the hike.

World.title: Who Is Running for France’s 2027 Presidency
World.content:
FRANCE · ANALYSIS

France is heading into a crowded presidential race, and the woman leading it has already been convicted of embezzlement. Marine Le Pen of the National Rally, the conservative nationalist party, tops every poll we found ahead of the vote on 18 April 2027.

For US readers the stakes are large: France is a NATO ally, holds a seat on the UN Security Council and runs the euro area’s second-largest economy. This analysis, which follows the Paris item in the Europe Intelligence Brief, explains who is running, how the vote works and what the polls say.

Key Facts What happened France votes 18 April 2027, and Marine Le Pen leads every poll we found.

Why it matters The next president leads a NATO ally and the euro area’s second-largest economy.

The numbers Le Pen polls 30.5% to 37%, ahead of Jean-Luc Mélenchon at 17.5% to 20%.

What to watch Sponsorship deadline 12 March, first round 18 April, runoff 2 May 2027.

Prediction markets Polymarket bets give Le Pen 46.8% to win, Lisnard 17.2% (21 Nov 2026, 5:16 p.m. ET).

Le Pen leads, Mélenchon is second in most polls, and a crowded centre and right could still reshuffle the field before April.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Édouard Philippe Email address Follow

How the Vote Works

The first round is on Sunday 18 April 2027, a date set by the French cabinet on 1 July 2026. If no candidate wins an absolute majority, the top two meet in a runoff on Sunday 2 May 2027.

Each candidate needs 500 sponsorships, called parrainages, from elected officials. They must come from at least 30 départements (France’s administrative areas) or overseas territories, and no more than a tenth from any one of them.

The deadline for collecting them is 12 March 2027, according to the government’s election calendar, and the official candidate list follows on 26 March 2027 (Vie-publique, the government’s civic information site). Emmanuel Macron’s second term ends in May 2027, so the presidency is open.

Who Is in the Race

No official list exists yet. The names below are those the pollsters test, and the parties behind them.

Marine Le Pen, National Rally (RN). She announced her candidacy on 7 July 2026, the day of her appeal ruling.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, France Unbowed (LFI), the hard-left party.

Édouard Philippe, Horizons, a centre-right party and a former prime minister.

Raphaël Glucksmann, Place publique, a centre-left movement.

David Lisnard, Nouvelle Énergie, the conservative mayor of Cannes, whose polling is rising.

Dominique de Villepin, a former prime minister under President Jacques Chirac, was due to speak at the Maison de l’Amérique latine, a Paris cultural centre, at 11:00 on Friday 20 November 2026 where he was expected to set out his plans. In October he said he had passed 300 of the 500 sponsorships he needs (LCP, the parliamentary channel).

We do not know what he said on 20 November, or whether he will reach 500.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who polls second, speaking to reporters at a book fair in Paris (file photo). photo: ActuaLitté, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

The Le Pen Question

On 7 July 2026 the Paris Court of Appeal upheld her conviction in the parliamentary assistants case, which concerned the use of European Parliament funds. It set 45 months of ineligibility, 30 of them suspended, and she remains eligible to run for now.

She has appealed to the Cour de cassation, France’s highest court of appeal. The date of its ruling is unconfirmed.

What the Polls Say

Most surveys we found have Le Pen first and Mélenchon second, and these are first-round figures. Pollsters test several scenarios, so each result is a range.

Ifop, a Paris polling firm, for the broadcaster LCI: Le Pen 37%, Mélenchon 17.5%, Philippe 15%.

Cluster17, another French polling firm, 9–10 November 2026, 1,164 people: Le Pen 30.5%, Mélenchon 20%, Philippe 13.5%, Glucksmann 11%, Lisnard 10%.

The Ifop-Fiducial wave of 18 November also pointed to a Le Pen–Mélenchon runoff in its most likely scenario, but we could not confirm its figures. Head-to-head runoff polls, the numbers that matter most for investors, were not confirmed either.

What Prediction Markets Say On Polymarket, where users bet real money on outcomes, the market on the next French president priced Le Pen at 46.8%, David Lisnard at 17.2% and Mélenchon at 14.5%, on US$181 million traded (read 21 November 2026, 5:16 p.m. ET). A separate Polymarket market on who will make the ballot put Mélenchon at 96.7% and Le Pen at 92.5%. These prices are bets, not polls. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Three Scenarios, Not Forecasts

In the first, the polls hold and Le Pen meets Mélenchon in the runoff. Markets would face a clear contest, and the winner’s budget plans would matter more than the name.

In the second, the centre-right consolidates behind one name, as Lisnard’s rise suggests it might. In the third, the Cour de cassation bars Le Pen before April, and the race loses its poll leader.

What It Means for You

For US readers, France shapes Europe’s line on Ukraine and trade, so the next president’s platform is worth reading once manifestos appear. We did not research any candidate’s stance on NATO, Ukraine or trade.

For holders of French assets, a candidate’s budget plan will tell you more than the first-round ranking. The runoff matchup is the marker to follow.

What Is Not Known

We do not know the date of the Cour de cassation ruling, the final list of candidates or the runoff polling. We also did not research bond spreads, credit ratings or market reactions to the polls.

What to Watch

12 March 2027: deadline for sponsorships.

26 March 2027: official list of candidates.

Early 2027: Cour de cassation ruling on Le Pen, date unconfirmed.

18 April 2027: first round. 2 May 2027: runoff.

Further declarations and withdrawals are likely given the size of the field. Treat any single poll with caution until runoff numbers are published.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the French presidential election in 2027?

The first round is on Sunday 18 April 2027. A runoff between the top two candidates follows on Sunday 2 May 2027 if no one wins an absolute majority.

Who is running for president of France in 2027?

Pollsters test Marine Le Pen, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, Édouard Philippe, Raphaël Glucksmann and David Lisnard, among others. No official list exists yet.

Can Marine Le Pen run in 2027?

She remains eligible for now after a 7 July 2026 appeal ruling set 45 months of ineligibility, 30 suspended. Her appeal to the Cour de cassation is pending, with no confirmed ruling date.

What do polls say about the French election?

Le Pen leads at 30.5% to 37% in first-round polls, with Mélenchon second at 17.5% to 20%. Runoff head-to-head polls were not confirmed.

How many sponsorships does a French presidential candidate need?

A candidate needs 500 sponsorships from elected officials in at least 30 départements (France’s administrative areas) or overseas territories. No more than a tenth may come from one territory.

Sources: info.gouv.fr, vie-publique.fr, lcp.fr, commission-des-sondages.fr, polymarket.com. Retrieved 21 November 2026.

World.title: Landing in San José? Your Taxi, Shuttle and Rental Car Now Leave From One Spot
World.content:
If you fly into Juan Santamaría International Airport this high season, your ride is probably waiting somewhere new. The airport has opened a ground transport center where official taxis, hotel shuttles and rental car transfers all pick up passengers. You’ll find it between the international arrivals area and the domestic terminal. Until now, those services were scattered around the outside of the building.

Aeris, the company that runs the airport, says the center began operating in November and covers about 2,800 square meters (30,100 square feet). Shuttle buses load at three covered islands, so you can wait out of the sun or rain. Cars come in one way and leave another, and marked crossings and sidewalks ring the site to keep people on foot away from traffic. There are restrooms, security cameras and controlled vehicle access.

Ricardo Hernández, executive director of Aeris, said the center improves the flow of vehicles and makes it easier for people arriving at or leaving the airport to get around. Two things the announcement does not cover are ride-hailing apps and private pickups. If a friend, relative or app driver is collecting you, agree on a meeting point before you board.

If you booked a hotel shuttle or a rental car, ask the company where its driver will be. Confirmation emails sent before November may still describe the old pickup point. The center belongs to the first phase of a westward expansion of the international terminal, a project budgeted at $62 million. Aeris has not said how much of that went to the transport center or when the next stages will open.

The same expansion produced the international arrivals hall that opened May 21, a 3,800-square-meter space (40,900 square feet) with a larger customs inspection zone, rental car counters and an outdoor meeting plaza. Give yourself a few extra minutes the first time you use the new layout, especially on a late arrival.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Dollar Slide Is Cutting Into Workers’ Pension Savings
World.content:
Workers in Costa Rica who are building retirement savings through the mandatory complementary pension system have seen part of those savings lose value this year, not because markets fell but because the dollar did. The Superintendencia de Pensiones (Supen), which regulates the pension funds, said in its November bulletin that the dollar’s slide has reduced the value in colones of the funds’ dollar-denominated investments.

According to Supen, the reference buy rate fell from about 496 colones per dollar in December 2025 to about 450 in October 2026, a drop of roughly 9%. Many of the Mandatory Pension Regime’s (ROP) foreign investments are held in dollars but reported in colones, so every dollar in those portfolios now shows up as fewer colones on workers’ account statements.

The regulator illustrated the effect with a simple example. An investment of $100 is worth 50,000 colones at an exchange rate of 500, but only 45,000 colones at 450. That is a 10% reduction in local-currency terms, even though the number of dollars has not changed. The slide has continued since October. The dollar closed Friday at 443.97 colones on Monex, the Central Bank’s wholesale foreign-exchange platform, setting a new record low for the third consecutive session. That is about 53 colones, or 10.7%, below where it started the year.

Supen stressed that savers’ total balances have not fallen by the same proportion. The impact depends on how much of each fund is invested abroad and on how its other holdings perform. The regulator noted that strong gains in international stock markets have offset part of the currency loss, citing year-on-year gains of 16.3% for the S&P 500 and 17.4% for the MSCI World index as of March 2026.

Costa Rican law allows pension operators to invest up to 50% of ROP funds in international markets, a limit Supen described as a way to diversify portfolios and reduce the concentration of risk. The cap is a ceiling, and not every operator holds that much abroad. Over longer periods the funds remain in positive territory. Supen reported nominal ROP returns through October 2026 of 10.85% over three years, 6.69% over five years and 8.63% over 10 years. The regulator cautioned that those figures do not represent any individual saver’s return this year.

Supen advised workers to review their account statements regularly and to judge fund performance over three-, five- and 10-year horizons rather than reacting to short-term swings. The pressure on the dollar has drawn heavy intervention from the Banco Central de Costa Rica. The Central Bank bought $39.65 million in stabilization operations on Friday alone to limit the decline. Through Nov. 20 it had bought $261.3 million in stabilization operations this month, the highest monthly total of 2026, ahead of the $259.1 million it bought in February.

Analysts see little short-term relief. Economist Pablo González of brokerage Mercado de Valores said that as long as dollar supply keeps outpacing weak demand, a major change in the trend is unlikely, and he noted that early December often brings additional downward pressure. That outlook is in line with earlier forecasts that the dollar would keep falling through year-end.

The stronger local currency cuts both ways. It makes dollar-priced goods cheaper in colones, but it reduces the colón income of anyone paid in dollars, from exporters to retirees living on foreign pensions, who already face some of the highest retirement costs in Latin America.

The currency hit to pension statements comes as Costa Rica also debates the future of its main public pension, with a proposed overhaul that could require 30 years of contributions instead of 25. For most savers, Supen’s message is one of patience. Pension savings are built over decades, and exchange-rate moves can reverse, as they did in 2022, when the dollar climbed from about 640 to about 691 colones in the first half of the year.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Grynspan Leads UN Race Again, but Two Veto Powers Stand in Her Way
World.content:
Costa Rican economist Rebeca Grynspan finished first again on Friday in the United Nations Security Council’s informal vote on the next Secretary-General, but the result made clear that two of the five permanent members still stand between her and the job. In the ninth closed-door straw poll since late July, Grynspan received 10 votes encouraging her candidacy, four discouraging it and one with no opinion, according to diplomats and a tally reported by the UN-focused outlet PassBlue. Two of the negative votes came from permanent members, each of which holds a veto.

The ballots were color-coded, the first time since Oct. 16 that the votes of the United States, China, Russia, France and the United Kingdom could be told apart from those of the 10 elected members. The ballots do not show which countries voted against her. The tally was a step back from early November, when Grynspan collected 12 encouraging votes and three discouraging ones on undifferentiated ballots. It also repeated the picture from the October color-coded round, when two permanent members likewise opposed her.

Even so, Grynspan remains the only candidate to reach the nine-vote threshold in every poll since September, and on Friday she was the only one backed by a majority of both the permanent and the elected members. Argentina’s Rafael Grossi, head of the International Atomic Energy Agency, came second with eight encouraging votes and six discouraging ones, three of them from permanent members. Lana Nusseibeh of the United Arab Emirates drew seven in favor and six against, also with three permanent-member objections.

Guyana’s Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett received six votes on each side. Türkiye’s Feridun Sinirlioğlu, who joined the race after the October color-coded round, received five encouraging votes and 10 discouraging ones, four of them from permanent members. PassBlue reported that every one of the eight candidates on the ballot drew at least two negative votes from permanent members.

Washington’s position remains the central question. US Ambassador Mike Waltz said Friday that the United States would welcome a Latin American candidate, in keeping with the informal practice of rotating the post among regions, while adding that Washington wants the best candidate to emerge and acknowledging there is no consensus yet. He also urged candidates with little support to withdraw so the Council can focus on a smaller field.

Diplomats cited by the development news outlet Devex said earlier this month that the United States and Russia had backed Nusseibeh, while China has signaled a preference for a Latin American without publicly endorsing anyone. Analysts have pointed to reports issued by UN Trade and Development under Grynspan that criticized the effect of Israeli policies on the Palestinian economy as a source of friction with the current US administration.

After the color-coded round in October, Grynspan said that because no formal vote had taken place, the results could not be described as vetoes, and that she would keep negotiating to broaden her support. To be recommended, a candidate needs at least nine votes on the Council and no veto from a permanent member. The 193-member General Assembly then makes the formal appointment.

Time is running short as António Guterres ends his second term on Dec. 31, and the UN Charter makes no provision for an interim leader. Reuters reported this week that UN officials are drafting contingency plans. Kirill Logvinov, a senior Russian Foreign Ministry official, said the options under discussion include temporarily extending Guterres’ term or naming another official to fill in. Daniel Safran-Hon, a former UN official, warned that senior appointments and the budget cannot move forward without a Secretary-General in place.

Grynspan, 70, served as Costa Rica’s vice president from 1994 to 1998 and later as UN Under-Secretary-General and associate administrator of the UN Development Programme. She led the Ibero-American General Secretariat from 2014 to 2021 before becoming the first woman to head UNCTAD, a post from which she took leave to campaign.

Costa Rica announced her candidacy in October 2025 and formally nominated her on March 3. If she clears the final hurdle, Grynspan would become the first woman and the first Central American to lead the United Nations.

World.title: Shakira Tickets for Costa Rica Go on Sale Monday
World.content:
Tickets for Shakira’s concert in Costa Rica go on sale Monday at noon, but only if you hold the right bank card. Everyone else has to wait until Friday, and by then you will be buying whatever the presales leave behind. The Colombian singer plays the Estadio Nacional in La Sabana, San José, on Sunday, Jan. 31, 2027, as part of her Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour. Organizers say 45,000 tickets will be available. It will be her first show in the country in almost 16 years.

The sale runs in three stages. The first presale opens Monday, Nov. 23, at noon and runs through Tuesday for holders of Visa cards from Davivienda and DAVIbank. The second opens Wednesday, Nov. 25, at 10 a.m. and runs through Thursday for holders of any Davivienda or DAVIbank card.

General sale opens Friday, Nov. 27, at 10 a.m. with any payment method. All three stages draw from the same pool of tickets, so if demand is strong early in the week there may be little left in the cheaper sections by Friday.

Prices range from 34,500 colones (about $77) to 124,500 colones (about $279). Those figures do not include service fees, which are added at checkout, so expect to pay more than the listed price.

VIP Waka Waka and La Loba, standing in front of the stage, adults only: 124,500 colones (about $279)

Platea east and west: 69,500 colones (about $156)

Balcony east and west: 64,500 colones (about $144)

VIP Las de la Intuición, standing on the field: 54,500 colones (about $122)

Sombra east and west: 44,500 colones (about $100)

South stands: 34,500 colones (about $77)

Dollar amounts use yesterday’s central bank’s rate of 446.48 colones, which, unfortunately, is when the dollar hit its third record low. This means that if you earn in dollars, the same ticket costs you more than it would have a few months ago.

However, if you find it difficult to afford at the moment and you really want to go, you can spread the cost as organizers are offering 12-month interest-free financing on ticket purchases. Children can attend from age four in every section except the two front VIP areas, which are restricted to adults. Promoter Juan Carlos Campos of ONE Costa Rica said the restriction is there for safety reasons.

Tickets are sold through publitickets.com, the only platform the organizers have named. Buy there and nowhere else, because a ticket from a reseller or a social media seller may not get you through the gate. Plan to arrive early on the day. An entertainment area outside the stadium will open at noon, with sponsor activities and stalls run by women-owned businesses.

If you miss out, there is a slim chance of a second night. Campos said the producers want to add another date but have not been able to confirm one because of the singer’s schedule.

World.title: Nearly 7 in 10 in Costa Rica Say Tourism Prices Are Driving Locals Out
World.content:
Nearly seven in 10 people in Costa Rica believe rising prices in tourist areas have forced local residents to move away, according to a national survey that also found crime is now seen as the biggest problem facing tourism.

The National Survey on Tourism in Costa Rica 2026, carried out by the Institute of Social Studies in Population (Idespo) at the Universidad Nacional (UNA), found that 68.6% of respondents said the displacement of residents by higher prices happens a lot in tourist areas. Another 71.4% said luxury housing is prioritized over affordable housing, and 75.2% said the profits from tourism benefit some sectors more than others.

The survey also points to unease about who shapes life in tourism towns. Six in 10 respondents, 60.3%, said tourism develops without taking the views of local communities into account, and 47.8% said foreigners have more influence in those communities than the people who live there. A further 41.7% said hotel and residential development has made basic public services worse.

Trust in oversight is low. Some 59.7% said authorities handle complaints about legal violations with little or no effectiveness. More than half of respondents, 52.9%, said they were unfamiliar with the work of the National Environmental Technical Secretariat (Setena), the agency that reviews the environmental impact of development projects, and 62% said the same of the Environmental Administrative Tribunal.

Asked to name the main problems of tourism in Costa Rica, 37.7% pointed to crime and insecurity, well ahead of the cost of travel at 17.6%. The deterioration of San José and the greater metropolitan area followed at 10.2%, then road conditions at 8.2% and pollution at 6.5%. The result contrasts with an international risk map released this week that ranked Costa Rica among the 10 safest countries to visit in 2027.

None of that has stopped people from traveling at home. Seven in 10 respondents, 69.8%, said they had taken a trip inside the country in the past two years, staying an average of three nights, and 75.7% of those travelers went by private car. Guanacaste was the preferred destination for 45.6%, followed by Puntarenas at 19.2% and Limón at 16%, and beaches were named as the main draw by 56.4%.

Budgets are tight. Some 44.2% said they spend less than 50,000 colones (about $112) per person per day on domestic trips, and nearly three-quarters spend less than 100,000 colones (about $224). Price was the most cited factor in choosing lodging, at 44.1%, in a place that has become Latin America’s priciest place to retire as the dollar hits a record low.

Views on where the industry is heading are mixed. Only 34.5% said Costa Rica has improved as a destination for domestic travelers, while 41.6% said it has improved for foreign visitors. Idespo interviewed 899 adults by cell phone between June 3 and 11, including Costa Ricans and foreign residents who have lived here for at least two years. The survey has a margin of error of 3.3 percentage points at a 95% confidence level.

The research team identified three challenges from the results. They are narrowing the gap between what Costa Rica offers domestic and foreign tourists, strengthening environmental oversight, and giving communities an effective say in decisions about local development.

World.title: Expect Intense Heat and Almost No Rain in Costa Rica This Weekend
World.content:
Plan for heat this weekend. Costa Rica stays dry and sunny through Sunday, and the breeze that has kept things bearable is about to drop off. Saturday’s highs will reach 35.5°C (96°F), according to the National Meteorological Institute (IMN). Skies will be clear to partly cloudy across the country, with the odd gust near the mountain ranges early in the day.

If you are in the South Pacific, you are the exception: sea breezes pushing toward the mountains give that region the only chance of rain on Saturday. The bigger change is the wind. The trade winds that have been blowing over Guanacaste and the Central Valley will go through a weak spell this weekend, the IMN says. With less air moving, it will feel hotter and stickier than the thermometer suggests.

That matters if you are spending the day outside. Drink water before you feel thirsty, find shade around midday, and don’t leave children or pets in a parked car, even for a few minutes. Rain is not coming back in any real way. The IMN’s weekend outlook allows for scattered afternoon showers in the western Central Valley and the Central Pacific, and more often in the South Pacific. On the Caribbean side and in the Northern Zone, any rain should be brief and fall in the morning.

For most beach plans, that means good conditions. If you are headed to Limón or the Northern Zone, do your outdoor activities after the morning showers pass. This is what the second half of November normally looks like, as the dry season takes hold across much of the country. What is not normal is how hot the month has been.

The IMN counted more than 23 record highs in the first 11 days of November alone, with readings near 37°C (99°F) in the North Pacific. The institute links the heat to thinner cloud cover, El Niño and warmer seas. It is not expected to ease soon. The IMN projects above-normal temperatures nationwide through January, running 1.5 to 2°C (2.7 to 3.6°F) over the average in the Pacific regions and the Central Valley.

With little rain ahead and months of dry season still to come, water is worth saving now. Short showers and fixing a dripping tap make a difference when supplies run low later in the season.

World.title: A Slow Earthquake Equal to Magnitude 6.4 Happened Off Osa and Nobody Felt It
World.content:
A slow-motion earthquake with the energy of a magnitude 6.4 tremor took place off Costa Rica’s Osa Peninsula in Octobe and no one on land felt a thing. The Volcanological and Seismological Observatory of Costa Rica (Ovsicori), part of the National University, detected the episode offshore of southern Osa, where the Cocos Plate meets the Panama Microplate. Its findings appear in a preliminary report updated on November 17.

In a slow earthquake, the strain stored between two plates escapes little by little across days or weeks rather than in one violent break. Because nothing shakes, only instruments that track ground position down to the millimeter can pick it up. Those instruments showed the observatory’s satellite positioning station in Puerto Jiménez sliding about 4.2 centimeters (1.7 inches) to the southwest over the month. Deeper down, Ovsicori’s model puts the largest slip between the two plates at roughly 13 centimeters (5.1 inches).

For comparison, the two plates normally close on each other at around 8 centimeters (3.1 inches) a year, as the Cocos Plate dives beneath the Panama Microplate. Ovsicori seismologist Cyril Müller stressed that the 6.4 figure measures the tectonic movement added up over the whole process and does not mean a quake of that size struck.

This is not the first such episode in the area. The observatory recorded slow slip in the same offshore area in 2018 and again in 2022, and both years brought a second episode, five months after the first in 2018 and two months after in 2022. The second 2022 episode covered more ground, spreading into a neighboring area to the northwest.

Since October’s slip sits in much the same place as the opening episodes of those earlier sequences, researchers consider a second episode possible in the coming months, though the report says the data cannot yet show whether, when or how far it would spread.

The report makes no forecast of a conventional earthquake and it neither claims the October episode will set one off nor estimates any rise in the odds. Studies published in 2023 and 2025 suggest slow slip can redistribute stress onto neighboring parts of a fault, a mechanism scientists are still working to understand.

The monitoring matters because parts of the plate boundary keep building up strain, among them the zone tied to the magnitude 7.4 Osa earthquake of 1983. Ovsicori will keep reviewing its station data for signs of a new episode or a spread to the northwest and will continue tracking ground deformation and seismic activity in the region.

The finding comes in a year when more earthquakes have been felt. Ovsicori data show felt quakes averaged 12 a month from January through April and 25 a month from May through October. The observatory’s researchers said the year’s activity shows nothing anomalous compared with recent years.

Costa Rica sits on one of the most active plate boundaries in the Americas, and strong earthquakes can occur at any time. Emergency authorities recommend keeping water, food, a flashlight and important documents within reach and agreeing on a meeting point with the people you live with.

World.title: Three Salvadoran Soldiers Die in Haiti Explosives Accident
World.content:
Three Salvadoran soldiers have died after an accidental explosion at a military camp in Haiti, El Salvador’s Armed Forces said yesterday. They are the first confirmed deaths since President Nayib Bukele sent troops to the Caribbean nation a month ago. Two soldiers died at the scene while handling explosive material, the Armed Forces said in a statement and two others were wounded.

Hours later, the military reported that one of the wounded had died in a hospital in the Dominican Republic, where he had been flown for treatment. The fourth soldier is out of danger, the Armed Forces said. The military has not identified the dead. It has not said where in Haiti the blast happened, when it occurred or what type of explosives were involved.

Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé offered his condolences to the Salvadoran government. The United States Embassy in San Salvador also expressed its condolences on X to the soldiers’ families and to the Salvadoran people. Bukele ordered more than 2,000 troops into Haiti after four Salvadoran airmen went missing in a gang attack in Port-au-Prince on October 18. The four were serving with the Gang Suppression Force, a United Nations-backed international mission.

The new deployment operates separately from that force. What began as a search for the missing airmen has since widened into a broader offensive against the armed groups that control much of the Haitian capital. Salvadoran troops have destroyed facilities belonging to two gangs and helped drive armed groups out of a soccer stadium in Port-au-Prince. On Thursday, Bukele said his soldiers were teaching Haiti’s gangs a lesson.

The president has said he will withdraw the troops once the four airmen are rescued. However, El Salvador and Haiti have signed a cooperation agreement that could extend the Salvadoran military presence. Its terms have not been made public. Haitian authorities have welcomed the deployment. They have long asked for more outside help against the gangs.

Bukele built his regional profile on a hard-line crackdown that dismantled the gangs once dominant in El Salvador. The Haiti operation is the first time he has applied that approach outside his own country. The four airmen remain missing.

World.title: International News: About 250 migrants enter Mexico in caravan hoping to reach U.S.
World.content:
International News: About 250 migrants enter Mexico in caravan hoping to reach U.S.

By Zoila Palma: A caravan of approximately 250 migrants, mostly from Central America, entered Mexico on Friday after crossing the border from Guatemala as they continued their journey toward the United States.

The group, made up largely of young men and families with children, crossed a border bridge into Tapachula carrying their belongings on their backs. They displayed a banner reading “God with us” and were not stopped by Mexican authorities.

Several migrants told AFP that they had previously lived in the United States but were deported during Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations.

Among them was 31-year-old Honduran national Saba Najera, who said she was determined to reach Houston to reunite with her newborn daughter. She described her deportation as painful but said the separation had strengthened her resolve to make the journey again.

The latest movement comes as several migrant caravans have entered Mexico hoping to reach the United States, despite warnings from President Donald Trump.

Mexican security forces have blocked some larger groups, while others have dispersed after immigration officials offered them the opportunity to seek asylum in Mexico.

World.title: Motorcycle collides with Sarita ice cream truck in Independence Village
World.content:
Motorcycle collides with Sarita ice cream truck in Independence Village

By Belize Live News Staff: A motorcycle and a Sarita ice cream truck were involved in a collision in Independence Village on Friday evening.

Reports are that the accident happened around 6:47pm on November 20 on Faden Street.

According to initial information, the driver of the motorcycle picked himself up after the collision and walked away from the scene.

The extent of any injuries is not known at this time. There are no reports of injuries to anyone in the truck.

The cause of the collision has not been established.

Breaking Belize News will provide more information as it becomes available.

World.title: Galen University offers free application opportunity at Christmas Extravaganza in Belize City
World.content:
By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belizeans planning to pursue higher education in 2027 will have an opportunity to save on university application fees when Galen University participates in the Belize Chamber of Commerce and Industry’s Christmas Extravaganza.

The event is scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026, at the Belize City Civic Center, from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Galen University is inviting prospective students to visit its booth and apply for the Spring 2027 semester, with the university waiving the application fee for those who apply at the event and bring their supporting documents.

The initiative provides an opportunity for students preparing to continue their education, working professionals considering additional qualifications and individuals interested in returning to school.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to bring their supporting documents to take advantage of the offer.

In addition to accepting applications, Galen University’s presence at the Christmas Extravaganza will give visitors an opportunity to learn more about the institution and its educational opportunities.

The event is organized by the Belize Chamber of Commerce and Industry and will take place at the Belize City Civic Center.

For additional information about admissions, interested persons can visit www.galen.edu.bz, email [email protected] or call 614-6415.

World.title: Enrique Martinez and Sons announces Black Friday Super Sale with up to 20% off and free gifts
World.content:
Enrique Martinez and Sons announces Black Friday Super Sale with up to 20% off and free gifts
