World.title: Russian cargo ship on fire in Gulf of Finland after reported drone strike
World.content:
A fire broke out aboard the Russian dry cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday morning, with Russian officials claiming the vessel was struck by two drones.

Finland's prime minister has confirmed on X the Sparta II had been hit by drones, adding Ukraine has the "right to fight back" against the aggressor.

According to the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA), explosions which rocked the vessel took place when it was in Estonia's economic zone but within the area of ​​responsibility of the St. Petersburg Maritime Rescue Center and in shipping lanes open to international vessels, with the vessel later drifting north into Finnish waters.

Finland's Border Guard is leading rescue and spill preparation and said in a statement that the damaged vessel, which is on fire, drifted from international waters into Finnish territorial waters in the eastern Gulf of Finland, adding that the situation poses no danger to other shipping. The border guard is coordinating maritime rescue and potential oil-spill response with domestic and international authorities.

Finland's Ministry of Defense had earlier said the attack took place in international waters, left the ship damaged, and prompted Finland to notify its allies as border guard units headed to the scene.

On X, Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo wrote: "War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity. The Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor".

Russian arms transport ship Sparta II on fire on the Gulf of Finland. It was most likely struck by Ukrainian drones or missiles. https://t.co/WYkr6yJqd7 — Petri Mäkelä (@pmakela1) November 21, 2026

Estonia's Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) aeronautical and maritime rescue coordination center first received word of a fire and preliminary reports of explosions aboard the Russian-owned dry cargo ship Sparta II at 9:35 a.m. on Saturday. According to a PPA statement cited by Finnish public broadcaster Yle, the vessel had departed from St. Petersburg.

PPA duty officer Andres Tiik said Estonian authorities are monitoring the incident alongside Finnish counterparts and will respond if Russia requests international assistance. No marine pollution has been reported so far.

When the incident began, the Sparta II was operating in an international shipping lane 11 nautical miles north of Estonia's Vaindloo Island, inside the St. Petersburg maritime rescue coordination zone. Current data indicates the vessel drifted out of Estonia's exclusive economic zone at around 10 a.m.

Ukrainian military intelligence has classified the Sparta II as a vessel that has carried weapons and military equipment, and the ship is on the U.S. sanctions list.

The Sparta II, the Russian cargo vessel which caught fire on the Gulf of Finland Saturday. Source: SCANPIX/REUTERS

Earlier, Leningrad Oblast Governor Alexander Drozdenko claimed on Telegram that two drones struck the Kaliningrad-bound cargo ship in neutral waters three nautical miles from Russia's border, and that crew evacuation was underway while damage was being assessed.

Meanwhile, the Finnish Defense Forces imposed temporary sea and air traffic restrictions in the Gulf of Finland twice on Saturday, Yle reported — first from early morning until 7:43 a.m., then again around 9:30 a.m. Finland's General Staff said the reimposed restrictions were not tied to a single acute threat, but were a precaution against Ukrainian drones straying into NATO airspace, a risk that also prompted an early-morning EE-ALARM warning in northeastern Estonia.

Russian media reported that more than 60 drones were shot down overnight in Leningrad Oblast.

PPA spokesperson: Ship's bridge was on fire before it drifted into Finnish waters

In an afternoon update, Estonian PPA duty officer Andres Tiik said explosions set the Sparta II's bridge on fire before the vessel drifted north into Finnish territorial waters, where Finnish authorities have likely evacuated the crew. Tiik added that the PPA raised the readiness level of its rescue helicopter, though Russia's St. Petersburg maritime rescue coordination center never requested assistance.

The Finnish Border Guard also said it has been in contact with Russian maritime rescue authorities as part of its response. Meanwhile, Russian media updated its overnight toll to report that 80 drones were shot down in Leningrad Oblast.

Editor's note: This piece has been updated to include confirmation from Finnish authorities that the vessel drifted into Finnish territorial waters, comments from Prime Minister Petteri Orpo, and background on the Sparta II and its sanctions status, and to include updates on the emergency response to the incident.

World.title: Gallery: Estonia's largest solar park opens in Risti with 340,000 panels
World.content:
Estonia's largest solar park has opened in Risti, Lääne County, with enough capacity to cover the annual electricity consumption of roughly 90,000 households.

Built by renewable energy firm Sunly at a cost of €125 million, the 244-megawatt site is set to expand into a hybrid energy hub with battery storage, wind and a data center.

Spanning 270 hectares with 340,000 panels, the facility is the second largest in the Baltic states. Sunly CEO Priit Lepasepp noted that 90,000 households equals the combined populations of Tartu, Narva and Pärnu.

A substation is already complete and battery park construction has begun with Rolls-Royce, while a wind farm and major data center are also in the pipeline. Lääne-Nigula Mayor Janno Randmaa welcomed the local community payments and future tech jobs tied to the project.

Rapid solar expansion in Estonia has pushed installed solar capacity past annual peak demand, driving summer midday power prices to zero. Lepasepp said standalone solar or wind farms are no longer viable, noting Sunly will earn revenue from frequency regulation and selling stored battery power when gas-fired electricity is expensive.

State-owned rival Enefit has paused standalone solar projects, with Baltic business development head Johann-Gustav Lend agreeing that future sites require hybrid setups paired with large on-site power consumers.

World.title: Stefan Vaaks one assist shy of triple-double in Illinois NCAA blowout
World.content:
Estonian guard Stefan Vaaks finished one assist short of a triple-double on Friday as 10th-ranked Illinois routed Eastern Illinois 114-52 in NCAA men's basketball.

Vaaks tied his season high with 20 points and grabbed an NCAA career-best 11 rebounds while the Fighting Illini tied a Big Ten Conference record with 23 three-pointers.

Building a 68-18 halftime lead, Vaaks shot 3 of 5 inside the arc, 4 of 8 from three-point range, and 2 of 2 from the free-throw line while adding a season-high nine assists alongside two turnovers and two fouls. Ethan Brown led Illinois with 26 points and Tomislav Ivišić added 22, while Jalen Calloway scored 17 for Eastern Illinois. Illinois improved to 5-1 overall and 4-0 at home ahead of Monday's home matchup against winless Winthrop.

Elsewhere for Estonians in U.S. college basketbal, Erik Makke scored 18 points with seven assists and two rebounds as Stephen F. Austin beat Indiana State 86-76. Kätlin Kangur went scoreless in 24 minutes with two rebounds and one assist as Idaho defeated Nevada 67-47 on the road.

World.title: New sand and gravel quarry blocked at Männiku quarry due to EDF training area
World.content:
A mining firm has been denied permission to extract sand at a new site in a quarry zone near Tallinn, because the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) needs the land.

Geological surveys at the site in Männiku, just south of the capital, have wrapped up, and mining company AS Silikaat has been denied permission to go ahead with quarrying.

The Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) wants the newly surveyed sand deposits registered as passive rather than active reserves, to protect training routes and safety zones.

Located in Männiku village in Harju County's Saku Municipality, the area has seen sand extraction for more than 70 years alongside an EDF training area spanning over 1,000 hectares and which encompasses the Männiku quarry.

Silikaat received an Environmental Board permit late last year to conduct geological surveys on 13 hectares of defense land — including up to 70 boreholes — with RKIK approval to assess sand volume and quality.

However, RKIK portfolio manager for training areas Elari Kalmaru said mining and quarrying cannot go ahead there now because the surveyed blocks sit directly on the Männiku training area, including a key transit route between sections of the site and firing danger zones.

"Whenever we review such permitting procedures, our only criterion is that the training area can continue operating in the same way it has up to now, and in this case that is not possible," Kalmaru told Vikerraadio.

The RKIK has proposed registering the deposits as passive reserves — meaning the sand's presence is noted, but cannot be extracted while the EDF uses the site for training — rather than active reserves sought by Silikaat for near-term mining. Kalmaru rejected the suggestion that the survey was pointless, saying passive registration remains valid, though mining would require offsetting changes elsewhere, such as expanded training facilities to accommodate growing conscript numbers.

Silikaat Group CEO Priit Poks declined to provide comment on the matter to ERR. Aside from Männiku, the company mines sand at the Tika II quarry in Rapla County and the Pihlaka quarry in Viljandi County.

World.title: RIA: Scammers create fake online stores to steal banking data
World.content:
Scammers are creating websites that imitate well-known brands and can appear highly convincing. Their goal is to lure shoppers to fraudulent pages and gain access to their banking information, the Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) warns.

With Black Friday and the holiday shopping season approaching, many online retailers have already launched sales campaigns, creating opportunities for fraudsters to target unsuspecting consumers.

As an example, RIA highlighted a fake website that imitated the online store of retailer JYSK in a Facebook post.

"A fake site can often be identified by its web address. Users should carefully read the URL and compare it with the official online store's address. Even a single different letter may indicate a fraudulent website," the agency warned.

"Consumers should also be cautious when clicking on s on social media. Alongside promotions from legitimate online stores, there may be ads leading to fake sites created to obtain banking card details and other sensitive information," RIA said.

If a website appears suspicious, RIA asks people to report it to cert@cert.ee. Specialists will investigate the information and, if necessary, block the site to help prevent further fraud.

Tips in English language for safe online shopping are available on RIA's website.

World.title: Külli Kraner: Minimum wage should rise no faster than prices
World.content:
Employers and labor unions are currently negotiating next year's minimum wage. Their responsibility is to agree on an increase that businesses and the broader economy can sustain. In the accommodation and food service sector, that means the minimum wage should not rise faster than inflation in 2027, writes Külli Kraner.

While the minimum wage across the economy equals about 43 percent of the average wage, in accommodation and food services it already amounts to roughly three-quarters of the sector's median wage. As a result, it is no longer merely the lowest permissible wage but effectively sets the pay level for the entire sector.

The purpose of the minimum wage is to protect the lowest-paid workers. When it approaches the standard wage level, the link between pay and skills, experience and responsibility begins to disappear, leaving employers with fewer opportunities to reward competence and experience through higher pay.

"Businesses have been unable to raise prices at the same pace because customers' purchasing power has declined."

If the minimum wage were to increase by, for example, 5.7 percent next year and reach €1,000 per month, the gap between the pay of an experienced chef or waiter and that of an entry-level assistant would narrow even further. Preserving that gap requires raising the wages of experienced employees as well, pushing up the entire pay structure. In Tallinn, where wages are higher, such increases are easier to absorb, but the minimum wage is the same throughout Estonia.

Rising costs with limited room for price increases

Over the past three years, costs for hotels and restaurants have risen faster than revenues. Wages per employee have increased by nearly 18 percent in restaurants and nearly 15 percent in hotels. Food, beverages, energy and services have become more expensive, while value-added tax rates for both accommodation and food services have increased.

Businesses have been unable to raise prices at the same pace because customers' purchasing power has declined. Restaurants are selling less than they did three years ago, and hotel room rates in Tallinn have remained nearly unchanged.

Labor costs are the largest expense in the sector. A survey conducted among members of the Estonian Hotel and Restaurant Association this fall found that nearly half of businesses would consider reducing staff numbers or working hours if the minimum wage rises rapidly.

Entry-level jobs disappear first

Hotels and restaurants provide many people's first jobs. Employees often enter the sector while studying, after graduation or while seeking a new career, frequently without training or experience. Skills are learned on the job, and employers invest both time and money in that process.

The minimum wage is the entry-level wage for these workers. If it rises faster than company revenues allow, employers will prefer experienced workers who can start immediately. Beginners will have fewer opportunities, and the jobs that launch so many careers will be the first to disappear.

"A reduction in value-added tax would also help the food service sector."

Minimum wage increases also affect competition in the accommodation market. Hotels pay wages and employment taxes for receptionists, cleaners and cooks. Short-term rental providers often have no formally employed workers, even though many operate at a scale comparable to a small accommodation business, with multiple apartments, daily cleaning, linen services and key handovers.

The work is still being done. The question is whether labor taxes are being paid on it. Minimum wage increases only raise costs for businesses that formally employ workers, and with every increase the gap widens between companies that comply with the rules and those that do not.

We do not want to restrict short-term rentals. We want equal rules for providers of the same service.

Tourism organizations have proposed a solution to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications, arguing that little has been done on the issue for years. One element would distinguish between occasional home-sharing and commercial activity. If someone rents out their home occasionally, it is part of the sharing economy. If a property is rented for more than 60 nights per year or if more than one apartment is rented out, it should be treated as a business, registered and subject to the same requirements as other accommodation providers.

Sustainable wage growth depends on what customers can afford

Workers' financial well-being matters. In terms of purchasing power, Estonia's minimum wage was the lowest in the European Union at the beginning of 2026. But purchasing power depends not only on wages, but also on taxes and prices. If the tax-free income threshold increases, workers take home more pay without increasing employers' costs.

A reduction in value-added tax would also help the food service sector. A large share of restaurant prices reflects labor costs, and because VAT is applied to the full price, labor is effectively taxed as well.

Estonia's VAT rate for food services is 24 percent, while most European countries apply lower rates. In Finland it is 13.5 percent, and Germany cut its rate to seven percent at the beginning of 2026. If Estonia reduced the rate to 13 percent, businesses could raise wages without cutting jobs, while customers would face less price pressure, helping to sustain demand.

We want our employees' wages to increase. Sustainable wage growth, however, comes from workers' skills and from what customers are willing to pay for services. A minimum wage increase raises everyone's wages equally, regardless of what a business can earn.

From the perspective of the hotel and restaurant sector, therefore, the minimum wage increase in 2027 should not exceed inflation. Flexible working-hour rates should be decoupled from the minimum wage, and policymakers should recognize that in some sectors the minimum wage is already close to the standard wage level. Measures such as increasing tax-free income and adjusting VAT spread the burden more broadly and do not threaten jobs as directly as rapid minimum wage increases.

Külli Kraner is chief executive officer of the Estonian Hotel and Restaurant Association, which is a member of the Estonian Employers' Confederation.

World.title: Data center boom in Estonia: Who is building, where and at what cost
World.content:
Developers have filed grid connection requests for 2,900 megawatts of data centers in Estonia, nearly double the country's current peak electricity demand of 1,700 megawatts.

While only one major facility operates today, billions of euros in proposed artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud campuses across western and northern Estonia could reshape both power prices and grid stability.

National grid operator Elering has received seven connection applications totaling 2,900 megawatts. By contrast, Estonia's sole existing next-generation facility — Greenergy Data Centers in Hüüru, near Tallinn — currently draws just 2 megawatts, though it plans to scale to 200 megawatts by early 2028.

Lääne County emerges as the main hotspot

Most of the proposed capacity is clustered along high-voltage transmission lines in western Estonia's Lääne-Nigula and Lääneranna municipalities, particularly around the small towns of Risti and Lihula.

In Risti, Estonian renewable energy firm Sunly and Norway's Magnora Data Center are jointly developing a campus designed to connect at 180 megawatts initially and expand up to 400 megawatts if the local substation is upgraded — a buildout estimated at €1.7 billion.

AI-generated illustration of a potential data center in Estonia. Source: ChatGPT

Domestic renewables developer Evecon is also pursuing a 41-hectare industrial park next to Risti featuring two data center buildings and up to nine industrial facilities, projected to create around 150 jobs. A third developer, Sinfra, has initiated planning for a center in nearby Jõgisoo village, while a fourth unnamed company has made early-stage inquiries.

Lääne-Nigula Mayor Janno Randmaa said Sunly's project is furthest along because the company is pairing the campus with a local solar park to cover its power demand. For the others, he said, municipalities still lack clarity on energy and cooling-water needs.

"These applications come in fairly quickly, and at times the question is whether this is a serious trend or a passing fad, and how much of it will actually become reality," Randmaa said, noting that local residents have so far focused on practical questions around water use and noise rather than outright opposition.

Thirty kilometers south in Lihula, Evecon has entered detailed planning for a 100-megawatt data center, while Norwegian group Northern Europe Energy Group has unveiled plans for a 136-hectare site targeting 100 MVA initially and up to 1,100 MVA via a nearby 330-kilovolt line. Project manager Janis Paeglitis said the venture remains at an early feasibility stage, with final scale and investment yet to be set.

Evecon CEO Karl-Joonatan Kvell said pairing data centers with generation is a logical business model: steady, long-term power buyers make new renewable and storage projects far easier to finance.

Concept rendering of Sunly and Magnora's planned Risti data center campus. Source: Sunly

Billions eyed in northern and southwestern Estonia

Plans extend beyond the west coast. In Tapa, domestic firms Sustainable Investments and Sinfra, alongside Finland's Ehrnrooth business family, are weighing an investment of up to €3.4 billion.

Evecon has also received design conditions for a project in Varja, Lüganuse Municipality, in northeastern Estonia, and applied for a 100-megawatt facility near Kilingi-Nõmme in Saarde Municipality — a proposal that sparked a local council dispute over municipal jurisdiction and triggered the collapse of the local governing coalition.

State backs local AI compute, warns against 'closed' campuses

The Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs considers domestic data centers essential for running critical public and private digital services and safeguarding sensitive state data.

"Artificial intelligence infrastructure technologies and their security are still in an early stage of development, which is why it is safer to keep servers close to home," the ministry said.

Estonia has joined the European Commission's AI gigafactory joint procurement, pledging €20 million over 2028–2032 to purchase high-performance computing capacity on condition that one branch of the facility is located in Estonia. However, the ministry warned that closed campuses built solely for a single foreign tech giant's global operations bring minimal economic benefit compared to centers serving Estonian businesses, researchers and public institutions.

Concept rendering of the Norwegian developer's planned Lihula campus. Source: Screenshot from Northern Europe Energy Group's website.

What 2,900 megawatts could mean for electricity bills

If even a fraction of the 2,900 megawatts is built without matching new power generation, Estonia will rely more heavily on electricity imports from Finland — where a parallel data center boom is already poised to push Nordic exchange prices higher, according to Baltic Energy Partners board member Marko Allikson.

Still, Allikson noted that actual data center demand in Estonia stands at just 2 megawatts today and may barely top 20 megawatts next year, remaining marginal in the short term. Over the longer run, he said, data centers could unlock subsidy-free power plants through long-term power purchase agreements — pointing to Finland, where Google's off-take deal helped utility Fortum justify extending the lifespan of its Loviisa nuclear reactors.

Energy expert Arvi Hamburg added that higher overall consumption could reduce per-kilowatt-hour grid and frequency-reserve fees for ordinary consumers — unless developers connect via direct lines that bypass the public network.

Hamburg also warned that Estonia's small grid faces technical risks from rapid load swings at large server farms, urging authorities to site facilities strictly near major backbone substations and require operators to help keep the system balanced.

In an interview given to ERR's science portal Novaator, Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) professor Mart Landsberg explained the impact of data centers on the electricity system in more detail, here.

World.title: Artist Raivo Järvi's cheerful drawings masked a life marked by personal tragedy
World.content:
Generations of Estonians grew up admiring the comics and illustrations of artist Raivo Järvi, better known as onu Raivo (uncle Raivo). Over the course of two decades, he also became a familiar radio voice and later spent nearly a decade in politics.

A new exhibition opening Friday at the Tartu Art Museum, "Pildi ees ja pildi sees" ("In Front of the Picture and Inside the Picture"), sheds light on lesser-known aspects of Järvi's life and work, revealing a more complex and at times deeply tragic personal story.

Born in Pärnu in 1954 as the only child of a violinist father and a ballet master mother, Järvi showed an interest in art from an early age. According to family recollections, he decided to become an artist at around age five after his mother warned him that an actor's life was difficult.

While artists are often associated with bohemian lifestyles, Järvi was known for discipline and meticulousness. From earning top marks in school to refining artistic motifs throughout his career, precision was one of his defining characteristics.

Uus kogumik tõi taas lugejate ette Raivo Järvi 1980. aastate koomiksid Autor/allikas: ERR

"It is a very interesting combination for an artist: meticulousness, a love of order and cleanliness. If you look at his graphic works, you see that same precision and stylistic purity," said his son, Richard-Erik Järvi.

Järvi's television career began almost by accident in 1977 while he was studying graphic arts at the Estonian State Art Institute (ERKI). When singer Voldemar Kuslap was unexpectedly unable to appear on the children's program "Laulujütsid," Järvi volunteered to draw with the children on air.

Over the next two decades, he became a beloved fixture of Estonian children's television, appearing in programs such as "Laupäeval koos isaga" ("Saturday With Dad"), "Kõige suurem sõber" ("The Greatest Friend") and "Jutupliiats" ("Story Pencil"). Viewers were particularly captivated by the drawings he created live on air, often completing elaborate characters before their eyes.

The 1983 children's television program "Kõige suurem sõber". Source: Heidi Maasikmets

Exhibition curator Stella Mõttus said audiences frequently wondered whether the outlines of the drawings had been prepared in advance.

"But no, he simply practiced them an enormous amount beforehand," she said.

Yet behind his public success lay significant personal hardship. Biography author Piret Kooli, who interviewed nearly 40 friends and colleagues while researching Järvi's life, said he endured profound losses. His father died when he was just ten years old. Later, he lost his first great love, dancer and actress Raili, who drowned during a film shoot under circumstances that remained unclear.

Richard-Erik Järvi said his father rarely spoke about her, but it was evident that the loss affected him deeply.

"It was the hardest period of his life," he said.

Järvi's later relationships were also troubled. His relationship with a beauty pageant princess named Signe, the mother of his son Richard-Erik, was short-lived. As a child, Richard-Erik knew little about his mother and was largely raised by his father, with invaluable help from family friend Tiia-Liis Jürgenson.

Jürgenson, whose own son was born just a week before Richard-Erik, helped care for the infant and later became a central figure in his upbringing.

"What began as a few days turned into a lifetime," she said. "For our family, it became completely natural."

Richard-Erik describes her as his guardian angel and says he often refers to her as his mother figure despite maintaining respect and gratitude toward his biological mother.

Raivo Järvi in "Pildi ees ja pildi sees". Source: Toomas Tuul

Despite his fame and productivity as an illustrator, radio host and later politician, Järvi never achieved substantial financial success. One notable example is the redesigned packaging for a popular curd snack introduced in 1996, featuring a cat illustration that became one of the most widely reproduced artworks in Estonia.

"Many people assume that cat earned him money for the rest of his life. In reality, it did not," Kooli noted.

According to those close to him, financial considerations partly motivated Järvi's decision to enter politics with the Reform Party. He served two terms in the Riigikogu, seeking financial stability for himself and his son.

A small room in an outbuilding on Faehlmanni tänav in Tallinn became his refuge when life became overwhelming. By then, his third major relationship, with an Estonia Theatre ballerina named Tatjana, had also deteriorated. Kooli believes Järvi spent much of his life searching for the love he had lost with Raili.

"He was looking for love, approval and himself," she said. "In reality, he was always looking for Raili."

Friends and family say that although Järvi maintained an upbeat public image, he often struggled privately. Kooli reflected that today he might well have been diagnosed with depression.

Despite being diagnosed with cancer, Järvi chose to keep his illness largely private. He continued working in Parliament and hosting radio programs until he was physically no longer able.

"He didn't want many people to know," his son recalled. "He had always felt the hardest way to leave was to slowly fade away in front of others."

Kooli remembered that Järvi continued broadcasting despite severe pain and diminishing strength. During his final broadcasts, medication affected his speech, leading some listeners to mistakenly assume he was intoxicated.

"Those comments were especially painful," Jürgenson said.

Raivo Järvi. Source: Ülo Josing/ERR

Fourteen years after Järvi's death, the Tartu Art Museum launched a public appeal for works to include in a retrospective exhibition. Nearly 500 pieces were identified in private collections and museums, with around 60 selected for display.

Curator Stella Mõttus said the exhibition reveals aspects of Järvi that many people never saw. While known primarily for the cheerful illustrations loved by children, some of his black-and-white graphic works are dark, unsettling and even apocalyptic.

"His life wasn't exactly rosy either," she said.

Richard-Erik Järvi, however, believes the works convey not only sadness and trauma but also resilience.

"We've talked about the tragic moments," he said, "but he always tried to remain positive."

World.title: Little Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
World.content:
CAPE CANAVERAL, Florida: A pair of spacecraft slipped into orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system to unravel our littlest planet’s mountain of mysteries.

The linked robotic explorers — one European, the other Japanese — will separate from one another next month in order to map and study the scorching little planet from different altitudes. The $2 billion (1.7 billion euros) mission is known collectively as BepiColombo.

The European Space Agency announced BepiColombo’s arrival via social media. A series of thruster firings slowed the spacecraft enough to be captured by the planet’s weak gravity. But it took several anxious hours before flight controllers in Germany — 94 million miles (152 million kilometers) away — could confirm that BepiColombo had achieved orbit. Teams pored over the data streaming back; additional information was not immediately available.

BepiColombo is only the third spacecraft to visit Mercury — the sun’s closest planet and barely bigger than our moon — and the first in more than a decade.

NASA’s Mariner 10 flew past Mercury three times in the mid-1970s. The team included the late Italian mathematician Giuseppe “Bepi” Colombo, for whom this latest mission is named. NASA’s Messenger spacecraft entered orbit around Mercury in 2011 and, after running out of fuel, crashed into the planet in 2015.

Launched in 2018, BepiColombo took a slower, more roundabout route to get to Mercury, flying once past Earth, twice past Venus and six times past Mercury for gravity-guiding assists. All those loop-de-loops put more than 6 billion miles (10 billion kilometers) on the odometer. The conjoined spacecraft shed their mother ship in September for the final leg of the journey.

Lead project scientist Geraint Jones said he and others can’t wait for all the new data to start streaming down in the spring. The mission will provide the ability to compare “unprecedented measurements taken by two spacecraft at the planet at the same time,” he noted.

Once orbiting separately, the European Space Agency’s satellite and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s smaller craft will study Mercury’s dense interior and exterior magnetic field, as well as everything in between: impact craters, volcanic plains, mountain ridges and peaks jutting as high as 3 miles (4 1/2 kilometers).

The mercury at Mercury can hit more than 800 degrees (427 degrees Celsius), adding strain to electronic and engineering systems. Space agency officials want to keep the mission going for at least one Earth year — or the equivalent of four Mercury years.

“The spacecraft and its instruments need to be kept as cool as possible, which is a huge technical challenge in itself,” Jones said in an email.

Despite its relative proximity to Earth, Mercury is one of the solar system’s least explored planets. Only outer planets Uranus and Neptune have had fewer visitors — a lone Voyager 2 back in the 1980s.

World.title: Canada defense chief sees no change despite reported US military curbs
World.content:
HALIFAX, Nova Scotia: Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty said on Saturday he had seen no change in military cooperation with the United States, despite a reported Pentagon directive imposing new restrictions on defense ties between the longtime allies.

McGuinty said he had not seen a classified memo that US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reportedly circulated last week setting out constraints on military cooperation with Canada.

“I still see no daylight between what we’re doing, military to military, and otherwise,” McGuinty told Reuters on the sidelines of a security conference in Halifax.

He said the two countries’ armed forces continued working “hand in glove” on operations, including efforts to stop trafficking of cocaine, fentanyl and other illegal drugs in the Caribbean, integrated missile systems and scrambling fighter jets to respond to threats across North America.

The Washington Post reported Friday that Hegseth had issued the classified directive, citing officials familiar with the decision. The precise scope of the reported restrictions remained unclear, and the newspaper said it had not seen the memo.

The Pentagon said it was refocusing its relationship with Canada around US defense priorities.

“The Department of War is taking steps to ensure its engagements with Canada advance tangible US defense objectives and ultimately support a reinvigorated defense relationship,” chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell told AFP.

Washington was prioritizing bilateral cooperation to strengthen the defense of the Americas while supporting Canada's ability to meet its NATO commitments, Parnell said.

He said the guidance did not affect defense intelligence cooperation, the binational North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) or cooperation through NATO.

US Senator Mike Rounds, a South Dakota Republican, said defense officials had briefed him on the memo, which he described as containing no major new measures beyond steps American military officials had taken for years.

Canada's Defense Ministry said it would not speculate on media reports but stressed that defense cooperation between the two countries continued.

“Canada and the United States have a long history of defense cooperation built on a shared commitment to continental defense and protecting our collective security around the globe. This collaborative work continues,” spokesman Tony Wright said in a statement.

McGuinty said the countries' 70-year partnership under NORAD had provided an effective continental defense system and that Ottawa wanted to continue investing in and cooperating through it.

The reported Pentagon move comes amid strained relations under US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly suggested Canada should become the 51st US state, imposed tariffs on Canadian goods and criticized Ottawa's defense spending.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has rejected Trump's annexation rhetoric and called for a reassessment of the global security order, prompting Ottawa to accelerate its defense investments.

McGuinty said Canada needed to take greater responsibility for its own security, particularly in the Arctic, and was working to develop a domestic alternative to Starlink satellite communications to safeguard its sovereignty.

Canada said last year it had reached NATO's defense spending target of 2 percent of gross domestic product for the first time. The government plans to increase spending to 5 percent of GDP by 2035.

“We’ve been in a comfortable position for decades, but things have now changed,” McGuinty said.

World.title: COP31 climate talks close to final deal, says summit president
World.content:
ANTALYA, ‌Turkiye: Climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, approached a final deal on Sunday with the announcement of a new package ​that COP31 presidents Australia and Turkiye hope will achieve consensus on how to advance the fight against global warming.

“We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” COP31 President Murat Kurum told a late-night plenary session. He said the conference would reconvene later on ‌Sunday morning ‌to approve the deal.

Negotiators ran ​past ‌a ⁠Friday ​deadline, straight ⁠through Saturday and into the early hours of Sunday. Their new version of the deal text refined an earlier draft, which had been heavily criticized by some for lacking ambition because it contained no reference to ending the use of fossil fuels.

Kurum said he ⁠believed concerns around fossil fuels had ‌been addressed, as had those ‌around helping developing countries finance their adaptations ​to climate change.

The new ‌text followed intensive consultations between Australia, which is ‌leading the talks, Turkiye, which is hosting the meeting, and nearly 200 delegations from many of the world’s richest, poorest, largest and smallest nations.

Delegations have until 0300 GMT to ‌raise any objections to the deal, with a session scheduled at 0600 GMT to ⁠begin approving ⁠it.

Australia’s task, supported by Turkiye, has been to find a deal that balances the needs of nations most vulnerable to climate change with those whose economies depend on either the production or consumption of fossil fuels.

This year’s COP is the first since the UN’s environmental body confirmed that the rise in global temperature was set to blow past 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit), a threshold all countries agreed over ​a decade ago ​to try not to exceed, and beyond which extreme weather impacts intensify.

World.title: Belgium faces air traffic shutdown due to national strike Monday
World.content:
BRUSSELS, Belgium: Almost all flights are set to be canceled in Belgium on Monday after the country’s air traffic controller said its staff will take part in a national strike against government austerity measures.

Skeyes, the company responsible for air traffic control in the country, said Saturday it will be unable to provide regular services at Belgian airports and in the airspace between 7:00 am (0600 GMT) and 9:00 p.m. (2000 GMT) on November 23.

“The anticipated staffing levels will not allow the safe handling of regular air traffic to be guaranteed during this period. Skeyes is therefore obliged to temporarily suspend the services concerned,” the company said.

Belgium has seen repeated rounds of strikes in recent months against efforts by Prime Minister Bart De Wever to save 10 billion euros over the next few years in a bid to reduce the country’s high deficit.

Skeyes said essential minimum services required for emergencies and other safety-critical flights will remain available.

But Charleroi Airport, a major European hub for low-cost airline Ryanair, said the controllers’ strike will result “in the complete shutdown of all the country’s airports for an entire day,” affecting thousands of passengers.

“Without air traffic control, no flights can take off or land,” the airport said, condemning what it described as a “last-minute decision” with “disastrous consequences.”

Brussels airport — the country’s largest — said that the majority of departing and arriving flights “will have to be canceled.”

De Wever, a Flemish conservative, has been locked in protracted talks with his governing partners to try to find a deal on a new cost-cutting budget by Monday.

Earlier this month he offered his resignation after his coalition failed to reach a deal.

But Belgium’s King Philippe refused to accept it and gave him more time to find a solution.

World.title: Democrats who swept into the Senate promised change. A leadership vote is testing them early
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The Democratic Party’s incoming senators haven’t even been sworn into office yet, but the decision over who will lead their new majority is already testing the promise of change they made as candidates.

The 13 new Democrats are part of the largest incoming Senate class in decades, with several winning in Republican strongholds by promising to shake up Washington and be independent voices. Now they are caught up in a classic insider fight, forced to decide whether to stick with longtime Senate leader Chuck Schumer of New York or back challenger Chris Van Hollen of Maryland.

Newly elected progressives, including Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, have backed Van Hollen, who is taking on Schumer with promises of a more aggressive legislative approach. Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio, who is returning to Washington after losing his seat in 2024, supports Schumer.

But the incoming senators from traditionally Republican states such as Texas, Mississippi, Iowa and South Carolina, whose victories helped deliver Democrats the majority, have so far largely avoided taking sides publicly. Annie Andrews of South Carolina has said she is talking with both candidates. Scott Colom of Mississippi says he wants to get to know them better before deciding and describes himself as being in “listening mode.”

Kansas Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton said Thursday he would not back Schumer, but declined to endorse anyone.

“I’m looking for someone who is going to bring people together,” Hamilton told MSNow. “Right now, in places like Kansas, there’s a lot of people who don’t feel that in Chuck Schumer.”

Schumer’s long-standing relationships and knowledge of Senate machinery are a big advantage heading into the Dec. 1 vote, which will be held by secret ballot. He also oversees Senate Democrats’ campaign spending group, funneling millions into many of the races and, in some cases, recruiting the candidates to run in the first place.

But the reluctance of many incoming senators to commit has put an unusual spotlight on first-term lawmakers who could help shape the party’s direction in the new Congress.

“We should be very embracing of the new people who have been through fire to get here,” said Hawaii Sen. Mazie Hirono, who is supporting Schumer. “We have to make sure that all these voices are heard, and they’ve got a lot of talent to bring to the table.”

The senators who campaigned for change

Many of the incoming senators campaigned as political outsiders, promising to bring fresh perspectives to a Washington establishment they argued had failed ordinary Americans.

Andrews, a 46-year-old pediatrician, became the first Democrat in nearly three decades to win a Senate race in South Carolina. She called for “generational change” and said that she would not support Schumer.

But she has also rejected policies that Van Hollen supports, such as “Medicare for All.” On a press call Tuesday, Andrews said she has made “no decision” on the majority leader’s race.

“The way I assess the situation as it is right now is that the generational change is represented by this incredibly dynamic incoming freshman class of senators,” Andrews said.

Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico called for “new blood” in the Democratic Party, arguing that fresh perspectives were needed to change a political system that had failed. But Talarico has stopped short of rejecting Schumer, saying in a CBS interview two days after the Nov. 3 election that he would meet with the leadership candidates and ask “tough questions.”

Iowa Sen.-elect Josh Turek has taken a similar approach, saying his decision will depend on which candidate best reflects the priorities he campaigned on. During a news conference Monday, he said that he had met with Schumer and Van Hollen and was waiting for “further updates” on questions he had.

“Whoever provides those answers to me that most closely align with my common sense, prairie populist agenda that I’ve been running on for the last year and a half, that’s who I’ll support,” Turek said.

Alaska Sen.-elect Mary Peltola, whose race was officially called on Wednesday, told The Associated Press soon after that she had not yet thought about the leadership race.

El-Sayed and Flanagan have been among the staunch supporters of Van Hollen. Another progressive, Maine Sen.-elect Troy Jackson, has said he wouldn’t support Schumer but hasn’t yet said he would vote for Van Hollen.

Schumer backed alternative candidates during the primaries in all three races. He supported all three once they were nominated.

A private decision has become a public fight

Senate leadership elections have traditionally been private affairs, decided by lawmakers in closed-door, secret-ballot votes that are shaped by the complicated inner workings of the Senate. The job requires holding together a caucus with competing political interests, a responsibility that doesn’t always align with the demands of the party’s most vocal activists.

Schumer’s allies point to his success in doing that job, most recently in the midterms. He helped recruit candidates such as Brown, Peltola and North Carolina Sen.-elect Roy Cooper, while his allied super PAC was the largest Democratic spender in tightly contested races such as in Michigan and Maine.

“When the manager takes you to the World Series, you give him another contract,” Arizona Sen. Ruben Gallego said.

But Democrats are also facing pressure from some in their base to confront Republican President Donald Trump more aggressively while delivering on ambitious policy promises. Large progressive organizations, including MoveOn and Indivisible, have endorsed Van Hollen, while many senators’ offices have been flooded with calls urging them to reject Schumer.

“Our members are tired of politicians content with incrementalism — they want bold, creative leadership that will help Democrats usher in affordability and accountability without delay or compromise in the next Congress,” MoveOn’s executive director, Joel Payne, said in a statement.

At a Schumer news conference Wednesday, several activists shouted from a distance, “Step down, Schumer! Step down, Schumer!”

The fifth-term senator has not said whether his term ending in 2028 will be his last.

Van Hollen, a supporter of progressive priorities including Medicare for All and restrictions on offensive weapons transfers to Israel, has promised a more confrontational approach to Trump, an ambitious economic agenda and changes to how the party operates in primaries.

The calls for change extend beyond the first-term lawmakers

The leadership fight has also drawn in more established Democrats, including senators whose political ambitions may include higher office.

Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff, fresh off a reelection victory in a presidential battleground state, is among the Democrats whose names have surfaced as potential White House contenders in 2028. Ossoff has served under Schumer’s leadership for nearly six years.

“I haven’t committed to any candidate, and I’ll hear everybody out,” Ossoff said this week.

Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin, elected in 2024 and now contemplating a presidential bid, said Thursday she was supporting Van Hollen. A moderate who has called for change in Senate leadership, Slotkin has also been critical of some of Van Hollen’s more progressive policies, underscoring how the leadership fight cuts across the party’s ideological divisions.

“Because I’ve been clear that I wasn’t supporting Schumer, I will be supporting Chris Van Hollen,” Slotkin said.

World.title: Libya loses $30.8 million as armed group blocks oil pipeline for over 20 days
World.content:
TRIPOLI: Libya has lost more than $30.8 million in oil revenue after an armed group forcibly shut the Hamada oil pipeline for more than 20 days, disrupting the transportation of more than 302,000 barrels of crude, the National Oil Corporation said Saturday.

The NOC said the shutdown had reduced crude output by an average of 14,418 barrels per day, resulting in daily revenue losses of approximately $1.47 million. Total losses reached 302,778 barrels, valued at $30.79 million based on average crude prices.

The losses also include fixed operating costs at affected Arabian Gulf Oil Company fields, including Hamada, NC5, NC8 and Tahara (NC4), the corporation said.

The NOC condemned attacks on oil infrastructure, warning that they were causing material and reputational damage to Libya’s energy sector, undermining efforts to restore international energy companies’ confidence and increase production capacity.

It said the disruptions were also damaging the country’s economy, hindering development efforts and threatening the operation of state institutions.

The corporation called on relevant authorities to intensify efforts to reopen the pipeline valve and prevent further attacks on oil facilities, stressing the need to safeguard national resources and ensure uninterrupted production.

The Hamada pipeline is a key link in Libya’s oil transportation network, connecting the Hamada oilfields to the Zawiya refinery, the country’s largest, which has a processing capacity of 120,000 barrels per day.

The pipeline shutdown comes amid recurring disruptions to Libya’s oil infrastructure. On Oct. 31, an armed group shut a valve on the main Hamada crude pipeline, halting flows to Zawiya and marking the second interruption of oil supplies to the refinery that month.

At the time, the NOC warned that the closure could result in the loss of about 15,000 barrels of crude daily and urged the Petroleum Facilities Guard, responsible for securing oil installations, to help reopen the valve.

The Zawiya refinery is connected to the Sharara oilfield, which has a production capacity of about 300,000 barrels per day. On Sept. 26, the NOC also announced the forced shutdown of a refining unit at Zawiya following the closure of a valve on the Sharara crude pipeline.

Libya’s oil production has repeatedly been disrupted by political disputes, security incidents and technical problems since the 2011 uprising that toppled longtime ruler Muammar Qaddafi.

Oil is the country’s main economic resource, accounting for approximately 90 percent of its economy. Libya holds Africa’s largest proven crude oil reserves, making the sector critical to government revenues and efforts to rebuild the country’s economy.

World.title: ‘We lost everything’: Brazil town clears rubble after deadly storm
World.content:
TUPANCIRETÃ, Brazil: Residents of a town in southern Brazil picked through the wreckage of their homes Saturday after a violent storm killed four people, injured 162 and tore roofs from thousands of buildings.

In Tupancireta, an agricultural town in Rio Grande do Sul state, residents salvaged furniture, mattresses and bicycles from the rubble, while others clambered onto rooftops to carry out makeshift repairs.

“I got up to go to the bathroom, and when I came back, I couldn’t get into the room. The door was jammed and the house had already been torn apart,” Ivair Prieto, a 64-year-old bricklayer, told AFP.

“We lost everything, we lost everything. But nobody was hurt, and life goes on,” he said, pointing to the ruins of his home in the town, nearly 400 kilometers (250 miles) inland from Porto Alegre on the coast.

The number of people injured in Friday’s storm nearly tripled to 162 from an earlier tally of 60, civil defense authorities said Saturday. One person who was hospitalized died, bringing the death toll to four.

Almost all of the town’s roughly 20,000 residents were forced to leave their homes, although only around 30 sought refuge in public shelters.

Winds tore roofs off buildings and damaged some 8,000 homes, as well as schools and the local hospital, while bringing down thousands of electricity poles.

Aerial images captured by AFP showed roofless houses and sheds stretching for kilometers, with fallen trees and debris littering the streets.

“The town is gone,” Mayor Gustavo Herter said Friday, describing how the storm tore through Tupancireta in just 40 minutes before dawn, leaving residents without electricity or running water.

Winds reached 114 kilometers (71 miles) per hour, according to Brazil’s national meteorological institute, Inmet.

Civil defense authorities classified the storm as a “supercell,” a powerful thunderstorm characterized by strong rising air currents that can produce tornadoes.

They did not rule out the possibility that a tornado had formed.

Severe weather has battered the region since November 16, bringing strong winds, hail and heavy rain to around 30 municipalities in Rio Grande do Sul.

Tupancireta suffered much of the damage and was the only municipality to report casualties.

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ordered medical teams to the area, while state Governor Eduardo Leite allocated seven million reais (about $1.2 million) for reconstruction.

Southern Brazil is frequently struck by tornadoes. In 2025, the country had a record 92 tornadoes and similar weather events, according to Prevots, a volunteer meteorological network associated with universities and research institutes.

World.title: French protesters rally for sixth weekend over living costs, public services
World.content:
PARIS, France: Tens of thousands of people marched in cities in France on Saturday, on the sixth weekend in a row of protests to demand better public services and express anger over the rising cost of living and inequality.

The protest movement, sparked in mid-September by high school students demanding better learning conditions, fueled a nationwide campaign against soaring prices, inadequate public services and police brutality that spread across Europe, even as turnout in France has dwindled.

Across the country, organizers reported 150,000 protesters, compared to 200,000 last week and 800,000 on the first one held October 17.

The interior ministry said numbers had “significantly declined,” counting 82,500 people, compared to 106,000 last Saturday.

Thousands of people gathered in central Paris’s Place de la Republique square in a festive atmosphere, with musicians playing, food trucks, costumes and homemade signs, before marching east through the city.

Flags and vests of trade unions and left-wing parties mingled with those of student organizations and the Yellow Vest movement, which is marking its anniversary eight years after it rattled President Emmanuel Macron’s government.

One group had set up mock headstones proclaiming the death of France’s public services, including social security and education.

“In a number of countries, young people are going through the same thing, namely precarity. You have to choose between having a roof over your head, getting medical care, and being able to eat your fill,” said Manon Moret, general secretary of the students’ union Unef.

On Friday crowds rallied across multiple countries to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people.

“I want to live, not survive,” read one placard held by a protester in Paris.

Police law

Another read: “No to the license to kill,” in reference to a law adopted by France’s parliament on Friday increasing protection for law enforcement officers using their weapons, heavily criticized by the left.

The protests have been largely peaceful but have seen fringe violence and accusations of police brutality.

At least 31 people have been seriously injured by security forces since the protests began, according to a count by AFP based on direct testimonies, victims’ lawyers and NGO records. Authorities have not provided an official toll.

Last month, huge rallies across France degenerated into the worst rioting seen in the country in years, with hundreds of shops looted and buildings attacked and torched.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez had warned regional authorities to be “particularly vigilant regarding the groups most hostile to law enforcement” after the police law was adopted.

Vehicles burned

Protesters marched on Saturday in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and Lyon in the southeast.

Clashes broke out on the sidelines of some protests as people tried to rally in banned areas, set fire to vehicles and bins, with police firing tear gas.

At 6:00 p.m. (1700 GMT) the interior ministry said there had been 144 arrests.

Unions and activists have called for more protests in the coming weeks.

Avril Bas, who attended the Paris protest with her knitting group to support high school students’ demands for better learning conditions, was not discouraged by the lower turnout on Saturday.

“If we take care of our young people, our students, we’ll have a wonderful tomorrow and that’s why I’m here,” the 27-year-old told AFP.

“We’ll be there next week and the next week and as long as we’re needed,” she said.

World.title: Iraq qualifies for 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup in Uzbekistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has officially confirmed the final 16-team lineup for the 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup, including Iraq, which topped Group B during the qualifiers in Thailand with 10 points—putting the young Lions of Mesopotamia just three group-stage matches away from securing a berth at the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Under head coach Salam Shaker, Iraq clinched first place in Group B after defeating tournament hosts Thailand 2–1 in their decisive final qualifier in Buriram on Friday, November 20, ending a nine-year continental qualification drought for the national under-17 side.

The finals are scheduled to take place in the Uzbek capital of Tashkent from May 13 to 29, 2027, following the official tournament draw on February 18, 2027.

Per AFC competition regulations, the top eight finishers at the tournament in Uzbekistan—specifically the eight teams that advance out of the group stage into the quarterfinals—will automatically qualify for the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Reaching the World Cup also carries a secondary continental incentive: under AFC rules, all Asian nations that qualify for the global finals earn direct entry into the 2028 AFC U-17 Asian Cup without having to contest the preliminary qualifying rounds.

The 16 participating nations in Tashkent comprise the seven qualifying group winners alongside the nine AFC representatives from the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup who received automatic entry:

Qualification Route Qualified Nations Qualifying Group Winners Iraq (Group B), Indonesia (Group A), Syria (Group C), Iran (Group D), India (Group E), Yemen (Group F), Lebanon (Group G) Automatic Qualifiers Uzbekistan (Hosts), Australia, China PR, Japan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Tajikistan, Vietnam

Coach Salam Shaker and his squad now shift their focus toward preparing for February’s draw, aiming to replicate the historic success of Iraq’s 2016 U-16 championship generation and re-establish Iraqi youth football on both the Asian and global stages.

World.title: Japanese cyclist killed in highway collision in southern Iraq’s Muthanna Governorate
World.content:
Samawah (IraqiNews.com) – A Japanese bicycle traveler died on Friday, November 20, 2026, following a traffic collision along the Rumaitha–Samawah highway in southern Iraq’s Muthanna Governorate.

According to a security source, the tourist was riding a bicycle along the highway when he collided with a Dodge Charger sedan.

The impact proved fatal for the cyclist and also injured a passenger riding inside the vehicle, identified as a security officer.

Traffic police and forensic investigators conducted an on-site inspection of the crash scene following the incident. Based on their preliminary field assessment, authorities determined that the Japanese cyclist was at fault for the collision.

World.title: Iraqi Energy Police establish 12 checkpoints along Jurf Al Sakhar oil pipelines
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior’s Directorate General of Energy Police continued field operations on Saturday, November 21, 2026, to secure vital oil pipeline corridors across the Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) subdistrict in northern Babylon Governorate.

Marking the second consecutive day since Baghdad formally inaugurated its new joint command center in the area, Energy Police units established full operational control along a pipeline stretch exceeding five kilometers.

In an official statement, Ministry of Interior Head of Relations and Media Major General Miqdad Miri confirmed that the deployment is being directed on the ground by Energy Police Director-General Lieutenant General Hamid Abdullah Ibrahim.

Executing the mission with a regiment from the Commando Brigade (Liwa al-Maghawir), engineering teams deployed specialized heavy machinery to carve a dedicated patrol road parallel to the pipeline bundles through rugged terrain, enabling rapid troop mobility and sustained field surveillance.

To lock down the corridor against illicit tampering, Energy Police established 12 new security checkpoints spaced roughly every 500 meters along the route, alongside a permanent regimental headquarters.

Major General Miri emphasized that these preventive measures are designed to elevate field command, safeguard crude transport infrastructure, and protect national wealth.

The deployment represents the first concrete operational phase following the expiration of Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s Friday ultimatum to Kata’ib Hezbollah.

On Friday, November 20, federal authorities inaugurated the joint control headquarters (Al-Musaytir)—commanded under the Federal Police and uniting Army, Federal Police, Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), and Energy Police formations—initiating a permanent security reorganization in Jurf al-Sakhar that includes securing pipeline networks and reopening closed transit arteries to civilian traffic.

World.title: US dollar steadies near 170,000 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged slightly lower across major domestic parallel markets on Saturday morning, November 21, 2026, hovering right at the 170,000-dinar threshold for retail sales while buying bids settled below that mark across key commercial hubs.

According to morning monitoring figures, physical banknote rates opened across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra as follows:

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 170,000 IQD against buying offers of 169,500 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks quoted retail selling rates slightly higher at 170,050 IQD alongside purchasing bids holding at 170,000 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices matched Baghdad’s selling quote at 170,000 IQD, with buying offers dipping to 169,250 IQD per $100.

Despite the downward drift at the start of the trading week, parallel cash rates maintain a spread of roughly 18,000 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.title: ICMR: Common antibiotics losing potency as drug resistance rises
World.content:
The findings come at a time when govt is drawing attention to the misuse of antibiotics

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Antibiotics used to treat common bacterial infections are increasingly losing their effectiveness, with a new Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) report finding only 18.4% of E. coli samples tested in hospitals were susceptible to cefotaxime, an antibiotic used to treat serious infections such as pneumonia and UTIs.The findings come at a time when govt is drawing attention to the misuse of antibiotics. At the launch of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week (Nov 18), the health ministry highlighted concerns over antibiotic sales without prescriptions and inappropriate prescribing.ICMRâs Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance and Research Network annual report for 2025 also found high resistance to stronger antibiotics used to treat severe infections. Only around one-third of Klebsiella pneumoniae samples were susceptible to carbapenems, powerful antibiotics often reserved for serious infections that do not respond to other medicines.Another finding was 91.1% of revived Acinetobacter baumannii isolates tested were resistant to carbapenems.This can cause serious hospital-acquired infections, particularly pneumonia and bloodstream infections among critically ill patients.Dr Kamini Walia, head of ICMRâs descriptive research division, said the findings showed antimicrobial resistance was not confined to large referral centres. Citing the secondary-care hospital data, she said ceftriaxone susceptibility in E. coli declined from 39.8% in category I hospitals to 28% in category II and just 11.5% in category III.

World.title: Ganges treaty: Bangladesh & India meeting today
World.content:
DHAKA: India and Bangladesh will meet under the Joint Rivers Commission (JRC) in Dhaka on Sunday, ahead of the expiry of the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty, signed on Dec 12, 1996. The meeting is likely to be the last under the current treaty, officials said.

Dhaka has described it as routine, saying treaty renewal or extension is beyond the committee's jurisdiction. The two countries share 54 transboundary rivers, but the Ganges is the only one covered by a bilateral water-sharing agreement.

World.title: Amit Shah & Sergio Gor laud joint India-US effort in transnational narcotics network bust
World.content:
NEW DELHI:Union home minister

and US ambassador to India Sergio Gor Saturday lauded the breakthrough success of âOperation Monsoon Thunder,â underscoring the deepening Indo-US synergy in dismantling transnational narcotics networks.

Taking to X, Shah said the arrests and seizures made across India and US stood as a testament to the strength of bilateral partnership in tackling drug menace. Reaffirming govtâs ze- ro-tolerance stance under PM Narendra Modi, Shah emphasised the commitment to ensuring neither a single gram of narcotics enters India nor leaves its borders for other nations. Gor also commended the joint effort, describing it on X as a âgreat exampleâ of US-India partnership in action.

World.title: India's cyber security agency Cert-IN flags payment fraud in govt-linked platforms
World.content:
CERT-In flagged that cyber-attacks have extended beyond banks and financial institutions

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's cyber security agency has said payment fraud extends beyond banks and financial firms to companies that process govt-linked payments and platforms paying vendors and business partners. In a critical advisory issued Friday, CERT-In separately said it had detected AI-driven cyberattacks targeting businesses, govt bodies and research institutions.The latest warning follows an Oct advisory on unauthorised transfers involving payment and disbursement systems in financial sector. In the newer cases, CERT-In said, attackers targeted "business records and approval processes" that determined who got paid.It urged govt bodies that outsource payments to independently verify changes to beneficiary details, payment instructions and who can approve transfers. It also advised service providers to keep client systems separate and restrict administrative access.

World.title: India crosses 1 crore HPV vax in 9 months
World.content:
India has administered more than one crore doses of the HPV vaccine in less than nine months of launching its national campaign, covering nearly 87% of the annual target of 1.2 crore 14-year-old girls, according to the Union health ministry.

Launched in Feb 2026, the campaign provides free, voluntary single-dose HPV vaccination to 14-year-old girls at designated govt health facilities, with parental consent. Six states - Gujarat, UP, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, MP and Bihar - have achieved 100% coverage of their identified target populations, the ministry said. In terms of the number of girls vaccinated, UP led with more than 29.3 lakh, followed by Bihar with 13.7 lakh.

World.title: Over 10k postgraduate medical seats in blocked category; govt may review float system
World.content:
NEW DELHI: More than 10,000 postgraduate medical seats were listed under the blocked category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling, with the data indicating that some candidates were holding one seat through All India counselling and another through state counselling simultaneously, prompting the govt to consider changes to the newly introduced float system.

According to the SARTHA app, a medical admission and counselling platform for NEET-PG and NEET-UG aspirants, 10,105 seats were listed under the 'Blocking' category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling. The app, filtered for MCC (All India) counselling, describes these as seats held by students who also have an allotment in another counselling process. The data was shared by Dr Kapil Dev on social media.

The branch-wise breakup showed MD General Medicine accounting for the highest number of blocked seats at 1,026, followed by MS Obstetrics and Gynaecology (861) and MS General Surgery (786), according to the app.



Dr Nachiket Bhatia, a medico-socio activist, has also flagged the issue on his social media account.

A senior official familiar with the counselling process said the float facility, which allows candidates to retain an allotted seat while seeking an upgrade, could be contributing to dual seat blocking as all-India and state counselling run parallelly on separate platforms. "A candidate may opt for float in both processes and end up blocking two seats," the official said.





Introduced for students' convenience, the facility allows candidates to retain seats while seeking an upgrade, with physical joining becoming compulsory in the third round. The official said govt may consider restricting float to the first round and making physical joining compulsory from the second round in future counselling cycles. "This is the first time we have introduced the float system in this manner.
