We will analyse the situation after the third round."

The official also flagged the absence of a common counselling platform linking all-India and state processes, which run simultaneously on separate portals, making it difficult to track candidates holding seats in both. A common portal could prevent multiple allotments, but differences in state reservation policies and concerns over loss of control have hindered integration.

Meanwhile, Federation of All India Medical Association has sought a 24-hour deferment of NEET-PG Round 2 results and a one-day window for eligible candidates to surrender either their All India or state quota seats.

World.title: Reflecting on Purana Qila's history, Pakistan minister invokes Humanyun & Sher Shah Suri at SCO civilisational dialogue to assert cultural diversity
World.content:
The remarks come amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. Malik is visiting India for the first time.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Venue of the first civilisational dialogue under the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Forum, Purana Qila symbolised civilisational continuity but in the case of Pakistan with a different perspective. In marked contrast to India, which Itâs minister Musadik Masood Malik on Saturday chose to emphasise that the foundations of the Old Fort were laid by Humanyun whose origins lay in central Asia and that its construction was carried forward by Sher Shah Suri who came from Afghanistan as he sought to focus on the sub continentâs cultural diversity.âIts foundation was laid by Humayun, who belonged to the Timurid dynasty and had arrived from Central Asia. Its construction was further carried forward by Sher Shah Suri, who came from Afghanistan. Thus, within a single wall, one could find the art of two different rulers, two cultural layers, and traces of two traditions,â Malik said.India has touted Old Fort as the perfect venue for the meet with its multi-layered history and its identity as the ancient city of Indraprastha mentioned in the epic âMahabharataâ. As part of the retelling of the approximately 3000-year long history of the site, India showcased nine layers of continuity--among them the standing ramparts built by Sher Shah Suri (1538-1545 CE) after demolishing and re-modeling Dinpanah, a city founded here by Humayun, around 1533 CE.Reflecting on the excavations at the site, Malik said, âDelhi has not been diminished by civilisations and people coming from outside; rather, it has grown strongerâ.During his inaugural speech on Friday Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also reflected on the history of Purana Qila to assert Indiaâs civilisational journey going back thousands of years to the Mahabharata period. He also visited the âMahabharata Pavillion - Anant: A rare 18th century Mahabharata scrollâ and the exhibition âAstitvaâ offering an immersive account of Delhiâs history through archaeological evidence, that have been curated for the leaders from SCO countries to see.Day two of the Fourm saw ministers of all participating nations make statements. Malik who happens to be the Climate Change and Environmental Coordination referring to archaeological remains from different periods discovered during excavations at Purana Qila, said that the fort in which the delegates were seated was, in itself, a story. He appreciated the description of the event as âTehzeeb Ki Guftaguâ, or âDialogue of Civilisationsâ.

World.title: Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren writes to CJI seeking urgent appointment of HC chief justice successor
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

wrote a letter to

Surya Kant and the Supreme Court Collegium, urging them to expedite the appointment of a successor to Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M S Sonak, who is due to retire on November 27.

In his letter to the CJI and Collegium members, Soren warned that the absence of a permanent successor could lead to another interim arrangement, affecting administrative continuity and institutional planning in the high court, as cited by PTI.

âWithout the Collegium's immediate action, the High Court of Jharkhand faces the prospect of yet another interim Acting Chief Justice arrangementâ¦ I hope it (the Collegium) will not disagree with me that the office of the Chief Justice is central to the administrative and judicial functioning of a high court,â he wrote.

Soren also stressed the need for stable judicial leadership to maintain public confidence in the justice delivery system, saying frequent leadership transitions could disrupt the functioning of the institution.

World.title: Morning digest: Indian team reaches Dhaka ahead of Ganga Water Treaty’s expiry; U.S. court dispatches summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun case; and more
World.content:
Indian team reaches Dhaka ahead of Ganga Water Treaty’s expiry

Ahead of the December 12 expiry of the India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty, a team of Indian officials has reached Dhaka for a meeting of the Joint Committee under the Joint River Commission (JRC), which looks after bilateral river-related issues.

U.S. court dispatches summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun case

A U.S. court has dispatched summonses to National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) Director Samant Goel to be served through Indian courts in connection with a case involving an alleged murder plot against Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.

Bihar’s development list is so long that it cannot be counted in one visit to the State: PM

Along with the completion of one year of the National Development Alliance (NDA) regime in Bihar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) formally inaugurated the cable-based 9.76 km long six-lane bridge on the Ganga river, constructed at a cost of over ₹5,500 crore, connecting Kacchi Dargah of Patna district to Bidupur in neighbouring Vaishali district. Mr. Modi also laid the foundation stones for several other development projects in the State at an estimated cost of ₹34,470 crore.

World needs skilled youth, not merely degree-holders, says PM Modi

The world needs skilled youth, not merely degree-holders, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said at the fifth Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh, a national-level convocation ceremony for graduating Industrial Training Institutes (ITI) trainees, in Lucknow on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

Why dismiss ‘reel-makers’ when police rely on reels: women media professionals ask in Supreme Court

Network of Women in Media, India, a women journalists’ group, responded to the Delhi Police in the Supreme Court on Saturday (November 21, 2026) that the freedom to gather and report news is not dependent upon State accreditation, formal employment with a recognised media organisation, or possession of an employer-issued identity card.

Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti

Kashmir’s prized saffron fields in Pampore, Pulwama, have been used as a municipal dumping ground for the past three years, former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

14-year-old hacker held for trying to sell private data of 4,000 Agniveers on dark web: Delhi Police

A 14-year-old boy from Haryana’s Ballabhgarh was apprehended by the Delhi Police Special Cell for allegedly hacking into a website and attempting to sell sensitive data linked to around 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web for $500, officials said.

COP31 extends into overtime in Turkiye meeting

Much like the 1.5 degree Celsius warming ceiling, COP31 proceedings under way at Antalya in Turkiye also breached upper limits with countries, as of Saturday (November 21, 2026) evening, yet to behold a final text or convene a final plenary meeting to decide on the path forward for climate action.

Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi as U.S. rejects terms

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still hoped diplomacy could end its war with the United States, while U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but one that was not acceptable to him.

Sri Lanka’s organised crime bill gets Supreme Court nod

Sri Lanka’s proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill has received the Supreme Court’s nod, which ruled that its provisions are “not inconsistent” with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickremaratna told Parliament on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

ISL: Chennaiyin FC, Punjab FC share honours

Chennaiyin FC, making another attempt to notch up consecutive league victories under the 44-year-old tactician, shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw with Punjab FC at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Chennai on Saturday (November 21, 2026). Punjab captain Nikhil Prabhu’s own goal in the 13th minute was cancelled out by Raphael Messi Bouli’s alert work in the 41st.

Nadal’s appointment to Real Madrid board ratified at general assembly

Retired tennis superstar Rafael Nadal joined Real Madrid’s board of directors on Saturday (November 21, 2026), after his appointment was ratified at the club’s general assembly. Nadal, a 22-time Grand Slam winner, has been an honorary club member since 2011, and shares a strong relationship with club President Florentino Perez.

World.title: Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti
World.content:
Kashmir’s prized saffron fields in Pampore, Pulwama, have been used as a municipal dumping ground for the past three years, former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

“For the past three years, Pampore’s priceless saffron fields have been used as a municipal dumping ground. Nearly 2,000 kanals were damaged, 150 families’ livelihoods threatened, and rats and rodents destroying crops. This is an outrageous assault on Kashmir’s saffron heritage. Such administrative negligence is indefensible. Our saffron fields are not dumping sites. They must be protected not poisoned,” Ms. Mufti said.

NGT directs action

Her statement came days after the National Green Tribunal (NGT) highlighted the “unscientific dumping of municipal solid waste in Patalbagh” in Pampore. The NGT bench, comprising chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Dr. Afroz Alam, directed the constitution of a joint committee “to conduct an on-site inspection and submit a comprehensive factual and action-taken report within eight weeks”.

It asked the Deputy Commissioner, Pulwama, to coordinate the inspection and facilitate the committee’s visit to the dumping site. Representatives of the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), the Regional Director of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, and a nominee of the Member Secretary, Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee, will be members of the committee.
